1	# Theming: fonts and colours from a theme
2	
3	This is the contract for every agent migrating call sites under
4	`docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md`, and for anyone writing a new view in the
5	SDK or the Ripul app. It says what a view writes, what the tokens are called,
6	what Ripul's theme document looks like, and how to check your work. If you
7	need a token, role or rule that is not here, ask the foundation owner (a
8	comment on the plan's Foundation section): do not invent one.
9	
10	Nothing in this file is pending. Where a thing is not built, it says so.
11	
12	The code is in `Sources/RipulAgent/ThemeCore/` (four files, compiling on iOS
13	and macOS). The tests are `Tests/RipulAgentTests/RipulThemeCoreTests.swift`.
14	
15	## The one idea
16	
17	Every token has a default, written in code, that is the system value the call
18	site used before: `Font.ripul(.body)` is `Font.body`, `.ripul(.textSecondary)`
19	is the system's `.secondary` style, `UIColor.ripul(.text)` is `UIColor.label`,
20	the same object. So a migrated call site draws the same pixels, and the
21	default theme document is empty. A theme document changes a token only by
22	naming it.
23	
24	## What a view writes
25	
26	### Fonts (SwiftUI)
27	
28	| Today | Write |
29	|---|---|
30	| `.font(.body)` | `.font(.ripul(.body))` |
31	| `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold))` | `.font(.ripul(.caption, weight: .semibold))` |
32	| `.font(.headline.bold())` | `.font(.ripul(.headline).bold())` |
33	| `.font(.caption.monospacedDigit())` | `.font(.ripul(.caption).monospacedDigit())` |
34	| `.font(.caption.monospaced())` | `.font(.ripul(.caption, family: .code))` |
35	| `.font(.system(.caption, design: .monospaced))` | `.font(.ripul(.caption, family: .code))` |
36	| `.font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))` on text | `.font(.ripul(size: 14, weight: .medium))` |
37	| `.font(.system(size: 12, design: .monospaced))` | `.font(.ripul(size: 12, family: .code))` |
38	| `.font(.system(size: 18))` on an `Image` | `.font(.ripulIcon(size: 18))` |
39	| `.font(.title2)` on an `Image` | `.font(.ripulIcon(.title2))` |
40	| `Font.caption` as a value | `Font.ripul(.caption)` |
41	
42	Rules:
43	
44	- `.bold()`, `.italic()`, `.monospacedDigit()`, `.leading(...)` stay chained
45	  calls. `.bold()` is not `weight: .bold`: the two draw different pixels
46	  (measured).
47	- `.monospaced()` and `design: .monospaced` draw the same pixels (measured),
48	  so both become `family: .code`.
49	- A fixed size stays fixed. In a custom family it is
50	  `Font.custom(_:fixedSize:)`, because `.system(size:)` does not scale with
51	  Dynamic Type and its replacement must not either.
52	- A bare text style is a font wherever its type is `Font`, not only inside
53	  `.font(`: a property (`var titleFont: Font { flag ? .caption2 : .caption }`),
54	  a `return .headline`, a ternary inside `.font(...)`. Each becomes
55	  `.ripul(<the same style>)`. These are easy to miss: the script does not
56	  rewrite them, and a row that takes its fonts from such properties stays in
57	  the system font under a themed family (found on the session row with the
58	  loud document).
59	- A weight may be the argument or a chained call: `.ripul(.body, weight: w)`
60	  and `.ripul(.body).weight(w)` are the same value under every theme, whatever
61	  `w` is, a ternary included. Prefer the argument.
62	- A design chosen at run time,
63	  `.font(.system(.caption, design: isTag ? .monospaced : .default))`, becomes
64	  `.font(.ripul(.caption, family: isTag ? .code : nil))`: a nil family is the
65	  role's own. The ternary may also go outside,
66	  `.font(isTag ? .ripul(.caption, family: .code) : .ripul(.caption))`; the lint
67	  reads both. (`.system(.caption, design: .default)` and `.caption` are taken
68	  to draw the same; that one is reasoned, not measured.)
69	- `ripulIcon` is never themed. A font on an `Image(systemName:)` is an icon
70	  size, not type.
71	- `.rounded` and `.serif` designs have no accessor. The two `.rounded` sites
72	  are exempt by name (`// theme-exempt: rounded design`).
73	- View-level `.fontWeight()`, `.bold()` and `.italic()` are left alone.
74	- `View.ripulTextStyle(.eyebrow)` applies a role's font and, when a theme sets
75	  them, its tracking and capitals. With no theme it is `.font(.ripul(role))`.
76	  A call site that writes `.textCase(.uppercase)` today keeps it.
77	
78	### Colours (SwiftUI)
79	
80	There are two forms, and which one you write matters.
81	
82	**The style form**, wherever a `ShapeStyle` is accepted (`foregroundStyle`,
83	`fill`, `stroke`, `background`, `tint`, `strokeBorder`):
84	
85	```swift
86	.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))     // was .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
87	.fill(.ripul(.danger))                        // was .fill(.red)
88	.background(.ripul(.canvas))                  // was .background(Color(.systemBackground))
89	```
90	
91	**The Color form**, only where a `Color` is required (a `shadow(color:)`, a
92	stored `Color`, a function argument, `foregroundColor`, an `.opacity()` on a
93	colour):
94	
95	```swift
96	Color.ripul(.textSecondary)                   // was Color.secondary
97	.foregroundColor(.ripul(.textSecondary))      // was .foregroundColor(.secondary)
98	.shadow(color: Color.ripul(system: .black).opacity(0.2), radius: 4)
99	```
100	
101	Why two. The text roles' defaults are SwiftUI's hierarchical styles, and the
102	system draws `.secondary` differently from the colour `Color.secondary` in a
103	list row, inside a button and in a section header (measured: in a light list
104	row the style is 128,128,128 and the colour is 138,138,142; in a prominent
105	button 128,195,255 against 36,90,142). The style form hands back the system's
106	own style, so it matches `.secondary` in every place tested. The Color form
107	hands back `Color.secondary`, which matches what `Color.secondary` drew. So:
108	
109	- Replace a style with the style form and a `Color` with the Color form.
110	  Never turn `Color.secondary` into the style form, or `foregroundColor` into
111	  `foregroundStyle`: that changes pixels. The lint refuses it.
112	- A bare `.secondary` or `.primary` is whichever the compiler makes it. It is
113	  a **Color** when the other branch of its ternary is a colour
114	  (`flag ? .white : .primary`, `flag ? Color.accentColor : .secondary`: the
115	  two branches share one type, and `.white` is only a Color), when its line
116	  says so (`var tint: Color = .secondary`), when it is the fallback of a
117	  `Color?` (`tint ?? .primary` becomes `tint ?? Color.ripul(.text)`), and when it is passed to a `Color`
118	  parameter or returned from a function that returns `Color`. Write the Color
119	  form for those: `flag ? Color.ripul(.onAccent) : Color.ripul(.text)`. It is
120	  the **style** when it is the whole argument of a style call
121	  (`.foregroundStyle(.secondary)`), or both branches are hierarchy names. The
122	  lint knows the cases it can read from the line, and takes either form for a
123	  bare name passed to a parameter or returned, or beside a variable in a
124	  ternary (`selected ? color : .secondary`), where only the compiler knows:
125	  there, check the type yourself. If `color` is a `Color`, write the Color form.
126	- In a ternary, both sides must be the same form:
127	  `flag ? .ripul(.text) : .ripul(.textSecondary)`. A ternary that mixes a
128	  colour and a hierarchy style (`flag ? Color.accentColor : .secondary`) is
129	  not rewritten by the script, and by the rule above it was a `Color` on both
130	  sides: write the Color form for the hierarchy name and leave the accent.
131	
132	**The accent is not edited.** `.tint`, `Color.accentColor`, `.accentColor` and
133	`UIColor.tintColor` stay as they are: the theme's accent reaches them through
134	the window's tint (see "What the root reaches"). `Color.ripul(.accent)` exists
135	for a literal that means the accent, such as `Color.blue` on a selected mark,
136	and that replacement is a judgement, so it needs a marked reason (below).
137	A read of `.tint` or `Color.accentColor` under a local `.tint(...)` is that
138	local tint, not the app's accent: leave it.
139	
140	### UIKit
141	
142	```swift
143	label.textColor = .ripul(.textSecondary)      // was .secondaryLabel
144	view.backgroundColor = .ripul(.canvas)        // was .systemBackground
145	label.font = .ripul(.caption)                 // was .preferredFont(forTextStyle: .caption1)
146	label.font = .ripul(size: 12, weight: .semibold)            // was .systemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .semibold)
147	label.font = .ripul(size: 12, weight: .regular, family: .code)   // was .monospacedSystemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .regular)
148	layer.borderColor = UIColor.ripul(.separator).cgColor
149	```
150	
151	The type may be left out on either side, as UIKit code usually does:
152	`v.font = .preferredFont(forTextStyle: .body)` becomes `v.font = .ripul(.body)`,
153	`label.textColor = .placeholderText` becomes
154	`label.textColor = .ripul(system: .placeholderText)`. The check and the lint
155	read both spellings.
156	
157	UIKit has no hierarchical style, so there the text roles are the label
158	colours: `UIColor.ripul(.textSecondary)` is `UIColor.secondaryLabel` itself.
159	
160	### A system colour that no role fits
161	
162	```swift
163	Color.ripul(system: .secondarySystemBackground)
164	.fill(.ripul(system: .tertiarySystemFill))
165	UIColor.ripul(system: .systemGray5)
166	Color.ripul(system: .white)        // a scrim, a shadow, a mark on a photograph
167	```
168	
169	This draws exactly what the system colour draws and is never themed. The
170	check counts these apart, and the brand step decides what each becomes. Use
171	it when the closed table below gives no role. Do not pick the nearest role:
172	`secondarySystemBackground` is not `surface`.
173	
174	### Colours that are not theme
175	
176	Mark them and leave them: `// theme-exempt: <reason>` on the line or the line
177	above; `// theme-exempt-file: <reason>` in a file's first 30 lines for a
178	whole file. Exempt by the plan: SF Symbol sizes (use `ripulIcon`), colours
179	that are data (a provider's, a model's, a chat's, ANSI, syntax and diff
180	colours), brand marks, materials and glass, `#if DEBUG` harness views,
181	`CmsRender/`.
182	
183	### A replacement that is a judgement
184	
185	When you replace a literal with a token whose default is a different value
186	(`Color.blue` with `.accent`), the lint stops you. If it is right, say why on
187	the new line: `// theme-mapping: this blue is the selection mark`. Expect few.
188	
189	### A colour that meant the app's colour
190	
191	```swift
192	.foregroundStyle(.ripul(accentOr: .info))    // was .foregroundStyle(.ripul(.info)), itself .blue
193	Color.ripul(accentOr: .info)
194	UIColor.ripul(accentOr: .info)
195	```
196	
197	For a system blue that was the app's own colour and not a notice (a machine's
198	icon, a tile with no colour of its own): the theme's accent once a theme names
199	one, and until then the role it was. `.ripul(.accent)` is not an identity
200	there. Measured on the reference screens: the system's tint and its blue are
201	the same pixels in light, and differ in dark (by up to 19 in a channel) and
202	under Increased Contrast (by up to 64).
203	
204	### Controls that style their own text
205	
206	A root gives a themed family to text with no font of its own, and a themed
207	accent to tints. Four things it cannot reach, each with a modifier that is the
208	system's own style while no theme names the value (so nothing changes under
209	the default document):
210	
211	| Today | Write | Under a theme |
212	|---|---|---|
213	| `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)` | `.ripulProminentButtonStyle()` | the label is drawn in `onAccent` (the system draws it white whatever the fill) |
214	| `.buttonStyle(.glassProminent)` | `.ripulGlassProminentButtonStyle()` | the same |
215	| `Section("Title") { }` in a list or form | `Section(themed: "Title") { }` | the header keeps its size and weight, in the family |
216	| `header: { X }` of a section | `header: { RipulSectionHeader { X } }` | the same |
217	| `footer: { X }` of a section | `footer: { RipulSectionFooter { X } }` | the footer keeps its small size, in the family |
218	| `ContentUnavailableView("T", systemImage: "i", description: Text("d"))` | `ContentUnavailableView(themed: "T", systemImage: "i", description: Text("d"))` | title and description in the family |
219	| `Label("T", systemImage: "i")` as an empty state's label | `RipulEmptyStateLabel("T", systemImage: "i")` | the same |
220	| `Text("d")` in an empty state's `description:` | `Text("d").ripulEmptyStateDescription()` | the same |
221	
222	Why sections need it. A grouped list chooses a header's and a footer's font
223	only while the environment holds no font, and the root's themed family is an
224	environment font, so without these a header loses its weight and a footer
225	grows to body size (seen in Settings under the brand document). SwiftUI has
226	no public way to give a family and leave a control's own choice alone.
227	
228	Not inside a menu, a picker, a toolbar or a lazy stack: a `Section` there is
229	not a grouped list's, and a menu takes only a plain title. `ContentUnavailableView.search`
230	is the system's own wording and stays in the system font.
231	
232	The sizes are the system's on iOS 27, read from pictures: an empty state's
233	title is title3 bold and its description body; a section's header is
234	headline and its footer footnote. They are the same in every list style,
235	which is not true of the system (a plain list's header differs): a limit.
236	
237	### Text UIKit draws
238	
239	Navigation titles (large and inline, so sheet titles too), segmented
240	controls and tab bar labels are set through UIKit's appearance settings by
241	`RipulTheme.applySystemTextAppearance()`, which `adopt` and `resetToDefaults`
242	call. It does nothing until a theme names a text family, restyles the bars
243	already on screen when one does, and puts every setting back to "not set"
244	when the family returns to the system's. Not reached: alerts, menus, swipe
245	action labels, a menu picker's value, and a navigation title on Mac
246	Catalyst, which the Mac draws in the window's toolbar.
247	
248	### Never store a token
249	
250	Call the accessor where the value is used, or where a view is made. These are
251	fine, because each runs again whenever the view that owns it is rebuilt, and
252	the read is made inside that view's body:
253	
254	```swift
255	struct Chip: View { var tint: Color = Color.ripul(.info) }   // a view's property default
256	func badge(tint: Color = .ripul(.info)) -> some View          // a parameter's default
257	```
258	
259	These are not, because nothing runs them again: a `static let`, a stored
260	property of a model, a controller or a singleton, a cache. The check fails a
261	`static let` that holds one; the others it cannot see.
262	
263	## The closed table
264	
265	For each literal you will meet, the one thing to write. "S" is the system
266	form. Anything not here: the system form if it is a system colour, a comment
267	on the plan if it is a raw RGB value.
268	
269	| Literal | SwiftUI | UIKit |
270	|---|---|---|
271	| `.primary` as a style | `.ripul(.text)` | |
272	| `.secondary` as a style | `.ripul(.textSecondary)` | |
273	| `.tertiary` as a style | `.ripul(.textTertiary)` | |
274	| `.quaternary` as a style | `.ripul(.textQuaternary)` | |
275	| `Color.primary`, `.foregroundColor(.primary)` | `Color.ripul(.text)` | |
276	| `Color.secondary`, `.foregroundColor(.secondary)` | `Color.ripul(.textSecondary)` | |
277	| `.label` | S: `Color.ripul(system: .label)` | `.ripul(.text)` |
278	| `.secondaryLabel` | S: `Color.ripul(system: .secondaryLabel)` | `.ripul(.textSecondary)` |
279	| `.tertiaryLabel` | S | `.ripul(.textTertiary)` |
280	| `.quaternaryLabel` | S | `.ripul(.textQuaternary)` |
281	| `.tint`, `Color.accentColor`, `.tintColor` | unchanged | unchanged |
282	| `.systemBackground` | `.ripul(.canvas)` | `.ripul(.canvas)` |
283	| `.secondarySystemGroupedBackground` | `.ripul(.surface)` | `.ripul(.surface)` |
284	| `.systemGroupedBackground` | `.ripul(.surfaceSunken)` | `.ripul(.surfaceSunken)` |
285	| `.secondarySystemBackground`, `.tertiarySystemBackground`, `.tertiarySystemGroupedBackground` | S | S |
286	| the four fills (`.systemFill` ... `.quaternarySystemFill`) | S | S |
287	| `.separator` | `.ripul(.separator)` | `.ripul(.separator)` |
288	| `.opaqueSeparator`, `.placeholderText`, `.link` | S | S |
289	| `.red`, `Color.red`, `.systemRed` | `.ripul(.danger)` | `.ripul(.danger)` |
290	| `.orange`, `.systemOrange` | `.ripul(.warning)` | `.ripul(.warning)` |
291	| `.green`, `.systemGreen` | `.ripul(.success)` | `.ripul(.success)` |
292	| `.blue`, `.systemBlue` | `.ripul(.info)` | `.ripul(.info)` |
293	| `.gray`, `.systemGray` | `.ripul(.neutral)` | `.ripul(.neutral)` |
294	| `.systemGray2` to `.systemGray6` | S | S |
295	| `.white` on an accent or coloured fill | `.ripul(.onAccent)` | `.ripul(.onAccent)` |
296	| `.white` otherwise (scrim, highlight) | S: `.ripul(system: .white)` | S |
297	| `.black` | S: `.ripul(system: .black)` | S |
298	| `.yellow`, `.mint`, `.teal`, `.cyan`, `.indigo`, `.purple`, `.pink`, `.brown` | S (`.systemPink` ...), or exempt if it is data | S |
299	| `Color.clear` | unchanged, not counted | unchanged |
300	| `.fill`, `.fill.secondary`, `.fill.tertiary`, `.fill.quaternary`, `.background`, `.separator`, `.placeholder`, `.selection` as styles | unchanged, not counted: the system's own styles, like a material | |
301	
302	The roles are named for a job, so check the job too. A red that is a
303	recording light, not an error, is still `.ripul(.danger)` only if it should
304	change when the theme's danger colour changes; if not, it is the system form.

341	## Ripul's theme document
342	
343	**Path:** `theme/ripul-theme.json` at the repository root. One file for native
344	and web. The native app bundles it; the web build reads the same file.
345	`theme/ripul-theme-loud.json` is a test document (see "The loud document"), and
346	`theme/ripul-theme-brand.json` a trial of the brand (see "The brand document").
347	
348	**Shape.** Every key is optional. An absent key means "today's look": the
349	default written in code on that platform. The default document sets nothing.
350	
351	```json
352	{
353	  "schema": 1,
354	  "name": "Ripul",
355	  "palette": {
356	    "teal": { "light": "#1f6f70", "dark": "#62b9b4" },
357	    "ink": "#1b2a41"
358	  },
359	  "roles": {
360	    "ripul.accent": "teal",
361	    "ripul.text": "system:label"
362	  },
363	  "typography": {
364	    "families": { "text": "system", "display": "system", "code": "system-monospaced" },
365	    "roles": {
366	      "eyebrow": { "family": "text", "size": 15, "weight": "semibold",
367	                   "relativeTo": "subheadline", "tracking": 0, "uppercase": true }
368	    }
369	  }
370	}
371	```
372	
373	(The values show the grammar. They are not the default document.)
374	
375	| Key | Holds |
376	|---|---|
377	| `schema` | `1`. A reader ignores keys it does not know. A document with a higher number is refused whole and the theme in use stays |
378	| `name` | A label for people |
379	| `palette` | Named colours. Name to a **colour value** |
380	| `roles` | Colour roles. Role name to a **reference** |
381	| `typography.families` | The three families: `text`, `display`, `code` |
382	| `typography.roles` | Type roles. Role name to an object, every field optional |
383	
384	**Colour value**: a string, or an object `{ "light": <string>, "dark": <string> }`.
385	Each string is one of:
386	
387	- `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA` (the `#` is optional);
388	- `system:<name>`: a platform system colour, live (it follows light, dark,
389	  increased contrast and elevation). The web has no system colours: a web
390	  reader treats a `system:` value as absent and uses its own default.
391	
392	A light and dark pair exists only in `palette`, so `roles` is a flat map of
393	strings. A pair has no increased-contrast or elevated variant.
394	
395	**Reference** (the value of a role): a string that is, tried in this order,
396	
397	1. a palette name (`"teal"`),
398	2. another role's name (`"ripul.accent"` or `"accent"`), followed until it ends,
399	3. a literal colour string as above.
400	
401	A reference that leads nowhere, or round in a circle, gives the role's default
402	in code. Nothing resolves to magenta.
403	
404	**Role names** are written `ripul.accent` in Ripul's own document. The reader
405	also accepts `accent`.
406	
407	**Families**: `"system"`, `"system-serif"`, `"system-rounded"`,
408	`"system-monospaced"`, or the name of a font family the app bundles.
409	
410	**Type role object**:
411	
412	| Field | Meaning | When absent |
413	|---|---|---|
414	| `family` | `text`, `display` or `code` | the role's default family |
415	| `size` | points at the default Dynamic Type size | the system size of `relativeTo` |
416	| `weight` | `ultraLight`, `thin`, `light`, `regular`, `medium`, `semibold`, `bold`, `heavy`, `black` | the system weight of `relativeTo` |
417	| `relativeTo` | the system text style it scales with | the role's default |
418	| `tracking` | points; applied by `ripulTextStyle` only | 0 |
419	| `uppercase` | boolean; applied by `ripulTextStyle` only | false |
420	| `catalystSize` | a fixed size on Mac Catalyst | `size` |
421	
422	### In another host's document
423	
424	One rule, one reader (`RipulTheme.adopt(documentData:)`): if the document has
425	an object under the reserved top-level key `ripul`, that object is the SDK's
426	part, in the shape above, and the rest of the document is the host's
427	business. Otherwise the whole document is the SDK's part (Ripul's own file).
428	
429	```json
430	{ "colors": { "accent": "12CEA8" }, "semantic": { }, "fonts": { },
431	  "ripul": { "roles": { "accent": "#12CEA8" } } }
432	```
433	
434	The SDK never reads a host's own palette, roles or fonts, and a host's theme
435	editor never lists the SDK's roles. A build older than this ignores the key.
436	
437	**Not built:** nothing yet hands a host's document to that reader. A host
438	that follows a hosted theme decodes its document itself and gives the engine
439	only its own slice, so a `ripul` section in WAC's hosted theme would be read
440	by nobody and dropped by the next publish from a phone. Until the three
441	paths are built (remote apply, bundled load and restored draft reading the
442	key from the raw data; publish merging it back), the SDK's screens inside
443	another host show the system look, which is what the plan decided. The key
444	is reserved so that it can be built without a format change.
445

468	## Live repaint
469	
470	A view already on screen changes when a document is adopted, with nothing
471	written in the view.
472	
473	How. Each accessor reads an `@Observable` store when it is called. SwiftUI
474	records that read against the body that made the call and runs the body
475	again when the store changes. A colour style carries its resolved colour
476	inside it, so the new body produces a different style.
477	
478	Proved on 10 October 2026 (iPhone 18 Pro, iOS 27.0, light and dark) with a
479	probe app linking this package: a view with no state and no inputs, drawn in
480	a window, a list row, a sheet, a hosting controller that is a theme root and
481	one that is not. After `RipulTheme.adopt` of the loud document with no other
482	change:
483	
484	| Read by the view | Window | List row | Sheet | Rooted hosting controller | Bare hosting controller |
485	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
486	| `Font.ripul(.body)`, with a weight, and a fixed size | changed | changed | changed | changed | changed |
487	| `.ripul(.danger)`, `.ripul(.textSecondary)` (style form) | changed | changed | changed | changed | changed |
488	| `Color.ripul(.success)` (Color form) | changed | changed | changed | changed | changed |
489	| `.tint`, `Color.accentColor` | changed | changed | changed | changed | changed |
490	| Text with no font of its own | changed | changed | changed | changed | not changed |
491	| A UIKit view that read `UIColor.ripul` once | not changed | not changed | not changed | not changed | not changed |
492	
493	And every value went back after `RipulTheme.resetToDefaults()`.
494	
495	What does not repaint by itself, and what to do:
496	
497	- **UIKit code**: a colour or font read in `makeUIView`, a cell's
498	  configuration, `viewDidLoad`. Read it again on
499	  `Notification.Name.ripulThemeDidChange`, or in `updateUIView`. A dynamic
500	  `UIColor` (a light and dark pair) follows the appearance by itself; it does
501	  not follow a new document.
502	- **Anything computed outside a body and kept**: an attributed string built
503	  and cached by a renderer or a model, a `Canvas` drawing closure's captured
504	  values, a value computed in an `init`. It changes when it is next rebuilt.
505	- **Text with no font of its own** in a presented hosting controller that is
506	  not a theme root. (One embedded as a child of a rooted tree does change.)
507	
508	The first version of the style looked the colour up when it was drawn, and
509	did not repaint: SwiftUI resolves a style again only when the style's own
510	value changes. That is why the style holds its value.
511	
512	The older contract still works: a view that reads
513	`@Environment(\.ripulThemeVersion)` is invalidated under a theme root.
514	
515	## What the root reaches
516	
517	`ripulThemeRoot()` is on both of the app's window groups, on the content of
518	`ripulSheet(isPresented:)` and `ripulSheet(item:)`, in
519	`ripulThemedHostingController`, and on 14 of the SDK's 24 hosting
520	controllers. It sets the window's tint to the accent, the theme's `body` font
521	as the default font, and nothing else. With no theme all of them are nil,
522	which means "inherit", so it changes nothing.
523	
524	**Measured** (10 October 2026; throwaway apps under `/tmp`; iOS 17.2 and
525	27.0; light and dark; centre pixel of a square of each style):
526	
527	- **The accent, with no call-site edit.** Setting `UIWindow.tintColor`
528	  reaches `.tint`, `Color.accentColor`, `UIColor.tintColor` and button labels
529	  in a window, a list row, a sheet, a full-screen cover, a popover, a
530	  presented hosting controller and a child hosting controller. SwiftUI's
531	  `.tint()` alone does not: `Color.accentColor` stays system blue in a sheet,
532	  a cover and a popover, and nothing follows in a hosting controller.
533	- **Text colours cannot come from a root.** A root `.foregroundStyle` changes
534	  what `.secondary` draws even when given today's label colour (138,138,142
535	  becomes 128,128,128, because SwiftUI then derives secondary as half the
536	  root colour), recolours borderless button labels to the text colour, and
537	  does not reach a hosting controller. Hence the edit at the call site.
538	- **The style form is the system's style**: `.ripul(.text)`,
539	  `.ripul(.textSecondary)`, `.ripul(.textTertiary)`, `.ripul(.textQuaternary)`
540	  and `.ripul(.danger)` against `.primary`, `.secondary`, `.tertiary`,
541	  `.quaternary` and `.red`, side by side: identical on a plain background, in
542	  a list row, a section header, a sheet, inside a prominent button, inside a
543	  small bordered button, on `.glassEffect(.regular)` and on
544	  `.glassEffect(.clear)`. On `.regularMaterial` and `.ultraThinMaterial` they
545	  agree to within 1 in one channel, and so do two squares of the very same
546	  `Color.secondary` there, so that difference is the material's own.
547	- **System controls under a themed accent and family** (looked at, not
548	  sampled): toolbar buttons, a toggle's on colour, plain, bordered and
549	  prominent buttons, a menu's label, a progress bar, a slider, a label's
550	  symbol, the selected tab and an alert's buttons all take the accent. Text
551	  in form rows, buttons, menus and toolbar buttons takes the family.
552	  **Not reached by the family:** a large navigation title, a segmented
553	  picker's labels, tab bar labels, an alert's title and buttons. Those are
554	  drawn by UIKit and need its appearance API: a brand-step item.
555	
556	### Measured again, with Mac Catalyst
557	
558	A second run on 10 October 2026 (probe app under `/tmp/theme-cat`; iPhone 17
559	simulator on iOS 27.0, and the Mac idiom on this Mac; light and dark; pixels
560	read from screenshots). The full table is plan task `t_2f86f3c4bfce`'s report.
561	It confirms the above for iPhone and adds these.
562	
563	**Confirmed.** With the default document every colour role, in both forms,
564	draws the system's pixels on Catalyst in every container, in light and dark,
565	and under Increased Contrast on both platforms. In a selected `.sidebar` row
566	on Catalyst the system draws the hierarchy styles in the accent, and the
567	style form matches it exactly. With no theme the root leaves a Mac user's own
568	accent colour alone. A second window group with a root takes the tint and
569	repaints. A text field's cursor and selection follow the accent on iPhone,
570	its selection on Catalyst.
571	
572	**On Catalyst the window's tint does not cross a presentation.**
573	
574	| Place, under a themed accent | iPhone | Catalyst |
575	|---|---|---|
576	| `ripulSheet`, `ripulThemedHostingController`, a rooted second window | follows | follows |
577	| A bare `.sheet`, a popover with no root inside | follows | `.tint` follows; `Color.accentColor` stays the system's |
578	| A presented hosting controller that is not a root | follows | nothing of the accent follows |
579	| A window group or a `UIWindow` with no root | does not follow | does not follow |
580	
581	So on Catalyst a presented view needs a root inside it. A popover's content
582	has none unless you give it one: `.popover { content.ripulThemeRoot() }`.
583	
584	**On Catalyst the Mac keeps some of its own accent.** When the user has
585	chosen an accent colour, `Color.accentColor` stays that colour under a theme,
586	even in the root window, while `.tint` is the theme's. The checkbox a `Toggle`
587	becomes and a progress bar stay the system accent under any theme. Toolbar
588	items stay black. So on Catalyst a `Color.accentColor` site follows the theme
589	only if it is written `Color.ripul(.accent)`: a brand-step decision, since
590	that edit is not an identity where the user has chosen an accent.
591	
592	**`Color(UIColor.tintColor)` as a SwiftUI colour follows on neither
593	platform.** Write `Color.accentColor` or `.tint`.
594	
595	**A themed accent colours things that have no colour today.** On iPhone
596	toolbar buttons go from the label colour to the accent, a swipe action with no
597	tint goes to the accent (a destructive one too, which is red today), and a
598	toggle goes from green to the accent. On Catalyst plain and bordered buttons
599	stop looking like Mac buttons. None of this happens with the default
600	document. A swipe action tinted with a role in the Color form keeps its role.
601	
602	**Text the system draws keeps the system font on both platforms:** a
603	navigation title, segmented labels, tab bar labels, alerts, menu items, swipe
604	action labels. In an open menu the icons take the accent and nothing else
605	follows.
606	
607	**A themed text role in a selected sidebar row** draws the document's colour
608	and loses the selection treatment the system gives the hierarchy styles.
609	
610	**Not measured:** on Catalyst an open menu, a context menu, swipe actions and
611	the insertion-point cursor (the Mac's screen was locked for the run, so
612	Catalyst controls were read under a forced active appearance and nothing was
613	clicked); iOS 17 for either later run.
614	
615	**Hosting controllers that are not theme roots**, because their type is
616	declared and a wrapped root view would change it: `FloatingPanel`,
617	`KeyboardAttachedOverlay` (it copies its parent's environment),
618	`NativeToolStripAnchorController`, `RipulConformanceScreen` (one of two),
619	`NativeInteractionRenderer`, `NativeTaskRunRenderer`, `NativeTrainRenderer`,
620	`NativeDeclarativeArtefactRenderer`, and two in `RipulDevAssistantOverlay`.
621	On iPhone the accent reaches them through their window. On Catalyst it does
622	not reach one that is presented (the floating panel and the overlays are in
623	windows of their own, with no root): there, under a themed accent, `.tint` and
624	`Color.accentColor` stay the system's. Tokens they read repaint on both. Text
625	with no font of its own misses a themed family in a presented one. In those
626	files give every `Text` a font, and expect to make them roots before a brand

692	each build into its own empty DerivedData:

694	| Builds at once | The first build | After touching one app file |
695	|---|---|---|
696	| one | 79 to 117 s | |
697	| two | 124 and 126 s | 5 s with nothing changed |
698	| four | 335 to 340 s each | 18 s each |

747	python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/ship_duo_sim.py --simulator <udid> --no-launch
748	python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_reference_screens.py capture --simulator <udid> --out /tmp/theme-ref/<stream>
749	python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_reference_screens.py compare ~/.ripul/theme-reference/baseline /tmp/theme-ref/<stream>
750	ripul-train release <lease>
751	```
752	
753	Use a simulator with no account signed in. The baseline is on this Mac, not
754	in git: `~/.ripul/theme-reference/baseline` is fourteen screens in four
755	conditions, captured by S1 from `2a6c772dd`, before any stream's files were
756	touched, after a simulator restart, with the session-list fixtures and with no
757	system alert over any of them. The two earlier baselines beside it
758	(`baseline-foundation`, `baseline-s1`) hold captures covered by the
759	notification-permission alert: do not compare against them. `capture` now
760	restarts the simulator first and has no signed-out screen, which is what
761	raised that alert. Look at a few of your captures before you trust a
762	comparison: two covered pictures compare as identical.
763	
764	## The loud document
765	
766	`theme/ripul-theme-loud.json`: every colour role a different saturated
767	colour, three different families, every type role a different size. In a
768	Debug build of the app:
769	
770	- launch argument `-ripul.theme.document ripul-theme-loud`, or
771	- open `ripul://theme?name=ripul-theme-loud` (and `name=ripul-theme` to go
772	  back). The choice is kept between launches.
773	
774	A view that does not change has a call site the migration missed; a view in
775	the wrong loud colour has the wrong role. A Release build ignores the choice.
776	
777	## The brand document (a trial)
778	
779	`theme/ripul-theme-brand.json` is a first look at the website's brand, chosen
780	exactly as the loud document is (`-ripul.theme.document ripul-theme-brand`, or
781	`ripul://theme?name=ripul-theme-brand`), in a Debug build only. It is not the
782	default and not the finished brand step.
783	
784	| It sets | To |
785	|---|---|
786	| `ripul.accent` | the website's teal: `#1f6f70` light, `#62b9b4` dark |
787	| `ripul.onAccent` | white in light (5.89 to 1 on the teal); the website's ink `#23253a` in dark (6.53 to 1), where white is 2.30 to 1 and fails |
788	| the `text` family | `Archivo` |
789	| the `display` family | `Instrument Serif` |
790	| `display` | 36 points (28 on Mac Catalyst) |
791	| `eyebrow` | semibold, capitals, 1.8 points of tracking (the website's 0.14 em at 13 px) |
792	
793	It sets no canvas, surface or text colour, and no size but the display
794	role's, so each other style keeps the platform's own size.
795	
796	**The fonts** are in `theme/fonts/`, copied into the app as the folder `fonts`
797	and registered at launch by `RipulAppTheme.registerFonts()` in every build.
798	`theme/fonts/SOURCES.md` says where each file came from; the licences are
799	beside them.
800	
801	**Measured on 10 October 2026** (a macOS probe that registers the files and
802	draws with SwiftUI; then looked at in the simulator):
803	
804	- Archivo is one variable file. `Font.custom("Archivo", ...)` takes
805	  `.weight()`: light, regular, medium, semibold and bold each draw more ink
806	  than the last, and `.bold()` equals `weight: .bold`. `heavy` draws as black.
807	- Archivo has fixed-width digits (`tnum`): under `.monospacedDigit()` ten ones
808	  and ten zeros are the same width; without it they differ by 8 per cent.
809	- Instrument Serif is regular and italic only. `.bold()` on it draws the
810	  regular: the system does not fake a bold.
811	
812	It gives the `display` role a size (36 points, 28 on Mac Catalyst): Instrument
813	Serif has one weight, so the title carries by size where a bold 28 point
814	sans did.
815	
816	**The display role is read in one place:** the four onboarding titles
817	(`OnboardingView.swift`). `ripulTextStyle(.eyebrow)` is used nowhere yet, so
818	the eyebrow's tracking shows nowhere.
819	
820	## The View Explorer
821	
822	Select an element in the View Explorer and its Appearance section names the
823	theme tokens that style it: each colour role with a swatch, each type role
824	with its face and size, and for both whether the value is the default or
825	comes from the theme document. The same lines are in the explorer's text
826	readout (Copy, and the `explorer_probe` device tool) under `appearance:`.
827	
828	Nothing registers this and no call site declares anything. The identifier and
829	the accessor were already in the source.
830	
831	**How it knows.** SwiftUI draws into layers, so the view that was tapped holds
832	no colour and no font. `ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_usage_map.py` reads the
833	source at build time: every `.uiKitIdentifier("…")` and
834	`.accessibilityIdentifier("…")`, and the accessors in the view expression it
835	ends. The app's Debug build writes the result into the bundle as
836	`ripul-theme-usage.json`, and `RipulBaseTokenProvider` (SDK) looks the selected
837	element's identifier up in it and resolves each token against the live theme.
838	
839	For an identifier it records the accessors:
840	
841	| Found | Shown as |
842	|---|---|
843	| in the element's own expression | `Foreground` |
844	| on a `.font(…)`, `.foregroundStyle(…)`, `.foregroundColor(…)` or `.tint(…)` applied to a view that encloses it in the same function | `Font (from an enclosing view)` |
845	| through a `Font` or `Color` property of the same type, or a local `let` | `Font (in titleFont, one of several)` |
846	| inside a view type, a view-returning member or a `View` extension modifier that the expression names, two steps deep | `Foreground (in SessionTitleLozenge)` |
847	
848	A font or colour written on the element that is not a token (a model's
849	colour, a material, a value passed in) is listed as "not a theme token" with
850	the source text, so that no token is never read as nothing sets it.
851	
852	**What the system draws, where it is not what the source writes.** A text
853	role's default is the system's hierarchical style, and inside a `Button`, a
854	`Menu` or a `Link` that style is a step of the control's own foreground, which
855	is its tint. So the top bar's buttons write `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))`
856	and are drawn in the accent (seen on the phone under the brand document: the
857	chevron is the teal). The map marks every accessor that sits inside such a
858	control, with any `.buttonStyle` chained to it, and the section then shows:
859	
860	| The source | The section says |
861	|---|---|
862	| a default text role, style form, in a control with no button style | `ripul.accent, as the system draws it`, the accent's value and swatch, and that the source writes the text role |
863	| the same under `.buttonStyle(.plain)`, or in the Color form, or a role the theme names | the role as written |
864	| the same under another button style | the role, "a step of the control's own label colour", and no swatch |
865	| the same in a toolbar with no themed accent | the role, and that it becomes the accent once a theme names one |
866	| a control with no foreground written at all | "the system colours it": usually the accent, and no swatch, because a menu or a toolbar draws it otherwise |
867	| a control that is an item of a menu, a context menu, swipe actions, an alert or a dialog | the role, "the system's own colour for a menu item", and no swatch |
868	| a `Toggle` | its on colour: the system's green, and the accent once a theme names one |
869	
870	A button style set by a view around the control, in another function, is not
871	seen, and each of these lines says so.
872	
873	**Checked against pixels** on 11 October 2026 (iPhone Duo simulator, iOS 27.1,
874	the Agents screen; the app's own frame at one pixel a point, the strongest ink
875	in each element's box):
876	
877	| Element | The section says | Default, light | Brand, light | Brand, dark |
878	|---|---|---|---|---|
879	| top bar menu button (`.ripul(.text)` in a `Button`) | the accent | blue `#3472AD` | teal `#2D5556` | teal `#8AB7B4` |
880	| top bar "…" (`.ripul(.text)` in a `Menu`) | the accent | blue `#2579C7` | teal `#2A5E5E` | teal `#7EB6B0` |
881	| new-session "+" in the bar (no foreground, toolbar) | label colour, then the accent | black | teal `#205957` | teal `#98D1CE` |
882	| "New Chat" pill (plain button, no foreground in that branch) | "one of several" | black | black | white |
883	| "18 more" (plain button, `textSecondary`) | `ripul.textSecondary` | grey `#7D7D7D` | grey `#7F7F7F` | grey `#8F8F8F` |
884	
885	The accent's own values are `#0088FF`, `#1F6F70` and `#62B9B4`: a thin symbol
886	on glass at one pixel a point reads darker or lighter than its colour, so the
887	hue is what these prove, not the value. On the phone at three pixels a point
888	the same button measured `#57B5AA` against `#62B9B4`.
889	
890	A token written in one branch of an `if` or a `switch` inside the element is
891	"one of several", like one side of a ternary. A swatch's hex is `#RRGGBBAA`
892	when the colour is not opaque (the system's secondary label is 60 per cent).
893	Where the nearest identifier is the whole screen's, nothing is listed.
894	
895	An accessor inside a part that has its own identifier belongs to the part.
896	An identifier with an interpolation (`"row.\(id)"`) is kept as a pattern.
897	
898	**A view with no identifier** gets the tightest identified element around it,
899	and the section says which one it used.
900	
901	**A UIKit view** (a navigation title, a label in a cell) holds its font and
902	colour, so they are read off the view and compared with the roles. A match is
903	shown as "the same colour as this role": it says what the view holds, not what
904	the code wrote.
905	
906	**When nothing can be named** the section says why: the view has no identifier
907	and nothing identified is around it; the identifier is not in the map (set in
908	UIKit, held in a variable, or in another package); the element's source names
909	no token; or the build carries no map.
910	
911	**Another host's provider is not replaced.** `RipulTokenInspector.provider` is
912	asked first, and its answer stands alone when it has one. The base vocabulary
913	answers only where the host has nothing to say, and inside such a host it
914	answers from the map only, never by matching a UIKit view's colours. A host
915	turns it off with `RipulTokenInspector.answersForBaseVocabulary = false`.
916	
917	**Limits.**
918	
919	- It reads text, it does not compile. A colour passed in as a parameter, a font
920	  set by a caller in another type, and an identifier held in a variable (40 of
921	  1,529 on 11 October 2026) are not seen. On that day 875 identifiers named at
922	  least one token and 44 more had only a font or colour that is not a token.
923	- It says what the source can draw, not what is on screen now: where the code
924	  chooses between roles, each is listed as "one of several".
925	- Text with no font written on it or around it is reported as taking the
926	  root's default font. That is reasoned from `ripulThemeRoot()`, not read.
927	- The explorer does not resolve an element drawn in the keyboard's overlay (the
928	  chat composer's buttons): it finds only the screen's identifier, and the
929	  section says so.
930	- Only an app whose build runs the script has a map. A host that does not sees
931	  the SDK's own screens without tokens, and the section says the map is missing.
932	- Debug builds only.
933	- Reading only. The explorer cannot change a base token: see Limits.
934	
935	```bash
936	python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_usage_map.py --stats
937	python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_usage_map.py --explain AgentScreen.topBar.leadingButton
938	python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_usage_map.py --roots <an app's source directories> --out <file>
939	```
940	
941	The tests are `Tests/RipulAgentTests/RipulThemeUsageTests.swift`.
942	
943	## For the theme's owner
944	
945	```swift
946	try RipulTheme.adopt(documentData: data)   // a whole document; throws and changes nothing if it is refused
947	RipulTheme.resetToDefaults()               // back to the system look
948	RipulTheme.color(.accent)                  // the resolved value, light and dark
949	RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent)
950	```
951	
952	The app does this in `ripul-native-app/iOS/RipulAppTheme.swift`. The base
953	vocabulary is separate from the host engine (`RipulThemeEngine`): a host's
954	`configure` does not touch it.
955	
956	In the host engine, additive and for any host: a palette entry may be a light
957	and dark pair (held in `RipulThemeDocument.primitivesDark`, so `primitives`
958	stays a map of strings), and a colour reference may be `system:<name>` or
959	`#RRGGBBAA`.
960	
961	## Limits
962	
963	- **The theme editor cannot edit these tokens.** It writes one hex over a
964	  pair and cannot choose a system colour or a font. A look is tried by
965	  loading a document. There is no list of documents in the app's settings:
966	  the switch is the launch argument and the URL above.
967	- **The widgets and the Live Activity** do not link the SDK and are not
968	  themed.
969	- **A custom family and Dynamic Type.** A themed role with a size uses
970	  `Font.custom(_:size:relativeTo:)`, which scales on a slightly different
971	  curve from the system's at accessibility sizes.
972	- **Mac Catalyst type.** The text-size setting does nothing on Catalyst. A
973	  role with a `size` and no `catalystSize` is drawn at that size, which is an
974	  iPhone size (18 against a 13 point system body, measured), so a brand
975	  document needs a `catalystSize` for every role it sizes. A family with no
976	  sizes is drawn at the platform's own size for each style (13 for body on
977	  Catalyst): that was 17 when measured and was corrected afterwards, and the
978	  correction is reasoned, not rerun on Catalyst. The reference screens do not
979	  capture Catalyst.
980	- **A sized role in a system face, and `UIFont.ripul`,** follow the real
981	  text-size setting only, not a local `.dynamicTypeSize` or a trait override.
982	- **Reference screens** cover what a signed-out install can show: the start
983	  chooser, the standalone workspace and nine developer fixtures. No session
984	  list, chat or settings screen is in them, because nothing loads fixture
985	  data for those. Reduce Motion is not set.
986

# Theming: fonts and colours from a theme

This is the contract for every agent migrating call sites under
`docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md`, and for anyone writing a new view in the
SDK or the Ripul app. It says what a view writes, what the tokens are called,
what Ripul's theme document looks like, and how to check your work. If you
need a token, role or rule that is not here, ask the foundation owner (a
comment on the plan's Foundation section): do not invent one.

Nothing in this file is pending. Where a thing is not built, it says so.

The code is in `Sources/RipulAgent/ThemeCore/` (four files, compiling on iOS
and macOS). The tests are `Tests/RipulAgentTests/RipulThemeCoreTests.swift`.

## The one idea

Every token has a default, written in code, that is the system value the call
site used before: `Font.ripul(.body)` is `Font.body`, `.ripul(.textSecondary)`
is the system's `.secondary` style, `UIColor.ripul(.text)` is `UIColor.label`,
the same object. So a migrated call site draws the same pixels, and the
default theme document is empty. A theme document changes a token only by
naming it.

## What a view writes

### Fonts (SwiftUI)

| Today | Write |
|---|---|
| `.font(.body)` | `.font(.ripul(.body))` |
| `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold))` | `.font(.ripul(.caption, weight: .semibold))` |
| `.font(.headline.bold())` | `.font(.ripul(.headline).bold())` |
| `.font(.caption.monospacedDigit())` | `.font(.ripul(.caption).monospacedDigit())` |
| `.font(.caption.monospaced())` | `.font(.ripul(.caption, family: .code))` |
| `.font(.system(.caption, design: .monospaced))` | `.font(.ripul(.caption, family: .code))` |
| `.font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))` on text | `.font(.ripul(size: 14, weight: .medium))` |
| `.font(.system(size: 12, design: .monospaced))` | `.font(.ripul(size: 12, family: .code))` |
| `.font(.system(size: 18))` on an `Image` | `.font(.ripulIcon(size: 18))` |
| `.font(.title2)` on an `Image` | `.font(.ripulIcon(.title2))` |
| `Font.caption` as a value | `Font.ripul(.caption)` |

Rules:

- `.bold()`, `.italic()`, `.monospacedDigit()`, `.leading(...)` stay chained
  calls. `.bold()` is not `weight: .bold`: the two draw different pixels
  (measured).
- `.monospaced()` and `design: .monospaced` draw the same pixels (measured),
  so both become `family: .code`.
- A fixed size stays fixed. In a custom family it is
  `Font.custom(_:fixedSize:)`, because `.system(size:)` does not scale with
  Dynamic Type and its replacement must not either.
- A bare text style is a font wherever its type is `Font`, not only inside
  `.font(`: a property (`var titleFont: Font { flag ? .caption2 : .caption }`),
  a `return .headline`, a ternary inside `.font(...)`. Each becomes
  `.ripul(<the same style>)`. These are easy to miss: the script does not
  rewrite them, and a row that takes its fonts from such properties stays in
  the system font under a themed family (found on the session row with the
  loud document).
- A weight may be the argument or a chained call: `.ripul(.body, weight: w)`
  and `.ripul(.body).weight(w)` are the same value under every theme, whatever
  `w` is, a ternary included. Prefer the argument.
- A design chosen at run time,
  `.font(.system(.caption, design: isTag ? .monospaced : .default))`, becomes
  `.font(.ripul(.caption, family: isTag ? .code : nil))`: a nil family is the
  role's own. The ternary may also go outside,
  `.font(isTag ? .ripul(.caption, family: .code) : .ripul(.caption))`; the lint
  reads both. (`.system(.caption, design: .default)` and `.caption` are taken
  to draw the same; that one is reasoned, not measured.)
- `ripulIcon` is never themed. A font on an `Image(systemName:)` is an icon
  size, not type.
- `.rounded` and `.serif` designs have no accessor. The two `.rounded` sites
  are exempt by name (`// theme-exempt: rounded design`).
- View-level `.fontWeight()`, `.bold()` and `.italic()` are left alone.
- `View.ripulTextStyle(.eyebrow)` applies a role's font and, when a theme sets
  them, its tracking and capitals. With no theme it is `.font(.ripul(role))`.
  A call site that writes `.textCase(.uppercase)` today keeps it.

### Colours (SwiftUI)

There are two forms, and which one you write matters.

**The style form**, wherever a `ShapeStyle` is accepted (`foregroundStyle`,
`fill`, `stroke`, `background`, `tint`, `strokeBorder`):

```swift
.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))     // was .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
.fill(.ripul(.danger))                        // was .fill(.red)
.background(.ripul(.canvas))                  // was .background(Color(.systemBackground))
```

**The Color form**, only where a `Color` is required (a `shadow(color:)`, a
stored `Color`, a function argument, `foregroundColor`, an `.opacity()` on a
colour):

```swift
Color.ripul(.textSecondary)                   // was Color.secondary
.foregroundColor(.ripul(.textSecondary))      // was .foregroundColor(.secondary)
.shadow(color: Color.ripul(system: .black).opacity(0.2), radius: 4)
```

Why two. The text roles' defaults are SwiftUI's hierarchical styles, and the
system draws `.secondary` differently from the colour `Color.secondary` in a
list row, inside a button and in a section header (measured: in a light list
row the style is 128,128,128 and the colour is 138,138,142; in a prominent
button 128,195,255 against 36,90,142). The style form hands back the system's
own style, so it matches `.secondary` in every place tested. The Color form
hands back `Color.secondary`, which matches what `Color.secondary` drew. So:

- Replace a style with the style form and a `Color` with the Color form.
  Never turn `Color.secondary` into the style form, or `foregroundColor` into
  `foregroundStyle`: that changes pixels. The lint refuses it.
- A bare `.secondary` or `.primary` is whichever the compiler makes it. It is
  a **Color** when the other branch of its ternary is a colour
  (`flag ? .white : .primary`, `flag ? Color.accentColor : .secondary`: the
  two branches share one type, and `.white` is only a Color), when its line
  says so (`var tint: Color = .secondary`), when it is the fallback of a
  `Color?` (`tint ?? .primary` becomes `tint ?? Color.ripul(.text)`), and when it is passed to a `Color`
  parameter or returned from a function that returns `Color`. Write the Color
  form for those: `flag ? Color.ripul(.onAccent) : Color.ripul(.text)`. It is
  the **style** when it is the whole argument of a style call
  (`.foregroundStyle(.secondary)`), or both branches are hierarchy names. The
  lint knows the cases it can read from the line, and takes either form for a
  bare name passed to a parameter or returned, or beside a variable in a
  ternary (`selected ? color : .secondary`), where only the compiler knows:
  there, check the type yourself. If `color` is a `Color`, write the Color form.
- In a ternary, both sides must be the same form:
  `flag ? .ripul(.text) : .ripul(.textSecondary)`. A ternary that mixes a
  colour and a hierarchy style (`flag ? Color.accentColor : .secondary`) is
  not rewritten by the script, and by the rule above it was a `Color` on both
  sides: write the Color form for the hierarchy name and leave the accent.

**The accent is not edited.** `.tint`, `Color.accentColor`, `.accentColor` and
`UIColor.tintColor` stay as they are: the theme's accent reaches them through
the window's tint (see "What the root reaches"). `Color.ripul(.accent)` exists
for a literal that means the accent, such as `Color.blue` on a selected mark,
and that replacement is a judgement, so it needs a marked reason (below).
A read of `.tint` or `Color.accentColor` under a local `.tint(...)` is that
local tint, not the app's accent: leave it.

### UIKit

```swift
label.textColor = .ripul(.textSecondary)      // was .secondaryLabel
view.backgroundColor = .ripul(.canvas)        // was .systemBackground
label.font = .ripul(.caption)                 // was .preferredFont(forTextStyle: .caption1)
label.font = .ripul(size: 12, weight: .semibold)            // was .systemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .semibold)
label.font = .ripul(size: 12, weight: .regular, family: .code)   // was .monospacedSystemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .regular)
layer.borderColor = UIColor.ripul(.separator).cgColor
```

The type may be left out on either side, as UIKit code usually does:
`v.font = .preferredFont(forTextStyle: .body)` becomes `v.font = .ripul(.body)`,
`label.textColor = .placeholderText` becomes
`label.textColor = .ripul(system: .placeholderText)`. The check and the lint
read both spellings.

UIKit has no hierarchical style, so there the text roles are the label
colours: `UIColor.ripul(.textSecondary)` is `UIColor.secondaryLabel` itself.

### A system colour that no role fits

```swift
Color.ripul(system: .secondarySystemBackground)
.fill(.ripul(system: .tertiarySystemFill))
UIColor.ripul(system: .systemGray5)
Color.ripul(system: .white)        // a scrim, a shadow, a mark on a photograph
```

This draws exactly what the system colour draws and is never themed. The
check counts these apart, and the brand step decides what each becomes. Use
it when the closed table below gives no role. Do not pick the nearest role:
`secondarySystemBackground` is not `surface`.

### Colours that are not theme

Mark them and leave them: `// theme-exempt: <reason>` on the line or the line
above; `// theme-exempt-file: <reason>` in a file's first 30 lines for a
whole file. Exempt by the plan: SF Symbol sizes (use `ripulIcon`), colours
that are data (a provider's, a model's, a chat's, ANSI, syntax and diff
colours), brand marks, materials and glass, `#if DEBUG` harness views,
`CmsRender/`.

### A replacement that is a judgement

When you replace a literal with a token whose default is a different value
(`Color.blue` with `.accent`), the lint stops you. If it is right, say why on
the new line: `// theme-mapping: this blue is the selection mark`. Expect few.

### A colour that meant the app's colour

```swift
.foregroundStyle(.ripul(accentOr: .info))    // was .foregroundStyle(.ripul(.info)), itself .blue
Color.ripul(accentOr: .info)
UIColor.ripul(accentOr: .info)
```

For a system blue that was the app's own colour and not a notice (a machine's
icon, a tile with no colour of its own): the theme's accent once a theme names
one, and until then the role it was. `.ripul(.accent)` is not an identity
there. Measured on the reference screens: the system's tint and its blue are
the same pixels in light, and differ in dark (by up to 19 in a channel) and
under Increased Contrast (by up to 64).

### Controls that style their own text

A root gives a themed family to text with no font of its own, and a themed
accent to tints. Four things it cannot reach, each with a modifier that is the
system's own style while no theme names the value (so nothing changes under
the default document):

| Today | Write | Under a theme |
|---|---|---|
| `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)` | `.ripulProminentButtonStyle()` | the label is drawn in `onAccent` (the system draws it white whatever the fill) |
| `.buttonStyle(.glassProminent)` | `.ripulGlassProminentButtonStyle()` | the same |
| `Section("Title") { }` in a list or form | `Section(themed: "Title") { }` | the header keeps its size and weight, in the family |
| `header: { X }` of a section | `header: { RipulSectionHeader { X } }` | the same |
| `footer: { X }` of a section | `footer: { RipulSectionFooter { X } }` | the footer keeps its small size, in the family |
| `ContentUnavailableView("T", systemImage: "i", description: Text("d"))` | `ContentUnavailableView(themed: "T", systemImage: "i", description: Text("d"))` | title and description in the family |
| `Label("T", systemImage: "i")` as an empty state's label | `RipulEmptyStateLabel("T", systemImage: "i")` | the same |
| `Text("d")` in an empty state's `description:` | `Text("d").ripulEmptyStateDescription()` | the same |

Why sections need it. A grouped list chooses a header's and a footer's font
only while the environment holds no font, and the root's themed family is an
environment font, so without these a header loses its weight and a footer
grows to body size (seen in Settings under the brand document). SwiftUI has
no public way to give a family and leave a control's own choice alone.

Not inside a menu, a picker, a toolbar or a lazy stack: a `Section` there is
not a grouped list's, and a menu takes only a plain title. `ContentUnavailableView.search`
is the system's own wording and stays in the system font.

The sizes are the system's on iOS 27, read from pictures: an empty state's
title is title3 bold and its description body; a section's header is
headline and its footer footnote. They are the same in every list style,
which is not true of the system (a plain list's header differs): a limit.

### Text UIKit draws

Navigation titles (large and inline, so sheet titles too), segmented
controls and tab bar labels are set through UIKit's appearance settings by
`RipulTheme.applySystemTextAppearance()`, which `adopt` and `resetToDefaults`
call. It does nothing until a theme names a text family, restyles the bars
already on screen when one does, and puts every setting back to "not set"
when the family returns to the system's. Not reached: alerts, menus, swipe
action labels, a menu picker's value, and a navigation title on Mac
Catalyst, which the Mac draws in the window's toolbar.

### Never store a token

Call the accessor where the value is used, or where a view is made. These are
fine, because each runs again whenever the view that owns it is rebuilt, and
the read is made inside that view's body:

```swift
struct Chip: View { var tint: Color = Color.ripul(.info) }   // a view's property default
func badge(tint: Color = .ripul(.info)) -> some View          // a parameter's default
```

These are not, because nothing runs them again: a `static let`, a stored
property of a model, a controller or a singleton, a cache. The check fails a
`static let` that holds one; the others it cannot see.

## Ripul's theme document

**Path:** `theme/ripul-theme.json` at the repository root. One file for native
and web. The native app bundles it; the web build reads the same file.
`theme/ripul-theme-loud.json` is a test document (see "The loud document"), and
`theme/ripul-theme-brand.json` a trial of the brand (see "The brand document").

**Shape.** Every key is optional. An absent key means "today's look": the
default written in code on that platform. The default document sets nothing.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "name": "Ripul",
  "palette": {
    "teal": { "light": "#1f6f70", "dark": "#62b9b4" },
    "ink": "#1b2a41"
  },
  "roles": {
    "ripul.accent": "teal",
    "ripul.text": "system:label"
  },
  "typography": {
    "families": { "text": "system", "display": "system", "code": "system-monospaced" },
    "roles": {
      "eyebrow": { "family": "text", "size": 15, "weight": "semibold",
                   "relativeTo": "subheadline", "tracking": 0, "uppercase": true }
    }
  }
}
```

(The values show the grammar. They are not the default document.)

| Key | Holds |
|---|---|
| `schema` | `1`. A reader ignores keys it does not know. A document with a higher number is refused whole and the theme in use stays |
| `name` | A label for people |
| `palette` | Named colours. Name to a **colour value** |
| `roles` | Colour roles. Role name to a **reference** |
| `typography.families` | The three families: `text`, `display`, `code` |
| `typography.roles` | Type roles. Role name to an object, every field optional |

**Colour value**: a string, or an object `{ "light": <string>, "dark": <string> }`.
Each string is one of:

- `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA` (the `#` is optional);
- `system:<name>`: a platform system colour, live (it follows light, dark,
  increased contrast and elevation). The web has no system colours: a web
  reader treats a `system:` value as absent and uses its own default.

A light and dark pair exists only in `palette`, so `roles` is a flat map of
strings. A pair has no increased-contrast or elevated variant.

**Reference** (the value of a role): a string that is, tried in this order,

1. a palette name (`"teal"`),
2. another role's name (`"ripul.accent"` or `"accent"`), followed until it ends,
3. a literal colour string as above.

A reference that leads nowhere, or round in a circle, gives the role's default
in code. Nothing resolves to magenta.

**Role names** are written `ripul.accent` in Ripul's own document. The reader
also accepts `accent`.

**Families**: `"system"`, `"system-serif"`, `"system-rounded"`,
`"system-monospaced"`, or the name of a font family the app bundles.

**Type role object**:

| Field | Meaning | When absent |
|---|---|---|
| `family` | `text`, `display` or `code` | the role's default family |
| `size` | points at the default Dynamic Type size | the system size of `relativeTo` |
| `weight` | `ultraLight`, `thin`, `light`, `regular`, `medium`, `semibold`, `bold`, `heavy`, `black` | the system weight of `relativeTo` |
| `relativeTo` | the system text style it scales with | the role's default |
| `tracking` | points; applied by `ripulTextStyle` only | 0 |
| `uppercase` | boolean; applied by `ripulTextStyle` only | false |
| `catalystSize` | a fixed size on Mac Catalyst | `size` |

### In another host's document

One rule, one reader (`RipulTheme.adopt(documentData:)`): if the document has
an object under the reserved top-level key `ripul`, that object is the SDK's
part, in the shape above, and the rest of the document is the host's
business. Otherwise the whole document is the SDK's part (Ripul's own file).

```json
{ "colors": { "accent": "12CEA8" }, "semantic": { }, "fonts": { },
  "ripul": { "roles": { "accent": "#12CEA8" } } }
```

The SDK never reads a host's own palette, roles or fonts, and a host's theme
editor never lists the SDK's roles. A build older than this ignores the key.

**Not built:** nothing yet hands a host's document to that reader. A host
that follows a hosted theme decodes its document itself and gives the engine
only its own slice, so a `ripul` section in WAC's hosted theme would be read
by nobody and dropped by the next publish from a phone. Until the three
paths are built (remote apply, bundled load and restored draft reading the
key from the raw data; publish merging it back), the SDK's screens inside
another host show the system look, which is what the plan decided. The key
is reserved so that it can be built without a format change.
