## Live repaint

A view already on screen changes when a document is adopted, with nothing
written in the view.

How. Each accessor reads an `@Observable` store when it is called. SwiftUI
records that read against the body that made the call and runs the body
again when the store changes. A colour style carries its resolved colour
inside it, so the new body produces a different style.

Proved on 10 October 2026 (iPhone 18 Pro, iOS 27.0, light and dark) with a
probe app linking this package: a view with no state and no inputs, drawn in
a window, a list row, a sheet, a hosting controller that is a theme root and
one that is not. After `RipulTheme.adopt` of the loud document with no other
change:

| Read by the view | Window | List row | Sheet | Rooted hosting controller | Bare hosting controller |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Font.ripul(.body)`, with a weight, and a fixed size | changed | changed | changed | changed | changed |
| `.ripul(.danger)`, `.ripul(.textSecondary)` (style form) | changed | changed | changed | changed | changed |
| `Color.ripul(.success)` (Color form) | changed | changed | changed | changed | changed |
| `.tint`, `Color.accentColor` | changed | changed | changed | changed | changed |
| Text with no font of its own | changed | changed | changed | changed | not changed |
| A UIKit view that read `UIColor.ripul` once | not changed | not changed | not changed | not changed | not changed |

And every value went back after `RipulTheme.resetToDefaults()`.

What does not repaint by itself, and what to do:

- **UIKit code**: a colour or font read in `makeUIView`, a cell's
  configuration, `viewDidLoad`. Read it again on
  `Notification.Name.ripulThemeDidChange`, or in `updateUIView`. A dynamic
  `UIColor` (a light and dark pair) follows the appearance by itself; it does
  not follow a new document.
- **Anything computed outside a body and kept**: an attributed string built
  and cached by a renderer or a model, a `Canvas` drawing closure's captured
  values, a value computed in an `init`. It changes when it is next rebuilt.
- **Text with no font of its own** in a presented hosting controller that is
  not a theme root. (One embedded as a child of a rooted tree does change.)

The first version of the style looked the colour up when it was drawn, and
did not repaint: SwiftUI resolves a style again only when the style's own
value changes. That is why the style holds its value.

The older contract still works: a view that reads
`@Environment(\.ripulThemeVersion)` is invalidated under a theme root.

## What the root reaches

`ripulThemeRoot()` is on both of the app's window groups, on the content of
`ripulSheet(isPresented:)` and `ripulSheet(item:)`, in
`ripulThemedHostingController`, and on 14 of the SDK's 24 hosting
controllers. It sets the window's tint to the accent, the theme's `body` font
as the default font, and nothing else. With no theme all of them are nil,
which means "inherit", so it changes nothing.

**Measured** (10 October 2026; throwaway apps under `/tmp`; iOS 17.2 and
27.0; light and dark; centre pixel of a square of each style):

- **The accent, with no call-site edit.** Setting `UIWindow.tintColor`
  reaches `.tint`, `Color.accentColor`, `UIColor.tintColor` and button labels
  in a window, a list row, a sheet, a full-screen cover, a popover, a
  presented hosting controller and a child hosting controller. SwiftUI's
  `.tint()` alone does not: `Color.accentColor` stays system blue in a sheet,
  a cover and a popover, and nothing follows in a hosting controller.
- **Text colours cannot come from a root.** A root `.foregroundStyle` changes
  what `.secondary` draws even when given today's label colour (138,138,142
  becomes 128,128,128, because SwiftUI then derives secondary as half the
  root colour), recolours borderless button labels to the text colour, and
  does not reach a hosting controller. Hence the edit at the call site.
- **The style form is the system's style**: `.ripul(.text)`,
  `.ripul(.textSecondary)`, `.ripul(.textTertiary)`, `.ripul(.textQuaternary)`
  and `.ripul(.danger)` against `.primary`, `.secondary`, `.tertiary`,
  `.quaternary` and `.red`, side by side: identical on a plain background, in
  a list row, a section header, a sheet, inside a prominent button, inside a
  small bordered button, on `.glassEffect(.regular)` and on
  `.glassEffect(.clear)`. On `.regularMaterial` and `.ultraThinMaterial` they
  agree to within 1 in one channel, and so do two squares of the very same
  `Color.secondary` there, so that difference is the material's own.
- **System controls under a themed accent and family** (looked at, not
  sampled): toolbar buttons, a toggle's on colour, plain, bordered and
  prominent buttons, a menu's label, a progress bar, a slider, a label's
  symbol, the selected tab and an alert's buttons all take the accent. Text
  in form rows, buttons, menus and toolbar buttons takes the family.
  **Not reached by the family:** a large navigation title, a segmented
  picker's labels, tab bar labels, an alert's title and buttons. Those are
  drawn by UIKit and need its appearance API: a brand-step item.

### Measured again, with Mac Catalyst

A second run on 10 October 2026 (probe app under `/tmp/theme-cat`; iPhone 17
simulator on iOS 27.0, and the Mac idiom on this Mac; light and dark; pixels
read from screenshots). The full table is plan task `t_2f86f3c4bfce`'s report.
It confirms the above for iPhone and adds these.

**Confirmed.** With the default document every colour role, in both forms,
draws the system's pixels on Catalyst in every container, in light and dark,
and under Increased Contrast on both platforms. In a selected `.sidebar` row
on Catalyst the system draws the hierarchy styles in the accent, and the
style form matches it exactly. With no theme the root leaves a Mac user's own
accent colour alone. A second window group with a root takes the tint and
repaints. A text field's cursor and selection follow the accent on iPhone,
its selection on Catalyst.

**On Catalyst the window's tint does not cross a presentation.**

| Place, under a themed accent | iPhone | Catalyst |
|---|---|---|
| `ripulSheet`, `ripulThemedHostingController`, a rooted second window | follows | follows |
| A bare `.sheet`, a popover with no root inside | follows | `.tint` follows; `Color.accentColor` stays the system's |
| A presented hosting controller that is not a root | follows | nothing of the accent follows |
| A window group or a `UIWindow` with no root | does not follow | does not follow |

So on Catalyst a presented view needs a root inside it. A popover's content
has none unless you give it one: `.popover { content.ripulThemeRoot() }`.

**On Catalyst the Mac keeps some of its own accent.** When the user has
chosen an accent colour, `Color.accentColor` stays that colour under a theme,
even in the root window, while `.tint` is the theme's. The checkbox a `Toggle`
becomes and a progress bar stay the system accent under any theme. Toolbar
items stay black. So on Catalyst a `Color.accentColor` site follows the theme
only if it is written `Color.ripul(.accent)`: a brand-step decision, since
that edit is not an identity where the user has chosen an accent.

**`Color(UIColor.tintColor)` as a SwiftUI colour follows on neither
platform.** Write `Color.accentColor` or `.tint`.

**A themed accent colours things that have no colour today.** On iPhone
toolbar buttons go from the label colour to the accent, a swipe action with no
tint goes to the accent (a destructive one too, which is red today), and a
toggle goes from green to the accent. On Catalyst plain and bordered buttons
stop looking like Mac buttons. None of this happens with the default
document. A swipe action tinted with a role in the Color form keeps its role.

**Text the system draws keeps the system font on both platforms:** a
navigation title, segmented labels, tab bar labels, alerts, menu items, swipe
action labels. In an open menu the icons take the accent and nothing else
follows.

**A themed text role in a selected sidebar row** draws the document's colour
and loses the selection treatment the system gives the hierarchy styles.

**Not measured:** on Catalyst an open menu, a context menu, swipe actions and
the insertion-point cursor (the Mac's screen was locked for the run, so
Catalyst controls were read under a forced active appearance and nothing was
clicked); iOS 17 for either later run.

**Hosting controllers that are not theme roots**, because their type is
declared and a wrapped root view would change it: `FloatingPanel`,
`KeyboardAttachedOverlay` (it copies its parent's environment),
`NativeToolStripAnchorController`, `RipulConformanceScreen` (one of two),
`NativeInteractionRenderer`, `NativeTaskRunRenderer`, `NativeTrainRenderer`,
`NativeDeclarativeArtefactRenderer`, and two in `RipulDevAssistantOverlay`.
On iPhone the accent reaches them through their window. On Catalyst it does
not reach one that is presented (the floating panel and the overlays are in
windows of their own, with no root): there, under a themed accent, `.tint` and
`Color.accentColor` stay the system's. Tokens they read repaint on both. Text
with no font of its own misses a themed family in a presented one. In those
files give every `Text` a font, and expect to make them roots before a brand
theme ships on Catalyst.

## Checking your work

All from the repository root.

**1. Rewrite the mechanical cases.**

```bash
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/rewrite_theme_tokens.py --dry-run <file or directory>
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/rewrite_theme_tokens.py <file or directory>
```

It rewrites text-style fonts with their weight and chained calls, the
monospaced forms, fixed sizes whose view it can see is a `Text` or an
`Image`, and the hierarchy styles in both forms. It leaves named colours,
mixed ternaries and fixed sizes it cannot place. Its output over the whole
SDK (1,814 lines) compiles for iOS and macOS.

**2. Do the rest by the closed table.**

**3. Lint the diff.**

```bash
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/rewrite_theme_tokens.py --lint                 # working tree against HEAD
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/rewrite_theme_tokens.py --lint HEAD~3          # a range
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/rewrite_theme_tokens.py --lint HEAD -- <path>  # some paths
```

It pairs each removed line with the line that replaced it and accepts the
pair only if every token's default is the value it replaced. It reads a hunk
that removes and adds the same number of lines; where the counts differ it
asks you to pair the lines by hand or mark them.

**4. Compile, before every push.**

```bash
# SDK streams: for the iOS simulator. About 40 s after the first build.
cd ripul-ios-sdk && swift build --scratch-path /tmp/ripul-theme-<stream> \
  --triple arm64-apple-ios17.0-simulator --sdk "$(xcrun --sdk iphonesimulator --show-sdk-path)"

# and once at the end of the stream for macOS:
cd ripul-ios-sdk && swift build --scratch-path /tmp/ripul-theme-<stream>-mac
```

Do not use `-Xswiftc -sdk -Xswiftc ... -Xswiftc -target ...`: that form
builds for macOS whatever it is given. Measured: with a type error placed
inside `#if os(iOS)` it printed "Build complete", and the `--triple` form
reported the error. 151 of the SDK's files are iOS-only.

App streams build the app, with no install and no simulator:

```bash
cd ripul-native-app && DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-27.1.app/Contents/Developer \
  xcodebuild build -project RipulNativeApp.xcodeproj -scheme RipulApp -configuration Debug \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' ARCHS=arm64 ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=NO \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO RIPUL_SKIP_STANDALONE_BUILD=1 -derivedDataPath /tmp/ripul-theme-<stream>-dd
```

`RIPUL_SKIP_STANDALONE_BUILD=1` makes the build bundle the standalone web
interface that is already built and not write it again. Without it every app
build writes `ripul-native-app/StandaloneRuntime/`, and two at once write the
same files. Use it for a compile check only, never for a build you install.

Measured on this Mac (12 cores) on 10 October 2026, from a clean checkout,
each build into its own empty DerivedData:

| Builds at once | The first build | After touching one app file |
|---|---|---|
| one | 79 to 117 s | |
| two | 124 and 126 s | 5 s with nothing changed |
| four | 335 to 340 s each | 18 s each |

So four app streams can each compile before every push: the first build of a
stream is slow when the others start with it, and every one after is seconds.
It runs the app's pre-build steps, the check among them. It reads the
generated project: a stream that adds or removes no file does not run
`xcodegen`. It compiles the working tree, so another agent's unfinished file
in `ripul-native-app` fails your build too: read the error's path before you
look for the fault in your own change.

**5. Run the check on your paths.**

```bash
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/check_theme_tokens.py --paths <file or directory>...
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/check_theme_tokens.py --report
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/check_theme_tokens.py --update S1     # lower your baseline
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/check_theme_tokens.py --finish S1     # when your count is zero
```

**A count of zero is not proof that a file is clean.** The check counts a
bare name (`.orange`, `.secondary`) inside a style call, in an argument whose
label names a colour (`tint: .blue`, `colors: [.blue, .purple]`), on a line
that says its type is `Color`, and after `return`. A bare name passed to an
unlabelled parameter, or assigned to a property declared elsewhere, it cannot
see. Read your diff for those before `--finish`.

Each stream has its own baseline file in
`ripul-native-app/scripts/theme-baseline/`; edit only yours, and only through
`--update` and `--finish`. The app build runs the check. Until a stream is
finished, a count above its baseline is a warning in the build log. After
`--finish` its baseline is zero and any direct font or colour in its files,
in a new file too, fails the build. `--finish` refuses while anything is
left, other agents' additions included: clear those too.

Streams by path: `F` the foundation's five files; `S1` `Sessions/`; `S2`,
`S3`, `S4` the SDK's top-level files A to M, N to S, T to Z; `S5` the SDK's
other subdirectories; `A1`, `A2`, `A3` `ripul-native-app/iOS` A to L, M to R,
S to Z; `A4` `Shared/` and `Browser/`. Not counted: `CmsRender/`,
`ThemeCore/`, the theme editor's screens (`Theme*.swift`,
`Element*Screens.swift`), the View Explorer overlay (`RipulViewExplorer.swift`,
`ViewInspectorOverlay.swift`), `iOS/CarPlay/`, the widgets, the Mac host,
`Sources/RipulCommands/`, and any branch that compiles only for macOS
(`#if os(macOS)`, `#elseif os(macOS)`, the `#else` of `#if os(iOS)` or of
`#if canImport(UIKit)`). The rewrite script leaves those branches alone too.

**6. At the end of the stream, the reference screens.**

```bash
ripul-train acquire simulators os=27.0 type=iPhone booted=false --reason "theme <stream>: reference screens" --json
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/ship_duo_sim.py --simulator <udid> --no-launch
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_reference_screens.py capture --simulator <udid> --out /tmp/theme-ref/<stream>
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_reference_screens.py compare ~/.ripul/theme-reference/baseline /tmp/theme-ref/<stream>
ripul-train release <lease>
```

Use a simulator with no account signed in. The baseline is on this Mac, not
in git: `~/.ripul/theme-reference/baseline` is fourteen screens in four
conditions, captured by S1 from `2a6c772dd`, before any stream's files were
touched, after a simulator restart, with the session-list fixtures and with no
system alert over any of them. The two earlier baselines beside it
(`baseline-foundation`, `baseline-s1`) hold captures covered by the
notification-permission alert: do not compare against them. `capture` now
restarts the simulator first and has no signed-out screen, which is what
raised that alert. Look at a few of your captures before you trust a
comparison: two covered pictures compare as identical.

## The loud document

`theme/ripul-theme-loud.json`: every colour role a different saturated
colour, three different families, every type role a different size. In a
Debug build of the app:

- launch argument `-ripul.theme.document ripul-theme-loud`, or
- open `ripul://theme?name=ripul-theme-loud` (and `name=ripul-theme` to go
  back). The choice is kept between launches.

A view that does not change has a call site the migration missed; a view in
the wrong loud colour has the wrong role. A Release build ignores the choice.

## The brand document (a trial)

`theme/ripul-theme-brand.json` is a first look at the website's brand, chosen
exactly as the loud document is (`-ripul.theme.document ripul-theme-brand`, or
`ripul://theme?name=ripul-theme-brand`), in a Debug build only. It is not the
default and not the finished brand step.

| It sets | To |
|---|---|
| `ripul.accent` | the website's teal: `#1f6f70` light, `#62b9b4` dark |
| `ripul.onAccent` | white in light (5.89 to 1 on the teal); the website's ink `#23253a` in dark (6.53 to 1), where white is 2.30 to 1 and fails |
| the `text` family | `Archivo` |
| the `display` family | `Instrument Serif` |
| `display` | 36 points (28 on Mac Catalyst) |
| `eyebrow` | semibold, capitals, 1.8 points of tracking (the website's 0.14 em at 13 px) |

It sets no canvas, surface or text colour, and no size but the display
role's, so each other style keeps the platform's own size.

**The fonts** are in `theme/fonts/`, copied into the app as the folder `fonts`
and registered at launch by `RipulAppTheme.registerFonts()` in every build.
`theme/fonts/SOURCES.md` says where each file came from; the licences are
beside them.

**Measured on 10 October 2026** (a macOS probe that registers the files and
draws with SwiftUI; then looked at in the simulator):

- Archivo is one variable file. `Font.custom("Archivo", ...)` takes
  `.weight()`: light, regular, medium, semibold and bold each draw more ink
  than the last, and `.bold()` equals `weight: .bold`. `heavy` draws as black.
- Archivo has fixed-width digits (`tnum`): under `.monospacedDigit()` ten ones
  and ten zeros are the same width; without it they differ by 8 per cent.
- Instrument Serif is regular and italic only. `.bold()` on it draws the
  regular: the system does not fake a bold.

It gives the `display` role a size (36 points, 28 on Mac Catalyst): Instrument
Serif has one weight, so the title carries by size where a bold 28 point
sans did.

**The display role is read in one place:** the four onboarding titles
(`OnboardingView.swift`). `ripulTextStyle(.eyebrow)` is used nowhere yet, so
the eyebrow's tracking shows nowhere.

## The View Explorer

Select an element in the View Explorer and its Appearance section names the
theme tokens that style it: each colour role with a swatch, each type role
with its face and size, and for both whether the value is the default or
comes from the theme document. The same lines are in the explorer's text
readout (Copy, and the `explorer_probe` device tool) under `appearance:`.

Nothing registers this and no call site declares anything. The identifier and
the accessor were already in the source.

**How it knows.** SwiftUI draws into layers, so the view that was tapped holds
no colour and no font. `ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_usage_map.py` reads the
source at build time: every `.uiKitIdentifier("…")` and
`.accessibilityIdentifier("…")`, and the accessors in the view expression it
ends. The app's Debug build writes the result into the bundle as
`ripul-theme-usage.json`, and `RipulBaseTokenProvider` (SDK) looks the selected
element's identifier up in it and resolves each token against the live theme.

For an identifier it records the accessors:

| Found | Shown as |
|---|---|
| in the element's own expression | `Foreground` |
| on a `.font(…)`, `.foregroundStyle(…)`, `.foregroundColor(…)` or `.tint(…)` applied to a view that encloses it in the same function | `Font (from an enclosing view)` |
| through a `Font` or `Color` property of the same type, or a local `let` | `Font (in titleFont, one of several)` |
| inside a view type, a view-returning member or a `View` extension modifier that the expression names, two steps deep | `Foreground (in SessionTitleLozenge)` |

A font or colour written on the element that is not a token (a model's
colour, a material, a value passed in) is listed as "not a theme token" with
the source text, so that no token is never read as nothing sets it.

**What the system draws, where it is not what the source writes.** A text
role's default is the system's hierarchical style, and inside a `Button`, a
`Menu` or a `Link` that style is a step of the control's own foreground, which
is its tint. So the top bar's buttons write `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))`
and are drawn in the accent (seen on the phone under the brand document: the
chevron is the teal). The map marks every accessor that sits inside such a
control, with any `.buttonStyle` chained to it, and the section then shows:

| The source | The section says |
|---|---|
| a default text role, style form, in a control with no button style | `ripul.accent, as the system draws it`, the accent's value and swatch, and that the source writes the text role |
| the same under `.buttonStyle(.plain)`, or in the Color form, or a role the theme names | the role as written |
| the same under another button style | the role, "a step of the control's own label colour", and no swatch |
| the same in a toolbar with no themed accent | the role, and that it becomes the accent once a theme names one |
| a control with no foreground written at all | "the system colours it": usually the accent, and no swatch, because a menu or a toolbar draws it otherwise |
| a control that is an item of a menu, a context menu, swipe actions, an alert or a dialog | the role, "the system's own colour for a menu item", and no swatch |
| a `Toggle` | its on colour: the system's green, and the accent once a theme names one |

A button style set by a view around the control, in another function, is not
seen, and each of these lines says so.

**Checked against pixels** on 11 October 2026 (iPhone Duo simulator, iOS 27.1,
the Agents screen; the app's own frame at one pixel a point, the strongest ink
in each element's box):

| Element | The section says | Default, light | Brand, light | Brand, dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| top bar menu button (`.ripul(.text)` in a `Button`) | the accent | blue `#3472AD` | teal `#2D5556` | teal `#8AB7B4` |
| top bar "…" (`.ripul(.text)` in a `Menu`) | the accent | blue `#2579C7` | teal `#2A5E5E` | teal `#7EB6B0` |
| new-session "+" in the bar (no foreground, toolbar) | label colour, then the accent | black | teal `#205957` | teal `#98D1CE` |
| "New Chat" pill (plain button, no foreground in that branch) | "one of several" | black | black | white |
| "18 more" (plain button, `textSecondary`) | `ripul.textSecondary` | grey `#7D7D7D` | grey `#7F7F7F` | grey `#8F8F8F` |

The accent's own values are `#0088FF`, `#1F6F70` and `#62B9B4`: a thin symbol
on glass at one pixel a point reads darker or lighter than its colour, so the
hue is what these prove, not the value. On the phone at three pixels a point
the same button measured `#57B5AA` against `#62B9B4`.

A token written in one branch of an `if` or a `switch` inside the element is
"one of several", like one side of a ternary. A swatch's hex is `#RRGGBBAA`
when the colour is not opaque (the system's secondary label is 60 per cent).
Where the nearest identifier is the whole screen's, nothing is listed.

An accessor inside a part that has its own identifier belongs to the part.
An identifier with an interpolation (`"row.\(id)"`) is kept as a pattern.

**A view with no identifier** gets the tightest identified element around it,
and the section says which one it used.

**A UIKit view** (a navigation title, a label in a cell) holds its font and
colour, so they are read off the view and compared with the roles. A match is
shown as "the same colour as this role": it says what the view holds, not what
the code wrote.

**When nothing can be named** the section says why: the view has no identifier
and nothing identified is around it; the identifier is not in the map (set in
UIKit, held in a variable, or in another package); the element's source names
no token; or the build carries no map.

**Another host's provider is not replaced.** `RipulTokenInspector.provider` is
asked first, and its answer stands alone when it has one. The base vocabulary
answers only where the host has nothing to say, and inside such a host it
answers from the map only, never by matching a UIKit view's colours. A host
turns it off with `RipulTokenInspector.answersForBaseVocabulary = false`.

**Limits.**

- It reads text, it does not compile. A colour passed in as a parameter, a font
  set by a caller in another type, and an identifier held in a variable (40 of
  1,529 on 11 October 2026) are not seen. On that day 875 identifiers named at
  least one token and 44 more had only a font or colour that is not a token.
- It says what the source can draw, not what is on screen now: where the code
  chooses between roles, each is listed as "one of several".
- Text with no font written on it or around it is reported as taking the
  root's default font. That is reasoned from `ripulThemeRoot()`, not read.
- The explorer does not resolve an element drawn in the keyboard's overlay (the
  chat composer's buttons): it finds only the screen's identifier, and the
  section says so.
- Only an app whose build runs the script has a map. A host that does not sees
  the SDK's own screens without tokens, and the section says the map is missing.
- Debug builds only.
- Reading only. The explorer cannot change a base token: see Limits.

```bash
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_usage_map.py --stats
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_usage_map.py --explain AgentScreen.topBar.leadingButton
python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_usage_map.py --roots <an app's source directories> --out <file>
```

The tests are `Tests/RipulAgentTests/RipulThemeUsageTests.swift`.

## For the theme's owner

```swift
try RipulTheme.adopt(documentData: data)   // a whole document; throws and changes nothing if it is refused
RipulTheme.resetToDefaults()               // back to the system look
RipulTheme.color(.accent)                  // the resolved value, light and dark
RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent)
```

The app does this in `ripul-native-app/iOS/RipulAppTheme.swift`. The base
vocabulary is separate from the host engine (`RipulThemeEngine`): a host's
`configure` does not touch it.

In the host engine, additive and for any host: a palette entry may be a light
and dark pair (held in `RipulThemeDocument.primitivesDark`, so `primitives`
stays a map of strings), and a colour reference may be `system:<name>` or
`#RRGGBBAA`.

## Limits

- **The theme editor cannot edit these tokens.** It writes one hex over a
  pair and cannot choose a system colour or a font. A look is tried by
  loading a document. There is no list of documents in the app's settings:
  the switch is the launch argument and the URL above.
- **The widgets and the Live Activity** do not link the SDK and are not
  themed.
- **A custom family and Dynamic Type.** A themed role with a size uses
  `Font.custom(_:size:relativeTo:)`, which scales on a slightly different
  curve from the system's at accessibility sizes.
- **Mac Catalyst type.** The text-size setting does nothing on Catalyst. A
  role with a `size` and no `catalystSize` is drawn at that size, which is an
  iPhone size (18 against a 13 point system body, measured), so a brand
  document needs a `catalystSize` for every role it sizes. A family with no
  sizes is drawn at the platform's own size for each style (13 for body on
  Catalyst): that was 17 when measured and was corrected afterwards, and the
  correction is reasoned, not rerun on Catalyst. The reference screens do not
  capture Catalyst.
- **A sized role in a system face, and `UIFont.ripul`,** follow the real
  text-size setting only, not a local `.dynamicTypeSize` or a trait override.
- **Reference screens** cover what a signed-out install can show: the start
  chooser, the standalone workspace and nine developer fixtures. No session
  list, chat or settings screen is in them, because nothing loads fixture
  data for those. Reduce Motion is not set.

{"guide":"# Trains: builds and deploys shared between agents

When several agents work on one Mac, their builds and deploys collide: two deploys overwrite each other, a rebuild restarts an app someone is testing, an install lands on a phone mid-test. Trainyard, part of Ripul Host, queues that work. A **track** is one job (a deploy, a build, an install). Agents ask for it; one run serves everyone waiting.

## Does this repository use trains?

It does if it has a file `.ripul/trains.yaml`. Then:

```bash
ripul-train config     # the tracks and resources this repository defines
ripul-train status     # what is running, queued, held and held back
```

Where a repository has tracks, use them. Do not run the underlying build or deploy command yourself, even if you can see it in the file.

## Using a track

```bash
ripul-train request <track> --wait          # board the train and wait for the result
ripul-train hold <resource> --reason "testing sign-in" --ttl 20
ripul-train release <hold-id>               # as soon as the test is done
ripul-train block <commit> --reason "not to ship until the owner says"
ripul-train unblock <block-id>
```

- **Only committed, pushed work ships.** A track normally builds the tip of its branch on the remote, not your working tree. Commit and push first.
- **Take a hold before a test that depends on a shared thing** (the live build, a phone, a running app), and release it straight after. A hold keeps trains that would disturb that thing in the yard. Holds expire: 15 minutes by default, 60 at most.
- **A block stops the whole train**, including other agents' work queued behind that commit. It is for "this must not go live yet", not for routine caution.
- **Disruptive steps wait.** A track can end by restarting or reloading something. Trainyard does that only when the other agents' turns have ended, so the request can take a while to return.
- A repository's own scripts may board a train for you. Its instructions file will say which.

## Setting trains up

A repository without the file has no trains. If its agents are colliding, propose adding `.ripul/trains.yaml` to the user; do not add it unasked. In outline:

```yaml
version: 1
resources:
  staging-site: { kind: manual, description: "The staging site; hold it while testing" }
  dev-server:   { kind: port, port: 3000 }
tracks:
  deploy:
    branch: main
    checks: [ "npm test" ]
    run:    [ "npm run deploy" ]
    verify: [ "curl -fsS https://staging.example.com/health" ]
    disturbs: [ staging-site ]
```

A **resource** is a thing trains affect and agents use. Its kind says how Trainyard knows it is in use: `manual` (only while someone holds it), `port`, `process`, `command` (a probe that succeeds while in use) or `agents` (while any agent is mid-turn). A track lists the resources it disturbs. `ripul-train config` checks the file. The Trainyard screen in the Ripul app edits the same file.
","title":"Trains: builds and deploys shared between agents","topic":"trains"}

{"guide":"# Plans

In Ripul a plan is a design document in the repository that can be reviewed: people and agents file comments against its sections, the author answers them, and the fixes become tasks. The user reads and acts on plans in the **Plans** screen of the Ripul apps, where each plan shows as Open or Locked with its comments and tasks. Use this guide when asked to write, review, revise or carry out a plan.

## What a plan is made of

A plan is three files that share a name in `docs/plans/` of the chat's working directory:

- `<slug>.md` is the plan itself, in prose. This is the only file you write by hand, with your normal file tools.
- `<slug>.plan.jsonl` is the log of comments, replies, status changes and tasks. Only the plan tools add to it.
- `<slug>.review.md` is a readable review, rebuilt from the log on every change. Never edit it.

No tool creates a plan. To start one, write `docs/plans/<slug>.md` with a title and `##` sections (the Plans screen starts new plans with Problem, Approach and Open questions). If a file with that name already exists, it is someone's plan: revise it or choose another name.

These are ordinary repository files. The plan tools write to the working directory without asking the user for approval, and they do not commit; commit the files with the rest of your work.

## Which to use: a Ripul plan, or your own plan mode or todo list

When the user asks for a plan, a design or a proposal they will read or have reviewed, write a Ripul plan. Your built-in plan mode and todo list live inside your own session: the user cannot open them in the Plans screen, another agent cannot comment on them, and nothing records what was agreed. Keep your own todo list for private working steps. Work the user should see as owed on a plan goes in with `planTask`.

Plans are not artefacts: the artefact tools do not read or write them. If the user wants a visual summary of a plan, build that separately (see the `artefacts` guide) and keep the Markdown file as the source.

## The tools

| Tool | Use it to |
|---|---|
| `planStatus` | Read a plan's state: section anchors, outstanding comments, open tasks, Open or Locked. Call it first, every time. |
| `planComment` | File a review comment against a section. |
| `planReply` | Discuss a comment without changing its status. |
| `planResolve` | Move a comment to `accepted`, `resolved` or `wontfix`. |
| `planTask` | Record work owed, usually linked to an accepted comment. |
| `planTaskStatus` | Move a task between `open`, `doing`, `done` and `dropped`. |

Each acts on the plan in the working directory of the chat you are running in.

## Statuses and what moves them

**Comments** go one way: `open` to `accepted`, `resolved` or `wontfix`, and `accepted` to `resolved` or `wontfix`. `resolved` and `wontfix` are final and the tool refuses to move a comment back. This stops a later round reopening what an earlier one settled. If there is something new, file a new comment.

**Locked is computed, not set.** A plan is Locked when no `blocking` comment is `open` or `accepted`. You cannot mark a plan done; you can only clear what holds it open. `accepted` still holds it open: agreeing a fix is needed is not confirming it was made.

**Tasks** move freely in both directions. Take them one at a time: `doing` when you start, `done` when the work is finished. Marking a task `done` does not close the comment it came from; the reviewer does that.

**Severity** matters: `blocking` holds the plan open, `should-fix` is a real gap that does not, `nit` is editorial. Use `blocking` only for what would be expensive to find out later.

## Reviewing a plan

1. `planStatus`, to get the anchor list. An anchor is a section's heading turned into a slug. A shortened slug works if it matches exactly one section; an anchor that matches none, or more than one, is refused. Use `__plan__` for a remark about the plan as a whole.
2. `planComment` for each finding, with the defect, why it matters and a proposed fix.
3. On a later round, first check each `accepted` comment against the revised text. Mark it `resolved` if the change answers it; if not, `planReply` and leave it. Then review the plan again for anything new.

## Answering a reviewer's comment

1. `planStatus`, which lists outstanding comments with the hardest first.
2. Where you agree, edit the plan file to fix it, then `planResolve` with `accepted`, and `planTask` with `fromComment` for any work that remains.
3. Where you disagree, `planResolve` with `wontfix` and your reason in `note`. A decline without a reason will be raised again. Use `planReply` to argue the point or ask a question.
4. Do not mark someone else's comment `resolved`. That is the reviewer's confirmation that the fix is real. Sessions started from the Plans screen to draft or address a plan are refused it on comments they did not file. You may resolve a comment you filed yourself.

## Things that go wrong

- **Renaming or removing a heading orphans its comments.** They are kept and listed by `planStatus` as orphaned. When revising, keep existing headings and add subsections instead.
- **`planStatus` lists at most 40 anchors, comments and tasks each**, with long comment bodies cut short and no replies. For the full text and the replies, read `<slug>.review.md`.
","title":"Plans","topic":"plans"}

Your built-in plan mode and todo list live inside your own session: the user cannot open them in the Plans screen, another agent cannot comment on them, and nothing records what was agreed. Keep your own todo list for private working steps. Work the user should see as owed on a plan goes in with `planTask`.

Plans are not artefacts: the artefact tools do not read or write them. If the user wants a visual summary of a plan, build that separately (see the `artefacts` guide) and keep the Markdown file as the source.

## The tools

| Tool | Use it to |
|---|---|
| `planStatus` | Read a plan's state: section anchors, outstanding comments, open tasks, Open or Locked. Call it first, every time. |
| `planComment` | File a review comment against a section. |
| `planReply` | Discuss a comment without changing its status. |
| `planResolve` | Move a comment to `accepted`, `resolved` or `wontfix`. |
| `planTask` | Record work owed, usually linked to an accepted comment. |
| `planTaskStatus` | Move a task between `open`, `doing`, `done` and `dropped`. |

Each acts on the plan in the working directory of the chat you are running in.

## Statuses and what moves them

**Comments** go one way: `open` to `accepted`, `resolved` or `wontfix`, and `accepted` to `resolved` or `wontfix`. `resolved` and `wontfix` are final and the tool refuses to move a comment back. This stops a later round reopening what an earlier one settled. If there is something new, file a new comment.

**Locked is computed, not set.** A plan is Locked when no `blocking` comment is `open` or `accepted`. You cannot mark a plan done; you can only clear what holds it open. `accepted` still holds it open: agreeing a fix is needed is not confirming it was made.

**Tasks** move freely in both directions. Take them one at a time: `doing` when you start, `done` when the work is finished. Marking a task `done` does not close the comment it came from; the reviewer does that.

**Severity** matters: `blocking` holds the plan open, `should-fix` is a real gap that does not, `nit` is editorial. Use `blocking` only for what would be expensive to find out later.

## Reviewing a plan

1. `planStatus`, to get the anchor list. An anchor is a section's heading turned into a slug. A shortened slug works if it matches exactly one section; an anchor that matches none, or more than one, is refused. Use `__plan__` for a remark about the plan as a whole.
2. `planComment` for each finding, with the defect, why it matters and a proposed fix.
3. On a later round, first check each `accepted` comment against the revised text. Mark it `resolved` if the change answers it; if not, `planReply` and leave it. Then review the plan again for anything new.

## Answering a reviewer's comment

1. `planStatus`, which lists outstanding comments with the hardest first.
2. Where you agree, edit the plan file to fix it, then `planResolve` with `accepted`, and `planTask` with `fromComment` for any work that remains.
3. Where you disagree, `planResolve` with `wontfix` and your reason in `note`. A decline without a reason will be raised again. Use `planReply` to argue the point or ask a question.
4. Do not mark someone else's comment `resolved`. That is the reviewer's confirmation that the fix is real. Sessions started from the Plans screen to draft or address a plan are refused it on comments they did not file. You may resolve a comment you filed yourself.

## Things that go wrong

- **Renaming or removing a heading orphans its comments.** They are kept and listed by `planStatus` as orphaned. When revising, keep existing headings and add subsections instead.
- **`planStatus` lists at most 40 anchors, comments and tasks each**, with long comment bodies cut short and no replies. For the full text and the replies, read `<slug>.review.md`.

{"guide":"# Phones, tablets and simulators

You run on the Mac, but the app you are working on often runs on an iPhone, an iPad or a simulator. Use this guide when you need to put a build on a phone, or look at and operate an app running on a device.

## Two families, two different routes

| Family | Reaches the device through | Needs | Sees |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device_…` screen tools | the app itself, over Ripul's relay | the app running in the foreground, built with the Ripul SDK's developer tools | that one app, element by element |
| `host_bridge_…` | Apple's developer tunnel from this Mac, over Tailscale | an iPhone paired with this Mac | the whole phone, as pixels |

They are independent. The bridge can install and launch an app with no Ripul code in it; the screen tools can drive an app in a simulator, which the bridge cannot reach. A typical job uses the bridge to get the build there and the screen tools to test it.

## Choosing the device

Call `device_list_targets` first. It lists each device's handle (for example `iphone-c603`), model, whether it is connected, which tools it offers, and which agent holds it. For a paired iPhone it also gives the name the bridge tools know it by. Check that `inspect_screen` is among a device's tools: without it the device cannot be operated.

A chat has one **working device**: where every `device_…` call acts when it names no `device`. A message from another phone does not move it. `device_set_working_device` moves the chat, and takes the device for this chat alone: other agents' calls to it are refused until you move, pass `release: true`, or go an hour without using it. Release it when the work is done. If the working device is not connected the call fails; nothing falls back to another device.

`host_bridge_…` calls that name no `phone` act on the working device too, and one that would change a phone another agent holds is refused.

## The loop: install, launch, look, tap, verify

1. `host_bridge_status`: is the phone's tunnel active.
2. `host_bridge_run` builds an Xcode project, installs it, checks the installed build and launches it. If you already have a signed `.app`, use `host_bridge_install` (with `launch`). `host_bridge_ship` is not for your project: it builds Ripul's own app.
3. `host_bridge_launch` brings an installed app to the front, or restarts it with `relaunch`.
4. `device_inspect_screen`. Every element comes back with a short handle such as `e7`.
5. `device_tap_element`, `device_type_text`, `device_scroll_element` or `device_set_value`, addressed by that handle.
6. `device_wait_for_element` for the thing that should appear (or, with state `gone`, disappear). It returns the moment the screen matches.
7. `device_inspect_screen` again to confirm, then repeat from 5.

For a simulator, skip the bridge: install and launch with `xcrun simctl`, then start at step 4.

Prefer `device_set_value` for pickers, switches, sliders and segmented controls: it sets the value and fires the app's handler, which is more reliable than operating the control. Use `device_touch` for gestures or an exact point; it takes the window coordinates that inspect reports, and works in debug builds of the app only.

## What inspect can and cannot see

- **Only the app it runs in.** Not the home screen, not another app, not a phone whose app is closed. For those, `host_bridge_screenshot` returns a picture of the whole screen.
- **Only what a person could see.** Views scrolled out of sight, clipped, or covered by something else are left out and counted in `hidden`. Scroll and inspect again, or pass `includeHidden` to see what was left out.
- **Handles expire.** Inspect again after the screen changes.
- An ambiguous tap fails and lists the candidates; nothing is pressed. Narrow it with `within`, `role` or `id` rather than guessing with `nth`.

## What goes wrong

- **The app is in the background.** iOS suspends it, and `device_…` calls go unanswered. Use `host_bridge_launch`, or ask the user to open it.
- **A timeout is not a failure.** When a tap or typing call times out, the action may still have happened: look at the screen before repeating it. Likewise a `host_bridge_install` or `host_bridge_run` call can be cut off while the work carries on: check `host_bridge_projects` for how the last run ended, or inspect the app, before installing again.
- **The phone's network.** A phone accepts a new tunnel only while joined to a Wi-Fi network or to another phone's hotspot, unlocked at least once since it was switched on, with Tailscale connected. On its own cellular connection, or while providing a hotspot itself, it refuses.
- **A phone that was never paired.** Pairing needs the phone plugged into this Mac by USB once, unlocked, with Developer Mode on. Ask the user.
- **Debugging pauses the app.** `host_bridge_debug` attaches LLDB, runs your commands and detaches; the app is stopped while it is attached.

## Recording

`host_record_screen` records a window or a display of the Mac and shows the video in the chat, with a few stills for you to check. That covers a simulator, whose window is on the Mac, but not a physical phone: use `host_bridge_screenshot` before and after instead. It refuses while the Mac's screen is locked, because apps stop drawing behind the lock screen.

## The `device_bridge_…` twins

These are the same bridge tools on another Mac running Ripul Host, for a phone paired with that Mac; pairing is per Mac. Pass `device` for the Mac and `phone` for the phone: these calls do not follow the working device.
","title":"Phones, tablets and simulators","topic":"devices"}

Exit code 1
### 9. One theme system going forward

Decided by Peter on 11 October 2026, after the migration showed that the SDK now holds two theme systems: "I don't mind the WAC app carrying a legacy for a while as long as moving forward it is clean."

- **The base layer is the SDK's theme system.** That is `RipulTheme`, the accessors, the theme document, the root, the usage map and the provider built on it. Everything new is built on it and on nothing else.
- **The older engine is legacy.** `RipulThemeEngine`, its vocabulary registration and its editing screens stay as they are for WAC. They take fixes, not features, and nothing new may depend on them. The SDK's documents say so.
- **No bridges from the new to the old.** Ripul's roles do not go into a host's document, and the new layer reads nothing from the older engine. The reserved `ripul` key in a host's document stays reserved and unread (decision 4).
- **Editing is built new.** An editor for the base layer (light and dark pairs, system colours, type roles, a draft, publishing) is written for it, reusing only what is already general, such as hosting and the publish review. The older screens are not bent to fit.
- **WAC moves later, as its own piece of work,** by a mapping from its vocabulary. Until then it runs the legacy engine unchanged.

Two things have to be settled for the forward path to be clean for an app that is not ours. Neither is built:

- **A host's own tokens.** The base layer has a fixed set of roles. A customer's app, and WAC when it moves, need to add their own.
- **The tools travel with the SDK.** The rewrite script, the lint, the check and the usage map live in this app's scripts folder and carry its file layout.

## The vocabulary

    name: "RipulAgent",
    platforms: [
        .iOS(.v17),

    products: [

        .library(name: "RipulCommands", targets: ["RipulCommands"]),
    ],
    dependencies: [
        .package(url: "https://github.com/gonzalezreal/swift-markdown-ui.git", from: "2.4.1"),

        .package(url: "https://github.com/ripulio/thinking-orbs-swift.git", from: "0.2.0"),
        .package(url: "https://github.com/appstefan/HighlightSwift.git", from: "1.1.0"),
    ],
    targets: [

80	/// One side of a colour: a platform system colour by name, or fixed components.
81	public enum RipulColorLiteral: Equatable, Sendable {
82	    /// `system:label`. Live: it follows light, dark and increased contrast.
83	    case system(String)
84	    case rgba(red: Double, green: Double, blue: Double, alpha: Double)
85	
86	    /// Parse `system:<name>`, `#RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBBAA` (the `#` optional). nil for anything else.
87	    public init?(_ string: String) {
88	        let s = string.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
89	        if s.hasPrefix("system:") {
90	            let name = String(s.dropFirst(7))
91	            guard RipulTheme.systemColorNames.contains(name) else { return nil }
92	            self = .system(name); return
93	        }
94	        var hex = s
95	        if hex.hasPrefix("#") { hex.removeFirst() }
96	        guard hex.count == 6 || hex.count == 8, let value = UInt64(hex, radix: 16) else { return nil }
97	        let rgba = hex.count == 6 ? (value << 8) | 0xFF : value
98	        self = .rgba(red: Double((rgba >> 24) & 0xFF) / 255, green: Double((rgba >> 16) & 0xFF) / 255,
99	                     blue: Double((rgba >> 8) & 0xFF) / 255, alpha: Double(rgba & 0xFF) / 255)
100	    }
101	}

204	/// What SwiftUI watches. An accessor reads `revision` when it is called, and a body that
205	/// called one is run again when the theme changes: no view declares anything.
206	///
207	/// Written out rather than `@Observable`, so that the number itself sits behind a lock:
208	/// an accessor may read it off the main thread while the main thread bumps it.
209	final class RipulThemeStore: Observable, @unchecked Sendable {
210	    static let shared = RipulThemeStore()
211	    private let registrar = ObservationRegistrar()
212	    private let lock = NSLock()
213	    private var stored = 0
214	
215	    var revision: Int {
216	        registrar.access(self, keyPath: \.revision)
217	        lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }
218	        return stored
219	    }
220	
221	    /// Main thread only: this is what tells SwiftUI to run the bodies again.
222	    func bump() {
223	        registrar.withMutation(of: self, keyPath: \.revision) {
224	            lock.lock(); stored += 1; lock.unlock()
225	        }
226	    }
227	}

340	    public static func adopt(documentData: Data) throws {
341	        let (new, part) = try parse(documentData)
342	        lock.lock(); storedTable = new; storedDocument = part; lock.unlock()
343	        let announce = {

345	            #if os(iOS)

354	        guard let document = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data)) as? [String: Any] else {
355	            throw DocumentError.notAnObject

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# release-public.sh — Publish the monorepo RipulAgent SDK to the public
# ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk repo as a clean, one-way mirror + version tag.
#
# The monorepo copy (this script's parent dir) is the source of truth. Histories
# between the two repos diverged long ago, so we do NOT merge — we overwrite the
# public repo's working tree with the monorepo SDK (rsync --delete), commit, and
# tag vX.Y.Z. The push to GitHub happens ONLY with --push (outward-facing step).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/release-public.sh 0.1.0           # stage locally (mirror + commit + tag), no push
#   scripts/release-public.sh 0.1.0 --push    # also push commit + tag to origin
#
# Env:
#   RIPUL_PUBLIC_SDK   path to the public repo clone
#                      (default: $HOME/Documents/ripul-ios-sdk)
set -euo pipefail

VERSION="${1:-}"
PUSH=""
[ "${2:-}" = "--push" ] && PUSH=1

SRC="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"          # monorepo SDK root
DEST="${RIPUL_PUBLIC_SDK:-$HOME/Documents/ripul-ios-sdk}"        # public repo clone
REMOTE_NAME="origin"
TAG="v${VERSION}"

die() { echo "❌ $*" >&2; exit 1; }

[ -n "$VERSION" ] || die "usage: $0 <version> [--push]   e.g. $0 0.1.0"
echo "$VERSION" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' \
  || die "version must be semver X.Y.Z (got: $VERSION)"
[ -d "$SRC/Sources/RipulAgent" ] || die "source SDK not found at $SRC/Sources/RipulAgent"
[ -d "$DEST/.git" ]              || die "public repo clone not found at $DEST (set RIPUL_PUBLIC_SDK)"

echo "▶ Source (monorepo): $SRC"
echo "▶ Dest   (public):   $DEST"
echo "▶ Version:           $TAG"
echo

# Public clone must be clean and not already tagged at this version.
git -C "$DEST" diff --quiet && git -C "$DEST" diff --cached --quiet \
  || die "public repo has uncommitted changes — clean it first"
git -C "$DEST" fetch "$REMOTE_NAME" --tags --quiet || true
if git -C "$DEST" rev-parse --verify "refs/tags/$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  die "tag $TAG already exists — bump the version"
fi

# Stamp the marketing version into the SDK source, so the View Explorer's
# `sdk: …` line reports the release that is actually running on the device.
# Hand-bumping this drifted (it sat at 0.5.8 through the whole 0.6/0.7 series,
# making every element paste misreport the build), so the release owns it.
# Committed in the MONOREPO — the source of truth — before the dirty check
# below, so the tag and the constant can never disagree.
VERSION_FILE="$SRC/Sources/RipulAgent/ViewInspectorOverlay.swift"
CURRENT_VERSION="$(sed -n 's/^let ripulSDKVersion = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$VERSION_FILE")"
[ -n "$CURRENT_VERSION" ] || die "could not read ripulSDKVersion from $VERSION_FILE"
if [ "$CURRENT_VERSION" != "$VERSION" ]; then
  sed -i '' "s/^let ripulSDKVersion = \".*\"\$/let ripulSDKVersion = \"$VERSION\"/" "$VERSION_FILE"
  git -C "$SRC" add "$VERSION_FILE"
  git -C "$SRC" commit -q -m "chore(sdk): stamp ripulSDKVersion $VERSION"
  echo "▶ Stamped ripulSDKVersion: $CURRENT_VERSION -> $VERSION (committed to the monorepo)"
fi

# Concurrency guard: refuse to mirror a DIRTY monorepo tree. The rsync below copies
# the working tree, so uncommitted edits and untracked files ride into the tag —
# and several agents work in this tree concurrently (v0.4.14 shipped an in-flight
# AgentScreen port to WAC this way). Commit (or set aside) foreign work first, or
# pass ALLOW_DIRTY=1 when you really mean it.
if [ "${ALLOW_DIRTY:-}" != "1" ]; then
  dirty="$(git -C "$SRC" status --porcelain -- Sources Package.swift)"
  [ -z "$dirty" ] || die "monorepo SDK tree is dirty — refusing to scoop uncommitted work into $TAG:
$dirty
(commit it, or override with ALLOW_DIRTY=1)"
fi

# Guardrail: no `import Charts`. A host that already has a module named Charts (WAC links
# the danielgindi Charts pod under that name) shadows Apple's framework at link time, so the
# SDK fails to LINK in that host — v0.7.144 shipped that way and WAC could not take it.
if grep -rnE '^[[:space:]]*import[[:space:]]+Charts([[:space:]]|$)' "$SRC/Sources" 2>/dev/null; then
  die "the SDK imports Charts (see above) — hosts with a Charts pod cannot link it; draw the chart with SwiftUI shapes"
fi

# One-way mirror: make the public tree identical to the monorepo SDK, minus VCS
# and build artifacts. Excluded paths are also protected from --delete on DEST.
rsync -a --delete \
  --exclude '.git/' \
  --exclude '.build/' \
  --exclude '.swiftpm/' \
  --exclude 'scripts/' \
  --exclude 'Package.resolved' \
  --exclude '.DS_Store' \
  "$SRC"/ "$DEST"/

# Guardrail: refuse to publish obvious secrets (high-signal patterns only, so a
# normal release never trips it). Comment lines are ignored. Assignments must
# contain a nonempty string literal: passing an apiKey parameter or checking
# url.password == nil is not an embedded credential.
if grep -rniE \
     "(api[_-]?key|secret|password)[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*[\"'][^\"'[:space:]]|BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY|bearer [a-z0-9]{12}" \
     "$DEST/Sources" "$DEST/Examples" "$DEST/docs" 2>/dev/null \
     | grep -vE '^[^:]+:[0-9]+: *(//|\*|/\*)'; then
  die "possible secret in mirrored tree (see matches above) — aborting before commit"
fi

git -C "$DEST" add -A
if git -C "$DEST" diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo "ℹ️  No content changes since last release; tagging current HEAD."
else
  git -C "$DEST" commit -q -m "Release $TAG — sync from monorepo RipulAgent SDK"
fi
git -C "$DEST" tag -a "$TAG" -m "RipulAgent $TAG"

echo
echo "✅ Staged $TAG locally in $DEST"
git -C "$DEST" --no-pager log --oneline -1
echo

if [ -n "$PUSH" ]; then
  echo "▶ Pushing to $REMOTE_NAME …"
  git -C "$DEST" push "$REMOTE_NAME" HEAD
  git -C "$DEST" push "$REMOTE_NAME" "$TAG"
  echo "🚀 Pushed $TAG"
else
  echo "ℹ️  Not pushed (outward-facing step held back). To publish:"
  echo "     git -C \"$DEST\" push $REMOTE_NAME HEAD && git -C \"$DEST\" push $REMOTE_NAME $TAG"
fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Count fonts and colours written at the call site, and refuse a count that rises.
3	
4	Every font and colour in the first-party apps is moving to a theme token
5	(docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md; what to write instead is in
6	ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md). This check keeps the tree from refilling
7	behind the migration, and its totals are the progress measure.
8	
9	  check_theme_tokens.py                  compare with the baselines (this is what the app build runs)
10	  check_theme_tokens.py --report         the same, with the table of every stream
11	  check_theme_tokens.py --paths A B ...  the counted lines in those files or directories, then the comparison
12	  check_theme_tokens.py --list S1        every counted line in a stream
13	  check_theme_tokens.py --update S1      lower a stream's baseline to today's counts
14	  check_theme_tokens.py --finish S1      mark a stream finished (its counts must be zero)
15	
16	Counted, per line, comments stripped:
17	  font       .font(.body), Font.system(...), UIFont.systemFont(...) and the like
18	  colour     Color.red, .foregroundStyle(.orange), UIColor.systemBackground, Color(red:...), .cgColor of those
19	  hierarchy  .primary/.secondary/.tertiary/.quaternary as a style, Color.primary, Color.secondary
20	  stored     an accessor's result kept in a `static let`: it would never follow a theme change
21	
22	Counted apart, never failing: the system form (`.ripul(system: ...)`), and exempt lines.
23	
24	A bare name (`.orange`, `.secondary`) is counted inside a style call (`foregroundStyle`,
25	`fill`, `tint` and the rest), in an argument whose label names a colour (`tint: .blue`,
26	`colors: [.blue, .purple]`), on a line that says its type is `Color`, and after `return`.
27	A bare text style (`.caption`) is counted anywhere inside a `.font(...)` argument, on a
28	line that says its type is `Font`, and after `return`.
29	It cannot see every one: a bare name passed to an unlabelled parameter is invisible to
30	it, so a count of zero is not proof that a file is clean. Read the diff too.
31	
32	Not counted: `.tint`, `Color.accentColor`, `UIColor.tintColor` (the theme's accent
33	reaches those through the window's tint with no edit), view-level `.fontWeight()`,
34	`.bold()` and `.italic()`, and anything in a branch that compiles only for macOS
35	(`#if os(macOS)`, `#elseif os(macOS)`, the `#else` of `#if os(iOS)`).
36	
37	Exempt: a line marked `// theme-exempt: <reason>` (on the line or the line
38	above), and a file with `// theme-exempt-file: <reason>` in its first 30 lines.
39	
40	A stream owns a set of files by path and has one baseline file,
41	scripts/theme-baseline/<stream>.json, so two agents never edit the same one.
42	The check compares each stream's total per category, so moving code between a
43	stream's files is free. `--update` only ever lowers a number.
44	
45	Warn, then fail. Until a stream is marked finished, a count above its baseline
46	is a warning and the build goes on: other agents build `main` too. Once it is
47	finished its baseline is zero, and any direct font or colour in its files,
48	new files included, fails the build. `stored` fails at once in every stream.
49	"""
50	import json
51	import pathlib
52	import re
53	import sys
54	
55	REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
56	BASELINES = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "theme-baseline"
57	SDK = "ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/"
58	APP = "ripul-native-app/"
59	# Not theme at all: customer content follows the customer's portal theme, and
60	# ThemeCore is where the accessors themselves are written.
61	SKIPPED = (SDK + "CmsRender/", SDK + "ThemeCore/", APP + "iOS/CarPlay/")
62	# Developer tools drawn over a host keep the system look: the theme editor's
63	# screens and the View Explorer overlay.
64	SKIPPED_FILES = re.compile(r"^" + re.escape(SDK) + r"(Theme[A-Za-z]*|Element(Colour|Text)Screens|RipulViewExplorer|ViewInspectorOverlay)\.swift$")
65	# The foundation's own files, which belong to no stream.
66	FOUNDATION = {SDK + name for name in ("GlassModifiers.swift", "GlassButton.swift", "GlassMastheadView.swift",
67	                                      "GlassTopBar.swift", "SheetPresentation.swift")}
68	ROOTS = [SDK, APP + "iOS/", APP + "Shared/", APP + "Browser/"]
69	CATEGORIES = ("font", "colour", "hierarchy", "stored")
70	
71	STYLES = r"largeTitle|title[23]?|headline|subheadline|body|callout|footnote|caption2?"
72	NAMED = r"red|orange|yellow|green|mint|teal|cyan|blue|indigo|purple|pink|brown|gray|white|black"
73	UIKIT = (r"system[A-Z]\w*|label|secondaryLabel|tertiaryLabel|quaternaryLabel|separator|opaqueSeparator|"
74	         r"placeholderText|link|(?:secondary|tertiary)System\w+|quaternarySystemFill|lightGray|darkGray|lightText|darkText|"
75	         + NAMED)
76	STYLE_CALL = re.compile(r"\.(foregroundStyle|foregroundColor|fill|stroke|strokeBorder|background|border|listRowBackground|shadow|tint)\(")
77	# Places outside a style call where a bare `.orange` is a colour: an argument whose label
78	# names a colour, a list of colours, a line that says its type is Color, and `return .green`.
79	COLOUR_LABEL = re.compile(r"\b\w*(?:[tT]int|[cC]olou?rs?|[fF]oreground|[bB]ackground|[fF]ill|[sS]troke|[aA]ccent)\w*\s*:\s*(\[[^\]]*\]|[^,)]*)")
80	COLOUR_TYPED = re.compile(r":\s*\[?Color\b|->\s*Color\b")
81	RETURN_COLOUR = re.compile(r"\breturn\s+\.(?:" + NAMED + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)")
82	# A name that is being compared, or is a font weight, is not a colour: `style == .primary`, `weight: .black`.
83	NOT_A_COLOUR = re.compile(r"(?:==|!=)\s*\.\w+|\bcase\s+\.\w+|\b(?:weight|fontWeight|design)\s*[:(]\s*\.\w+")
84	
85	FONT = [
86	    re.compile(r"\.font\(\s*\.(?:" + STYLES + r"|system|custom)\b"),
87	    re.compile(r"\bFont\.(?:" + STYLES + r"|system|custom)\b"),
88	    re.compile(r"\bUIFont\.(?:systemFont|preferredFont|monospacedSystemFont|monospacedDigitSystemFont|boldSystemFont|italicSystemFont)\b"),
89	    re.compile(r"\bUIFont\(\s*name:"),
90	    # UIKit with the type left out: `label.font = .systemFont(ofSize: 12)`.
91	    re.compile(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.(?:systemFont|preferredFont|monospacedSystemFont|monospacedDigitSystemFont|boldSystemFont|italicSystemFont)\("),
92	]
93	# A bare text style (`.caption`, `.body.weight(.bold)`) where its type is Font: anywhere in a
94	# `.font(...)` argument, on a line that says its type is Font, and after `return`.
95	BARE_STYLE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.)\]])\.(?:" + STYLES + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)")
96	FONT_CALL = re.compile(r"\.font\(")
97	FONT_TYPED = re.compile(r":\s*Font\b|->\s*Font\b")
98	RETURN_STYLE = re.compile(r"\breturn\s+\.(?:" + STYLES + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)")
99	COLOUR = [
100	    re.compile(r"\bColor\.(?:" + NAMED + r")\b"),
101	    re.compile(r"\bUIColor\.(?:" + UIKIT + r")\b"),
102	    re.compile(r"\bColor\(\s*(?:uiColor:\s*)?\.(?:" + UIKIT + r")\b"),
103	    re.compile(r"\b(?:Color|UIColor)\(\s*(?:\.sRGB\s*,\s*|\.displayP3\s*,\s*)?(?:red|white|hue|displayP3Red)\s*:"),
104	    re.compile(r"\bColor\(\s*hex\s*:|#colorLiteral\("),
105	]
106	# UIKit with the type left out: `label.textColor = .secondaryLabel`.
107	COLOUR.append(re.compile(r"\b\w*[cC]olor\s*=\s*\.(?:" + UIKIT + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)"))
108	HIERARCHY = [re.compile(r"\bColor\.(?:primary|secondary)\b")]
109	CANVAS_COLOUR = re.compile(r"\.color\(\s*\.(?:" + NAMED + r")\b")
110	CANVAS_HIERARCHY = re.compile(r"\.color\(\s*\.(?:primary|secondary)\b")
111	STORED = re.compile(r"\bstatic\s+let\b[^=]*=.*\.ripul(?:Icon)?\(")
112	SYSTEM_FORM = re.compile(r"\.ripul\(\s*system\s*:")
113	MAC_ONLY = re.compile(r"^\s*#if\s+os\(macOS\)\s*$")
114	IMPLICIT_COLOUR = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.)\]])\.(?:" + NAMED + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)")
115	IMPLICIT_HIERARCHY = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.)\]])\.(?:primary|secondary|tertiary|quaternary)\b(?!\s*\(|:)")
116	
117	
118	def stream_of(rel: str):
119	    """The plan's stream that owns a file, by path alone."""
120	    if rel in FOUNDATION:
121	        return "F"
122	    if rel.startswith(SDK):
123	        rest = rel[len(SDK):]
124	        if rest.startswith("Sessions/"):
125	            return "S1"
126	        if "/" in rest:
127	            return "S5"
128	        first = rest[0].upper()
129	        return "S2" if first <= "M" else "S3" if first <= "S" else "S4"
130	    if rel.startswith(APP + "iOS/"):
131	        rest = rel[len(APP + "iOS/"):]
132	        first = rest[0].upper()
133	        return "A1" if first <= "L" else "A2" if first <= "R" else "A3"
134	    return "A4"
135	
136	
137	def style_arguments(code: str):
138	    """The text inside each style modifier's parentheses on a line."""
139	    for match in STYLE_CALL.finditer(code):
140	        depth, start = 1, match.end()
141	        for index in range(start, len(code)):
142	            depth += {"(": 1, ")": -1}.get(code[index], 0)
143	            if depth == 0:
144	                yield code[start:index]
145	                break
146	        else:
147	            yield code[start:]
148	
149	
150	ACCESSOR_ARGUMENT = re.compile(r"\.ripul(?:Icon)?\((?:[^()]|\([^()]*\))*\)")
151	
152	
153	def count_line(code: str):
154	    stored = len(STORED.findall(code))
155	    # What is inside an accessor's parentheses is a token name, not a colour: `.ripul(system: .black)`.
156	    code = ACCESSOR_ARGUMENT.sub(".ripul()", code)
157	    # Bare text styles, each counted once. The `.font(.body)` pattern below already counts the
158	    # first name in a `.font(` call, so that position is left to it.
159	    compared = NOT_A_COLOUR.sub("", code)
160	    styles = set()
161	    for match in FONT_CALL.finditer(compared):
162	        depth, start, end = 1, match.end(), len(compared)
163	        for index in range(start, len(compared)):
164	            depth += {"(": 1, ")": -1}.get(compared[index], 0)
165	            if depth == 0:
166	                end = index
167	                break
168	        first = re.match(r"\s*\.(?:" + STYLES + r"|system|custom)\b", compared[start:end])
169	        skip = start + first.end() if first else start
170	        styles.update(skip + m.start() for m in BARE_STYLE.finditer(compared[skip:end]))
171	    if FONT_TYPED.search(compared):
172	        styles.update(m.start() for m in BARE_STYLE.finditer(compared))
173	    styles.update(m.start() + m.group(0).index(".") for m in RETURN_STYLE.finditer(compared))
174	    counts = {
175	        "font": sum(len(p.findall(code)) for p in FONT) + len(styles),
176	        "colour": sum(len(p.findall(code)) for p in COLOUR) + len(CANVAS_COLOUR.findall(code)),
177	        "hierarchy": sum(len(p.findall(code)) for p in HIERARCHY) + len(CANVAS_HIERARCHY.findall(code)),
178	        "stored": stored,
179	    }
180	    code = NOT_A_COLOUR.sub("", code)
181	    # Each implicit name is counted once, wherever on the line it was found to be a colour.
182	    colour, hierarchy = set(), set()
183	
184	    def collect(text, offset):
185	        colour.update(offset + m.start() for m in IMPLICIT_COLOUR.finditer(text))
186	        hierarchy.update(offset + m.start() for m in IMPLICIT_HIERARCHY.finditer(text))
187	
188	    for match in STYLE_CALL.finditer(code):
189	        depth, start = 1, match.end()
190	        end = len(code)
191	        for index in range(start, len(code)):
192	            depth += {"(": 1, ")": -1}.get(code[index], 0)
193	            if depth == 0:
194	                end = index
195	                break
196	        collect(code[start:end], start)
197	    for match in COLOUR_LABEL.finditer(code):
198	        collect(match.group(1), match.start(1))
199	    if COLOUR_TYPED.search(code):
200	        collect(code, 0)
201	    colour.update(m.start() + m.group(0).index(".") for m in RETURN_COLOUR.finditer(code))
202	    counts["colour"] += len(colour)
203	    counts["hierarchy"] += len(hierarchy)
204	    return counts
205	
206	
207	def mac_only_lines(lines):
208	    """Indexes of the lines that compile only for the Mac host.
209	
210	    A branch is macOS-only when its condition is `os(macOS)`, `!os(iOS)` or
211	    `!canImport(UIKit)`, or when it is the `#else` of `#if os(iOS)` /
212	    `#if canImport(UIKit)` (the two platforms are iOS and macOS). Any other
213	    condition (DEBUG, a compound one) is taken to compile for iOS.
214	    """
215	    def kind(condition):
216	        condition = condition.strip()
217	        if condition in ("os(macOS)", "!os(iOS)", "!canImport(UIKit)"):
218	            return "mac"
219	        if condition in ("os(iOS)", "!os(macOS)", "canImport(UIKit)"):
220	            return "ios"
221	        return "other"
222	
223	    skipped, stack = set(), []   # each frame: [kind of the #if, whether the current branch is macOS-only]
224	    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
225	        text = line.split("//", 1)[0].strip()
226	        if text.startswith("#if"):
227	            first = kind(text[3:])
228	            stack.append([first, first == "mac"])
229	        elif text.startswith("#elseif") and stack:
230	            stack[-1][1] = kind(text[7:]) == "mac"
231	        elif text.startswith("#else") and stack:
232	            stack[-1][1] = stack[-1][0] == "ios"
233	        elif text.startswith("#endif") and stack:
234	            stack.pop()
235	        elif any(mac for _, mac in stack):
236	            skipped.add(index)
237	    return skipped
238	
239	
240	def scan():
241	    """rel path -> counts per category, "system", "exempt", and "lines": [(number, text, categories)]"""
242	    files = {}
243	    for root in ROOTS:
244	        for path in sorted((REPO / root).rglob("*.swift")):
245	            rel = path.relative_to(REPO).as_posix()
246	            if rel.startswith(SKIPPED) or SKIPPED_FILES.match(rel):
247	                continue
248	            lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
249	            whole_file = any("theme-exempt-file:" in line for line in lines[:30])
250	            mac_only = mac_only_lines(lines)
251	            entry = {c: 0 for c in CATEGORIES}
252	            entry.update(system=0, exempt=0, lines=[])
253	            for index, line in enumerate(lines):
254	                if index in mac_only:
255	                    continue
256	                code = line.split("//", 1)[0]
257	                entry["system"] += len(SYSTEM_FORM.findall(code))
258	                counts = count_line(code)
259	                total = sum(counts.values())
260	                if not total:
261	                    continue
262	                if whole_file or "theme-exempt:" in line or (index and "theme-exempt:" in lines[index - 1]):
263	                    entry["exempt"] += total
264	                    continue
265	                for category in CATEGORIES:
266	                    entry[category] += counts[category]
267	                entry["lines"].append((index + 1, line.strip(), [c for c in CATEGORIES if counts[c]]))
268	            if entry["lines"] or entry["exempt"] or entry["system"]:
269	                files[rel] = entry
270	    return files
271	
272	
273	def totals(files, stream):
274	    out = {c: 0 for c in CATEGORIES + ("system", "exempt")}
275	    count = 0
276	    for rel, entry in files.items():
277	        if stream_of(rel) != stream:
278	            continue
279	        count += 1
280	        for category in out:
281	            out[category] += entry[category]
282	    return out, count
283	
284	
285	def baseline_path(stream):
286	    return BASELINES / f"{stream}.json"
287	
288	
289	def read_baseline(stream):
290	    path = baseline_path(stream)
291	    base = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {}
292	    return {"finished": bool(base.get("finished")), **{c: int(base.get(c, 0)) for c in CATEGORIES}}
293	
294	
295	def write_baseline(stream, base):
296	    BASELINES.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
297	    baseline_path(stream).write_text(json.dumps(base, indent=2) + "\n")
298	
299	
300	STREAMS = ["F", "S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5", "A1", "A2", "A3", "A4"]
301	ADVICE = ("A font or colour was written at the call site. Use a theme token instead:\n"
302	          "  .font(.caption)                  ->  .font(.ripul(.caption))\n"
303	          "  .foregroundStyle(.secondary)     ->  .foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))\n"
304	          "  Color.red for an error           ->  Color.ripul(.danger)\n"
305	          "The full list is in ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md. To see the lines:\n"
306	          "  python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/check_theme_tokens.py --paths <file or directory>\n"
307	          "A colour that is data, not theme, takes `// theme-exempt: <reason>` on its line.")
308	
309	
310	def main(argv) -> int:
311	    files = scan()
312	    if argv[:1] == ["--list"]:
313	        target = argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else ""
314	        for rel, entry in files.items():
315	            if stream_of(rel) == target:
316	                for number, text, categories in entry["lines"]:
317	                    print(f"{rel}:{number}: [{','.join(categories)}] {text}")
318	        return 0
319	    if argv[:1] == ["--paths"]:
320	        wanted = [str(pathlib.Path(p).resolve().relative_to(REPO)) for p in argv[1:]]
321	        for rel, entry in files.items():
322	            if any(rel == w or rel.startswith(w.rstrip("/") + "/") for w in wanted):
323	                for number, text, categories in entry["lines"]:
324	                    print(f"{rel}:{number}: [{','.join(categories)}] {text}")
325	        print()
326	    if argv[:1] in (["--update"], ["--finish"]):
327	        for stream in argv[1:] or (STREAMS if argv[0] == "--update" else []):
328	            if stream not in STREAMS:
329	                print(f"No such stream: {stream}. Streams: {' '.join(STREAMS)}")
330	                return 2
331	            now, _ = totals(files, stream)
332	            exists = baseline_path(stream).exists()
333	            old = read_baseline(stream)
334	            new = {"finished": old["finished"], **{c: min(now[c], old[c]) if exists else now[c] for c in CATEGORIES}}
335	            new["stored"] = 0
336	            if argv[0] == "--finish":
337	                left = sum(now[c] for c in CATEGORIES)
338	                if left:
339	                    print(f"{stream} cannot be finished: {left} direct fonts and colours are left in its files, "
340	                          f"other agents' additions included. See --list {stream}.")
341	                    return 1
342	                new["finished"] = True
343	            write_baseline(stream, new)
344	            print(f"{stream}: baseline is now {new}")
345	        return 0
346	
347	    report = "--report" in argv or argv[:1] == ["--paths"]
348	    failed, warned = [], []
349	    grand = {c: 0 for c in CATEGORIES + ("system", "exempt")}
350	    rows = []
351	    for stream in STREAMS:
352	        now, count = totals(files, stream)
353	        base = read_baseline(stream)
354	        for category in CATEGORIES:
355	            grand[category] += now[category]
356	            if now[category] > base[category]:
357	                strict = base["finished"] or category == "stored"
358	                (failed if strict else warned).append((stream, category, base[category], now[category]))
359	        grand["system"] += now["system"]
360	        grand["exempt"] += now["exempt"]
361	        rows.append((stream, count, now, base))
362	    if report or failed or warned:
363	        print(f"{'stream':7}{'files':>6}{'font':>7}{'colour':>8}{'hierarchy':>11}{'total':>7}{'baseline':>10}"
364	              f"{'system':>8}{'exempt':>8}  state")
365	        for stream, count, now, base in rows:
366	            total = sum(now[c] for c in CATEGORIES)
367	            print(f"{stream:7}{count:>6}{now['font']:>7}{now['colour']:>8}{now['hierarchy']:>11}{total:>7}"
368	                  f"{sum(base[c] for c in CATEGORIES):>10}{now['system']:>8}{now['exempt']:>8}"
369	                  f"  {'finished' if base['finished'] else 'migrating'}")
370	        total = sum(grand[c] for c in CATEGORIES)
371	        print(f"{'all':7}{sum(r[1] for r in rows):>6}{grand['font']:>7}{grand['colour']:>8}{grand['hierarchy']:>11}{total:>7}"
372	              f"{'':>10}{grand['system']:>8}{grand['exempt']:>8}")
373	    for stream, category, base, now in warned:
374	        # Xcode shows a line that starts "warning:" in the build log without stopping the build.
375	        print(f"warning: check_theme_tokens: stream {stream} has {now} direct {category} uses, above its baseline of {base}. "
376	              f"Use the theme accessors (ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md); this will fail the build once {stream} is finished.")
377	    if failed:
378	        print()
379	        for stream, category, base, now in failed:
380	            what = "an accessor's result kept in a static let" if category == "stored" else f"direct {category} uses"
381	            print(f"error: check_theme_tokens: stream {stream} has {now} {what}, above its baseline of {base}.")
382	        print(ADVICE)
383	        return 1
384	    print(f"check_theme_tokens: {sum(grand[c] for c in CATEGORIES)} direct fonts and colours left "
385	          f"({grand['font']} font, {grand['colour']} colour, {grand['hierarchy']} hierarchy), none above a finished stream's baseline")
386	    return 0
387	
388	
389	if __name__ == "__main__":
390	    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
391
