#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Count fonts and colours written at the call site, and refuse a count that rises.

Every font and colour in the first-party apps is moving to a theme token
(docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md; what to write instead is in
ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md). This check keeps the tree from refilling
behind the migration, and its totals are the progress measure.

  check_theme_tokens.py                  compare with the baselines (this is what the app build runs)
  check_theme_tokens.py --report         the same, with the table of every stream
  check_theme_tokens.py --paths A B ...  the counted lines in those files or directories, then the comparison
  check_theme_tokens.py --list S1        every counted line in a stream
  check_theme_tokens.py --update S1      lower a stream's baseline to today's counts
  check_theme_tokens.py --finish S1      mark a stream finished (its counts must be zero)

Counted, per line, comments stripped:
  font       .font(.body), Font.system(...), UIFont.systemFont(...) and the like
  colour     Color.red, .foregroundStyle(.orange), UIColor.systemBackground, Color(red:...), .cgColor of those
  hierarchy  .primary/.secondary/.tertiary/.quaternary as a style, Color.primary, Color.secondary
  stored     an accessor's result kept in a `static let`: it would never follow a theme change

Counted apart, never failing: the system form (`.ripul(system: ...)`), and exempt lines.

A bare name (`.orange`, `.secondary`) is counted inside a style call (`foregroundStyle`,
`fill`, `tint` and the rest), in an argument whose label names a colour (`tint: .blue`,
`colors: [.blue, .purple]`), on a line that says its type is `Color`, and after `return`.
A bare text style (`.caption`) is counted anywhere inside a `.font(...)` argument, on a
line that says its type is `Font`, and after `return`.
It cannot see every one: a bare name passed to an unlabelled parameter is invisible to
it, so a count of zero is not proof that a file is clean. Read the diff too.

Not counted: `.tint`, `Color.accentColor`, `UIColor.tintColor` (the theme's accent
reaches those through the window's tint with no edit), view-level `.fontWeight()`,
`.bold()` and `.italic()`, and anything in a branch that compiles only for macOS
(`#if os(macOS)`, `#elseif os(macOS)`, the `#else` of `#if os(iOS)`).

Exempt: a line marked `// theme-exempt: <reason>` (on the line or the line
above), and a file with `// theme-exempt-file: <reason>` in its first 30 lines.

A stream owns a set of files by path and has one baseline file,
scripts/theme-baseline/<stream>.json, so two agents never edit the same one.
The check compares each stream's total per category, so moving code between a
stream's files is free. `--update` only ever lowers a number.

Warn, then fail. Until a stream is marked finished, a count above its baseline
is a warning and the build goes on: other agents build `main` too. Once it is
finished its baseline is zero, and any direct font or colour in its files,
new files included, fails the build. `stored` fails at once in every stream.
"""
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys

REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
BASELINES = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "theme-baseline"
SDK = "ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/"
APP = "ripul-native-app/"
# Not theme at all: customer content follows the customer's portal theme, and
# ThemeCore is where the accessors themselves are written.
SKIPPED = (SDK + "CmsRender/", SDK + "ThemeCore/", APP + "iOS/CarPlay/")
# Developer tools drawn over a host keep the system look: the theme editor's
# screens and the View Explorer overlay.
SKIPPED_FILES = re.compile(r"^" + re.escape(SDK) + r"(Theme[A-Za-z]*|Element(Colour|Text)Screens|RipulViewExplorer|ViewInspectorOverlay)\.swift$")
# The foundation's own files, which belong to no stream.
FOUNDATION = {SDK + name for name in ("GlassModifiers.swift", "GlassButton.swift", "GlassMastheadView.swift",
                                      "GlassTopBar.swift", "SheetPresentation.swift")}
ROOTS = [SDK, APP + "iOS/", APP + "Shared/", APP + "Browser/"]
CATEGORIES = ("font", "colour", "hierarchy", "stored")

STYLES = r"largeTitle|title[23]?|headline|subheadline|body|callout|footnote|caption2?"
NAMED = r"red|orange|yellow|green|mint|teal|cyan|blue|indigo|purple|pink|brown|gray|white|black"
UIKIT = (r"system[A-Z]\w*|label|secondaryLabel|tertiaryLabel|quaternaryLabel|separator|opaqueSeparator|"
         r"placeholderText|link|(?:secondary|tertiary)System\w+|quaternarySystemFill|lightGray|darkGray|lightText|darkText|"
         + NAMED)
STYLE_CALL = re.compile(r"\.(foregroundStyle|foregroundColor|fill|stroke|strokeBorder|background|border|listRowBackground|shadow|tint)\(")
# Places outside a style call where a bare `.orange` is a colour: an argument whose label
# names a colour, a list of colours, a line that says its type is Color, and `return .green`.
COLOUR_LABEL = re.compile(r"\b\w*(?:[tT]int|[cC]olou?rs?|[fF]oreground|[bB]ackground|[fF]ill|[sS]troke|[aA]ccent)\w*\s*:\s*(\[[^\]]*\]|[^,)]*)")
COLOUR_TYPED = re.compile(r":\s*\[?Color\b|->\s*Color\b")
RETURN_COLOUR = re.compile(r"\breturn\s+\.(?:" + NAMED + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)")
# A name that is being compared, or is a font weight, is not a colour: `style == .primary`, `weight: .black`.
NOT_A_COLOUR = re.compile(r"(?:==|!=)\s*\.\w+|\bcase\s+\.\w+|\b(?:weight|fontWeight|design)\s*[:(]\s*\.\w+")

FONT = [
    re.compile(r"\.font\(\s*\.(?:" + STYLES + r"|system|custom)\b"),
    re.compile(r"\bFont\.(?:" + STYLES + r"|system|custom)\b"),
    re.compile(r"\bUIFont\.(?:systemFont|preferredFont|monospacedSystemFont|monospacedDigitSystemFont|boldSystemFont|italicSystemFont)\b"),
    re.compile(r"\bUIFont\(\s*name:"),
    # UIKit with the type left out: `label.font = .systemFont(ofSize: 12)`.
    re.compile(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.(?:systemFont|preferredFont|monospacedSystemFont|monospacedDigitSystemFont|boldSystemFont|italicSystemFont)\("),
]
# A bare text style (`.caption`, `.body.weight(.bold)`) where its type is Font: anywhere in a
# `.font(...)` argument, on a line that says its type is Font, and after `return`.
BARE_STYLE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.)\]])\.(?:" + STYLES + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)")
FONT_CALL = re.compile(r"\.font\(")
FONT_TYPED = re.compile(r":\s*Font\b|->\s*Font\b")
RETURN_STYLE = re.compile(r"\breturn\s+\.(?:" + STYLES + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)")
COLOUR = [
    re.compile(r"\bColor\.(?:" + NAMED + r")\b"),
    re.compile(r"\bUIColor\.(?:" + UIKIT + r")\b"),
    re.compile(r"\bColor\(\s*(?:uiColor:\s*)?\.(?:" + UIKIT + r")\b"),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:Color|UIColor)\(\s*(?:\.sRGB\s*,\s*|\.displayP3\s*,\s*)?(?:red|white|hue|displayP3Red)\s*:"),
    re.compile(r"\bColor\(\s*hex\s*:|#colorLiteral\("),
]
# UIKit with the type left out: `label.textColor = .secondaryLabel`.
COLOUR.append(re.compile(r"\b\w*[cC]olor\s*=\s*\.(?:" + UIKIT + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)"))
HIERARCHY = [re.compile(r"\bColor\.(?:primary|secondary)\b")]
CANVAS_COLOUR = re.compile(r"\.color\(\s*\.(?:" + NAMED + r")\b")
CANVAS_HIERARCHY = re.compile(r"\.color\(\s*\.(?:primary|secondary)\b")
STORED = re.compile(r"\bstatic\s+let\b[^=]*=.*\.ripul(?:Icon)?\(")
SYSTEM_FORM = re.compile(r"\.ripul\(\s*system\s*:")
MAC_ONLY = re.compile(r"^\s*#if\s+os\(macOS\)\s*$")
IMPLICIT_COLOUR = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.)\]])\.(?:" + NAMED + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)")
IMPLICIT_HIERARCHY = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.)\]])\.(?:primary|secondary|tertiary|quaternary)\b(?!\s*\(|:)")


def stream_of(rel: str):
    """The plan's stream that owns a file, by path alone."""
    if rel in FOUNDATION:
        return "F"
    if rel.startswith(SDK):
        rest = rel[len(SDK):]
        if rest.startswith("Sessions/"):
            return "S1"
        if "/" in rest:
            return "S5"
        first = rest[0].upper()
        return "S2" if first <= "M" else "S3" if first <= "S" else "S4"
    if rel.startswith(APP + "iOS/"):
        rest = rel[len(APP + "iOS/"):]
        first = rest[0].upper()
        return "A1" if first <= "L" else "A2" if first <= "R" else "A3"
    return "A4"


def style_arguments(code: str):
    """The text inside each style modifier's parentheses on a line."""
    for match in STYLE_CALL.finditer(code):
        depth, start = 1, match.end()
        for index in range(start, len(code)):
            depth += {"(": 1, ")": -1}.get(code[index], 0)
            if depth == 0:
                yield code[start:index]
                break
        else:
            yield code[start:]


ACCESSOR_ARGUMENT = re.compile(r"\.ripul(?:Icon)?\((?:[^()]|\([^()]*\))*\)")


def count_line(code: str):
    stored = len(STORED.findall(code))
    # What is inside an accessor's parentheses is a token name, not a colour: `.ripul(system: .black)`.
    code = ACCESSOR_ARGUMENT.sub(".ripul()", code)
    # Bare text styles, each counted once. The `.font(.body)` pattern below already counts the
    # first name in a `.font(` call, so that position is left to it.
    compared = NOT_A_COLOUR.sub("", code)
    styles = set()
    for match in FONT_CALL.finditer(compared):
        depth, start, end = 1, match.end(), len(compared)
        for index in range(start, len(compared)):
            depth += {"(": 1, ")": -1}.get(compared[index], 0)
            if depth == 0:
                end = index
                break
        first = re.match(r"\s*\.(?:" + STYLES + r"|system|custom)\b", compared[start:end])
        skip = start + first.end() if first else start
        styles.update(skip + m.start() for m in BARE_STYLE.finditer(compared[skip:end]))
    if FONT_TYPED.search(compared):
        styles.update(m.start() for m in BARE_STYLE.finditer(compared))
    styles.update(m.start() + m.group(0).index(".") for m in RETURN_STYLE.finditer(compared))
    counts = {
        "font": sum(len(p.findall(code)) for p in FONT) + len(styles),
        "colour": sum(len(p.findall(code)) for p in COLOUR) + len(CANVAS_COLOUR.findall(code)),
        "hierarchy": sum(len(p.findall(code)) for p in HIERARCHY) + len(CANVAS_HIERARCHY.findall(code)),
        "stored": stored,
    }
    code = NOT_A_COLOUR.sub("", code)
    # Each implicit name is counted once, wherever on the line it was found to be a colour.
    colour, hierarchy = set(), set()

    def collect(text, offset):
        colour.update(offset + m.start() for m in IMPLICIT_COLOUR.finditer(text))
        hierarchy.update(offset + m.start() for m in IMPLICIT_HIERARCHY.finditer(text))

    for match in STYLE_CALL.finditer(code):
        depth, start = 1, match.end()
        end = len(code)
        for index in range(start, len(code)):
            depth += {"(": 1, ")": -1}.get(code[index], 0)
            if depth == 0:
                end = index
                break
        collect(code[start:end], start)
    for match in COLOUR_LABEL.finditer(code):
        collect(match.group(1), match.start(1))
    if COLOUR_TYPED.search(code):
        collect(code, 0)
    colour.update(m.start() + m.group(0).index(".") for m in RETURN_COLOUR.finditer(code))
    counts["colour"] += len(colour)
    counts["hierarchy"] += len(hierarchy)
    return counts


def mac_only_lines(lines):
    """Indexes of the lines that compile only for the Mac host.

    A branch is macOS-only when its condition is `os(macOS)`, `!os(iOS)` or
    `!canImport(UIKit)`, or when it is the `#else` of `#if os(iOS)` /
    `#if canImport(UIKit)` (the two platforms are iOS and macOS). Any other
    condition (DEBUG, a compound one) is taken to compile for iOS.
    """
    def kind(condition):
        condition = condition.strip()
        if condition in ("os(macOS)", "!os(iOS)", "!canImport(UIKit)"):
            return "mac"
        if condition in ("os(iOS)", "!os(macOS)", "canImport(UIKit)"):
            return "ios"
        return "other"

    skipped, stack = set(), []   # each frame: [kind of the #if, whether the current branch is macOS-only]
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        text = line.split("//", 1)[0].strip()
        if text.startswith("#if"):
            first = kind(text[3:])
            stack.append([first, first == "mac"])
        elif text.startswith("#elseif") and stack:
            stack[-1][1] = kind(text[7:]) == "mac"
        elif text.startswith("#else") and stack:
            stack[-1][1] = stack[-1][0] == "ios"
        elif text.startswith("#endif") and stack:
            stack.pop()
        elif any(mac for _, mac in stack):
            skipped.add(index)
    return skipped


def scan():
    """rel path -> counts per category, "system", "exempt", and "lines": [(number, text, categories)]"""
    files = {}
    for root in ROOTS:
        for path in sorted((REPO / root).rglob("*.swift")):
            rel = path.relative_to(REPO).as_posix()
            if rel.startswith(SKIPPED) or SKIPPED_FILES.match(rel):
                continue
            lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
            whole_file = any("theme-exempt-file:" in line for line in lines[:30])
            mac_only = mac_only_lines(lines)
            entry = {c: 0 for c in CATEGORIES}
            entry.update(system=0, exempt=0, lines=[])
            for index, line in enumerate(lines):
                if index in mac_only:
                    continue
                code = line.split("//", 1)[0]
                entry["system"] += len(SYSTEM_FORM.findall(code))
                counts = count_line(code)
                total = sum(counts.values())
                if not total:
                    continue
                if whole_file or "theme-exempt:" in line or (index and "theme-exempt:" in lines[index - 1]):
                    entry["exempt"] += total
                    continue
                for category in CATEGORIES:
                    entry[category] += counts[category]
                entry["lines"].append((index + 1, line.strip(), [c for c in CATEGORIES if counts[c]]))
            if entry["lines"] or entry["exempt"] or entry["system"]:
                files[rel] = entry
    return files


def totals(files, stream):
    out = {c: 0 for c in CATEGORIES + ("system", "exempt")}
    count = 0
    for rel, entry in files.items():
        if stream_of(rel) != stream:
            continue
        count += 1
        for category in out:
            out[category] += entry[category]
    return out, count


def baseline_path(stream):
    return BASELINES / f"{stream}.json"


def read_baseline(stream):
    path = baseline_path(stream)
    base = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {}
    return {"finished": bool(base.get("finished")), **{c: int(base.get(c, 0)) for c in CATEGORIES}}


def write_baseline(stream, base):
    BASELINES.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    baseline_path(stream).write_text(json.dumps(base, indent=2) + "\n")


STREAMS = ["F", "S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5", "A1", "A2", "A3", "A4"]
ADVICE = ("A font or colour was written at the call site. Use a theme token instead:\n"
          "  .font(.caption)                  ->  .font(.ripul(.caption))\n"
          "  .foregroundStyle(.secondary)     ->  .foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))\n"
          "  Color.red for an error           ->  Color.ripul(.danger)\n"
          "The full list is in ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md. To see the lines:\n"
          "  python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/check_theme_tokens.py --paths <file or directory>\n"
          "A colour that is data, not theme, takes `// theme-exempt: <reason>` on its line.")


def main(argv) -> int:
    files = scan()
    if argv[:1] == ["--list"]:
        target = argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else ""
        for rel, entry in files.items():
            if stream_of(rel) == target:
                for number, text, categories in entry["lines"]:
                    print(f"{rel}:{number}: [{','.join(categories)}] {text}")
        return 0
    if argv[:1] == ["--paths"]:
        wanted = [str(pathlib.Path(p).resolve().relative_to(REPO)) for p in argv[1:]]
        for rel, entry in files.items():
            if any(rel == w or rel.startswith(w.rstrip("/") + "/") for w in wanted):
                for number, text, categories in entry["lines"]:
                    print(f"{rel}:{number}: [{','.join(categories)}] {text}")
        print()
    if argv[:1] in (["--update"], ["--finish"]):
        for stream in argv[1:] or (STREAMS if argv[0] == "--update" else []):
            if stream not in STREAMS:
                print(f"No such stream: {stream}. Streams: {' '.join(STREAMS)}")
                return 2
            now, _ = totals(files, stream)
            exists = baseline_path(stream).exists()
            old = read_baseline(stream)
            new = {"finished": old["finished"], **{c: min(now[c], old[c]) if exists else now[c] for c in CATEGORIES}}
            new["stored"] = 0
            if argv[0] == "--finish":
                left = sum(now[c] for c in CATEGORIES)
                if left:
                    print(f"{stream} cannot be finished: {left} direct fonts and colours are left in its files, "
                          f"other agents' additions included. See --list {stream}.")
                    return 1
                new["finished"] = True
            write_baseline(stream, new)
            print(f"{stream}: baseline is now {new}")
        return 0

    report = "--report" in argv or argv[:1] == ["--paths"]
    failed, warned = [], []
    grand = {c: 0 for c in CATEGORIES + ("system", "exempt")}
    rows = []
    for stream in STREAMS:
        now, count = totals(files, stream)
        base = read_baseline(stream)
        for category in CATEGORIES:
            grand[category] += now[category]
            if now[category] > base[category]:
                strict = base["finished"] or category == "stored"
                (failed if strict else warned).append((stream, category, base[category], now[category]))
        grand["system"] += now["system"]
        grand["exempt"] += now["exempt"]
        rows.append((stream, count, now, base))
    if report or failed or warned:
        print(f"{'stream':7}{'files':>6}{'font':>7}{'colour':>8}{'hierarchy':>11}{'total':>7}{'baseline':>10}"
              f"{'system':>8}{'exempt':>8}  state")
        for stream, count, now, base in rows:
            total = sum(now[c] for c in CATEGORIES)
            print(f"{stream:7}{count:>6}{now['font']:>7}{now['colour']:>8}{now['hierarchy']:>11}{total:>7}"
                  f"{sum(base[c] for c in CATEGORIES):>10}{now['system']:>8}{now['exempt']:>8}"
                  f"  {'finished' if base['finished'] else 'migrating'}")
        total = sum(grand[c] for c in CATEGORIES)
        print(f"{'all':7}{sum(r[1] for r in rows):>6}{grand['font']:>7}{grand['colour']:>8}{grand['hierarchy']:>11}{total:>7}"
              f"{'':>10}{grand['system']:>8}{grand['exempt']:>8}")
    for stream, category, base, now in warned:
        # Xcode shows a line that starts "warning:" in the build log without stopping the build.
        print(f"warning: check_theme_tokens: stream {stream} has {now} direct {category} uses, above its baseline of {base}. "
              f"Use the theme accessors (ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md); this will fail the build once {stream} is finished.")
    if failed:
        print()
        for stream, category, base, now in failed:
            what = "an accessor's result kept in a static let" if category == "stored" else f"direct {category} uses"
            print(f"error: check_theme_tokens: stream {stream} has {now} {what}, above its baseline of {base}.")
        print(ADVICE)
        return 1
    print(f"check_theme_tokens: {sum(grand[c] for c in CATEGORIES)} direct fonts and colours left "
          f"({grand['font']} font, {grand['colour']} colour, {grand['hierarchy']} hierarchy), none above a finished stream's baseline")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

106	# A text-style font already written as a role, with at most a weight: `.font(.ripul(.caption))`.

111	def on_an_image(lines, index, column):
112	    """True when the modifier at lines[index][column] hangs from an `Image(...)`."""
113	    views = VIEW_NAMED.findall(base_of_chain(lines, index, column))
114	    # Only an Image, and nothing that draws text beside it: a font on `Label` or on a

116	    return bool(views) and all(view == "Image" for view in views)

119	def icon_fonts(lines, index, code):
120	    """A font on a symbol is an icon size, never type: `.ripul(.caption)` there is `.ripulIcon(.caption)`."""
121	    return ROLE_FONT.sub(lambda m: f".font(.ripulIcon({m.group(1)})" if on_an_image(lines, index, m.start()) else m.group(0), code)

124	def rewrite(text, icons_only=False):
125	    lines = text.split("\n")

128	    from check_theme_tokens import mac_only_lines
129	    mac_only = mac_only_lines(lines)
130	    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
131	        if index in mac_only:
132	            continue
133	        if "theme-exempt:" in line or (index and "theme-exempt:" in lines[index - 1]):
134	            continue
135	        code, slashes, comment = line.partition("//")
136	        original = code
137	        if icons_only:
138	            code = icon_fonts(lines, index, code)
139	            if code != original:
140	                lines[index] = code + slashes + comment
141	                changed += 1
142	            continue
143	        code = SYSTEM_STYLE_FONT.sub(system_style_font, code)
144	        code = STYLE_FONT.sub(style_font, code)

147	        def fixed_font(match, index=index):
148	            size, weight, design, chain = match.group(1).strip(), match.group(2), match.group(3), match.group(4)
149	            base = base_of_chain(lines, index, match.start())
150	            # The last view named before the modifier decides: `Image(...)` or `Text(...)`.
151	            views = re.findall(r"\b(Image|Text|Label|TextField|TextEditor|SecureField)\(", base)
152	            kind = views[-1] if views else None
153	            if design == "monospaced":
154	                kind = "Text" if kind in (None, "Text", "TextField", "TextEditor", "SecureField") else kind
155	            if kind == "Image" and design != "monospaced":
156	                name, family = "ripulIcon", ""
157	            elif kind in ("Text", "TextField", "TextEditor", "SecureField"):
158	                name, family = "ripul", ", family: .code" if design == "monospaced" else ""
159	            else:
160	                return match.group(0)
161	            weight_part = f", weight: {weight.strip()}" if weight else ""
162	            return f".font(.{name}(size: {size}{weight_part}{family}){chain})"

164	        code = FIXED_FONT.sub(fixed_font, code)
165	        code = HIERARCHY_TERNARY.sub(
166	            lambda m: f".{m.group(1)}({m.group(2)}? .ripul(.{HIERARCHY[m.group(3)]}) : .ripul(.{HIERARCHY[m.group(4)]})", code)
167	        code = HIERARCHY_ARG.sub(lambda m: f".{m.group(1)}(.ripul(.{HIERARCHY[m.group(2)]})", code)

177	# Both sides of a changed line are reduced to a skeleton in which every literal and
178	# every accessor is replaced by a name for the VALUE IT DRAWS BY DEFAULT. If the two
179	# skeletons are equal, each replacement kept its value, so nothing changed on screen.
180	
181	NAMED_ROLE = {"red": "danger", "orange": "warning", "green": "success", "blue": "info", "gray": "neutral", "white": "onAccent"}
182	HUES = "red|orange|yellow|green|mint|teal|cyan|blue|indigo|purple|pink|brown|gray|white|black"
183	# A system colour that is also a role's default, in both toolkits.
184	SYSTEM_ROLE = {"systemBackground": "canvas", "secondarySystemGroupedBackground": "surface",
185	               "systemGroupedBackground": "surfaceSunken", "separator": "separator", "systemGreen": "success",
186	               "systemOrange": "warning", "systemRed": "danger", "systemBlue": "info", "systemGray": "neutral",
187	               "white": "onAccent"}
188	# UIKit's label colours are the text roles' defaults there. In SwiftUI they are NOT:
189	# `Color(.secondaryLabel)` is a fixed colour, `.secondary` is the hierarchical style.
190	UIKIT_TEXT = {"label": "text", "secondaryLabel": "textSecondary", "tertiaryLabel": "textTertiary",
191	              "quaternaryLabel": "textQuaternary", "tintColor": "accent"}
192	SYSTEM_NAMES = (r"system[A-Z]\w*|label|secondaryLabel|tertiaryLabel|quaternaryLabel|separator|opaqueSeparator|"
193	                r"placeholderText|link|(?:secondary|tertiary)System\w+|quaternarySystemFill|tintColor|white|black")
194	UIFONT_STYLE = {"largeTitle": "largeTitle", "title1": "title", "title2": "title2", "title3": "title3", "headline": "headline",

196	                "caption1": "caption", "caption2": "caption2"}

199	def role(name):
200	    return f"\u00a7{name}\u00a7"

202	
203	def system(name):
204	    return role(SYSTEM_ROLE[name]) if name in SYSTEM_ROLE else f"\u00a7sys:{name}\u00a7"
205	
206	
207	def hue(name):
208	    return role(NAMED_ROLE[name]) if name in NAMED_ROLE else system("black" if name == "black" else "system" + name.capitalize())

211	BARE_HIERARCHY = re.compile(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.(primary|secondary|tertiary|quaternary)\b(?!\s*\(|:)")
212	# Evidence of a Color beside a bare name: the word, or a colour's symbol. Not the accent's
213	# (`.tint` is a style) and not another hierarchy name.
214	# `tint ?? .primary` counts too: `??` makes both sides one type, and the optional beside a
215	# colour name in a style call is in practice a `Color?`.
216	COLOUR_BESIDE = re.compile(r"\?\?|\bColor\b|\u00a7(?!accent\u00a7|\??text)|(?<![\w)\]])\.(?:" + HUES + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)")

221	def bare_hierarchy(code):
222	    if TYPED_COLOR.search(code):
223	        return BARE_HIERARCHY.sub(lambda m: role("C:" + HIERARCHY[m.group(1)]), code)
224	    spans = []
225	    for match in STYLE_OPEN.finditer(code):
226	        depth, start, end = 1, match.end(), len(code)
227	        for index in range(start, len(code)):
228	            depth += {"(": 1, ")": -1}.get(code[index], 0)
229	            if depth == 0:
230	                end = index
231	                break
232	        spans.append((start, end))
233	    out, last = [], 0
234	    for match in BARE_HIERARCHY.finditer(code):
235	        name = HIERARCHY[match.group(1)]
236	        inside = next(((a, b) for a, b in spans if a <= match.start() < b), None)
237	        if inside is None:
238	            symbol = role("?" + name)
239	        else:
240	            rest = code[inside[0]:match.start()] + code[match.end():inside[1]]
241	            rest = BARE_HIERARCHY.sub("", rest)
242	            is_color = COLOUR_BESIDE.search(rest) and "AnyShapeStyle(" not in rest
243	            # The other branch of a ternary is a name (`selected ? color : .secondary`): only the
244	            # compiler knows whether `color` is a Color, so either form is taken.
245	            beside_a_name = re.search(r"\?\s*[A-Za-z_]|\s:\s*[A-Za-z_]", rest) and "AnyShapeStyle(" not in rest
246	            symbol = role(("C:" if is_color else "?" if beside_a_name else "") + name)
247	        out.append(code[last:match.start()] + symbol)
248	        last = match.end()
249	    return "".join(out) + code[last:]

252	def same_value(before, after):
253	    """Equal skeletons, where an open `?name` on the old side takes either form on the new."""
254	    if before == after:
255	        return True
256	    pattern = re.escape(before)
257	    pattern = re.sub("\u00a7\\\\\\?(\\w+)\u00a7", lambda m: "\u00a7(?:C:|\\?)?" + m.group(1) + "\u00a7", pattern)

261	# The control modifiers of "Controls that style their own text" (docs/theming.md). With no
262	# theme each is the system's own style, or nothing at all, so the lint reads them that way.
263	CONTROL_IDENTITIES = [
264	    (re.compile(r"\.ripulProminentButtonStyle\(\)"), ".buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)"),
265	    (re.compile(r"\.ripulGlassProminentButtonStyle\(\)"), ".buttonStyle(.glassProminent)"),
266	    (re.compile(r"\.ripul(?:EmptyStateTitle|EmptyStateDescription|SectionHeader|SectionFooter)\(\)"), ""),
267	    # The accent once a theme names one; with no theme, the role it replaced.
268	    (re.compile(r"\.ripul\(\s*accentOr:\s*\.(\w+)\s*\)"), r".ripul(.\1)"),
269	    # Not a token: the notification's name.
270	    (re.compile(r"\.ripulThemeDidChange\b"), ".themeDidChange"),
271	]
272	
273	
274	def control_identities(code):
275	    for pattern, replacement in CONTROL_IDENTITIES:
276	        code = pattern.sub(replacement, code)
277	    return code
278	
279	
280	def skeleton(code):
281	    code = control_identities(code)
282	    if TYPED_COLOR.search(code):
283	        # On a line whose type is Color, a bare `.ripul(.textSecondary)` is the Color form.
284	        code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.ripul\(\s*\.(text\w*)\s*\)", lambda m: role("C:" + m.group(1)), code)

286	    code = re.sub(r"\.system\(\s*([^,()]*\?\s*\.(?:" + STYLES + r")\s*:\s*\.(?:" + STYLES + r"))\s*,\s*design:\s*\.monospaced\s*\)",
287	                  lambda m: f".ripul({m.group(1).strip()}, family: .code)", code)

293	    code = SYSTEM_STYLE_FONT.sub(system_style_font, code)
294	    code = STYLE_FONT.sub(style_font, code)
295	    code = FIXED_FONT.sub(lambda m: ".font(.ripul(size: %s%s%s)%s)" % (

297	        ", family: .code" if m.group(3) == "monospaced" else "", m.group(4)), code)
298	    # The same forms with no type written before them (`v.font = .preferredFont(...)`, a
299	    # property typed Font, a branch of a ternary inside `.font(`).
300	    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.system\(\s*\.(" + STYLES + r")\s*,\s*design:\s*\.monospaced\s*\)", r".ripul(.\1, family: .code)", code)

302	    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.preferredFont\(\s*forTextStyle:\s*\.(\w+)\s*\)",
303	                  lambda m: f".ripul(.{UIFONT_STYLE.get(m.group(1), m.group(1))})", code)
304	    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.monospacedSystemFont\(\s*ofSize:\s*([^,()]+)(,\s*weight:\s*[^,()]+)?\)",
305	                  lambda m: f".ripul(size: {m.group(1).strip()}{m.group(2) or ''}, family: .code)", code)
306	    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.systemFont\(\s*ofSize:", ".ripul(size:", code)
307	    code = re.sub(r"\bFont\.(" + STYLES + r")\b", r"Font.ripul(.\1)", code)
308	    # A bare text style wherever it stands (`return .headline`, `flag ? .caption2 : .caption`,
309	    # a property typed Font) is the same replacement as inside `.font(`. A name that is not a
310	    # font (an enum's `.body`) is changed on both sides alike, so it still compares equal.
311	    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w.)\]])(?<!ripul\()(?<!Icon\()(?<!To: )(?<!Style: )\.(" + STYLES + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)", r".ripul(.\1)", code)
312	    # `.ripul(.body).weight(w)` and `.ripul(.body, weight: w)` are one value, whatever `w` is.
313	    code = re.sub(r"\.ripul\(\s*\.(" + STYLES + r")\s*\)\.weight\(((?:[^()]|\([^()]*\))*)\)",
314	                  lambda m: f".ripul(.{m.group(1)}, weight: {m.group(2).strip()})", code)
315	    code = re.sub(r"\bFont\.system\(\s*size:", "Font.ripul(size:", code)
316	    code = re.sub(r"\bUIFont\.preferredFont\(\s*forTextStyle:\s*\.(\w+)\s*\)",
317	                  lambda m: f"UIFont.ripul(.{UIFONT_STYLE.get(m.group(1), m.group(1))})", code)
318	    code = re.sub(r"\bUIFont\.monospacedSystemFont\(\s*ofSize:\s*([^,()]+)(,\s*weight:\s*[^,()]+)?\)",
319	                  lambda m: f"UIFont.ripul(size: {m.group(1).strip()}{m.group(2) or ''}, family: .code)", code)
320	    code = re.sub(r"\bUIFont\.systemFont\(\s*ofSize:", "UIFont.ripul(size:", code)

323	    code = re.sub(r"\b(?:UIFont|Font)\.ripul\(", ".ripul(", code)

325	    code = re.sub(r"\.font\(\s*([^?]+?)\s*\?\s*\.ripul\(\s*\.(" + STYLES + r")\s*,\s*family:\s*\.code\s*\)\s*:\s*\.ripul\(\s*\.\2\s*\)\s*\)",

328	    code = re.sub(r"\bColor\(\s*(?:uiColor:\s*)?(?:UIColor)?\.(" + SYSTEM_NAMES + r")\s*\)", lambda m: system(m.group(1)), code)
329	    code = re.sub(r"(?:\b(?:Color|UIColor))?\.ripul\(\s*system:\s*\.(\w+)\s*\)", lambda m: system(m.group(1)), code)
330	    code = re.sub(r"\bUIColor\.ripul\(\s*\.(\w+)\s*\)", lambda m: role(m.group(1)), code)
331	    code = re.sub(r"\bUIColor\.(" + SYSTEM_NAMES + r")\b",
332	                  lambda m: role(UIKIT_TEXT[m.group(1)]) if m.group(1) in UIKIT_TEXT else system(m.group(1)), code)

334	    # `.secondary` draw differently in a list row, a button and a section header
335	    # (measured). `foregroundColor` takes a Color, so its argument is the Color form.
336	    code = re.sub(r"\.foregroundColor\(\s*\.(primary|secondary)\b", lambda m: ".foregroundColor(" + role("C:" + HIERARCHY[m.group(1)]), code)
337	    code = re.sub(r"\.foregroundColor\(\s*\.ripul\(\s*\.(text\w*)\s*\)", lambda m: ".foregroundColor(" + role("C:" + m.group(1)), code)
338	    code = re.sub(r"\bColor\.ripul\(\s*\.(text\w*)\s*\)", lambda m: role("C:" + m.group(1)), code)
339	    code = re.sub(r"\bColor\.ripul\(\s*\.(\w+)\s*\)", lambda m: role(m.group(1)), code)
340	    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.ripul\(\s*\.(text\w*|accent|onAccent|canvas|surface\w*|separator|success|warning|danger|info|neutral)\s*\)",
341	                  lambda m: role(m.group(1)), code)
342	    code = re.sub(r"\bColor\.(primary|secondary)\b", lambda m: role("C:" + HIERARCHY[m.group(1)]), code)
343	    code = re.sub(r"\bColor\.accentColor\b|(?<![\w)\]])\.(?:tint|accentColor)\b(?!\s*\()", role("accent"), code)
344	    code = re.sub(r"\bColor\.(" + HUES + r")\b", lambda m: hue(m.group(1)), code)
345	    # A bare `.secondary` is the style or the Color depending on its type, which only the
346	    # compiler knows. Three cases can be told from the text:
347	    #  - the whole argument of a style call, with no colour beside it: the style;
348	    #  - in a style call beside a colour (`flag ? .white : .primary`): a Color, because the
349	    #    two branches must share one type and `.white` is only a Color;

353	    code = bare_hierarchy(code)
354	    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.(primary|secondary|tertiary|quaternary)\b(?!\s*\(|:)", lambda m: role(HIERARCHY[m.group(1)]), code)
355	    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.(" + HUES + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)", lambda m: hue(m.group(1)), code)

358	    return re.sub(r"\s+", "", code)

361	def lint(arguments):
362	    paths = []
363	    if "--" in arguments:
364	        cut = arguments.index("--")
365	        arguments, paths = arguments[:cut], arguments[cut + 1:]
366	    revision = arguments[0] if arguments else "HEAD"
367	    import subprocess
368	    diff = subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "-U0", "--no-color", revision, "--", *(paths or ["*.swift"])],
369	                          capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
370	    problems, checked, file, removed, added, line = [], 0, "", [], [], 0
371	
372	    def flush():
373	        nonlocal checked
374	        # The accessors' own implementation is not a call site (the check does not count it either).
375	        if "/ThemeCore/" in file:
376	            return
377	        # A line whose only `.ripul` is a control modifier holds no token: nothing to pair.
378	        touched = [a for a in added if ".ripul" in control_identities(a[1])]
379	        if not touched:
380	            return
381	        if len(removed) != len(added):
382	            for number, text in touched:
383	                if "theme-mapping:" not in text:
384	                    problems.append((file, number, text, "the hunk adds and removes different numbers of lines; pair it by hand, "
385	                                                          "or mark the line `// theme-mapping: <reason>`"))
386	            return
387	        for (_, old), (number, new) in zip(removed, added):
388	            if ".ripul" not in new:
389	                continue
390	            if ".ripul" not in control_identities(new) and skeleton(old.split("//", 1)[0]) == skeleton(new.split("//", 1)[0]):
391	                checked += 1
392	                continue
393	            checked += 1
394	            if "theme-mapping:" in new or "theme-exempt:" in new:
395	                continue
396	            before, after = skeleton(old.split("//", 1)[0]), skeleton(new.split("//", 1)[0])
397	            if not same_value(before, after):
398	                problems.append((file, number, new, f"was: {old.strip()}"))
399	
400	    for raw in diff.splitlines():
401	        if raw.startswith("+++ "):
402	            flush(); removed, added = [], []
403	            file = raw[6:] if raw.startswith("+++ b/") else raw[4:]
404	        elif raw.startswith("@@"):
405	            flush(); removed, added = [], []
406	            line = int(re.search(r"\+(\d+)", raw).group(1))
407	        elif raw.startswith("-") and not raw.startswith("---"):
408	            removed.append((0, raw[1:]))
409	        elif raw.startswith("+") and not raw.startswith("+++"):
410	            added.append((line, raw[1:])); line += 1
411	    flush()
412	    for file, number, text, why in problems:
413	        print(f"{file}:{number}: {text.strip()}\n    {why}")
414	    if problems:
415	        print(f"\nrewrite_theme_tokens --lint: {len(problems)} of {checked + len(problems)} replacements do not keep the value they replaced.\n"
416	              "The closed table in ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md gives the one token for each literal. Where the\n"
417	              "change is meant, put `// theme-mapping: <reason>` on the new line.")
418	        return 1
419	    print(f"rewrite_theme_tokens --lint: {checked} replacements, each keeps the value it replaced")
420	    return 0
421	
422	
423	def main(argv) -> int:
424	    if argv[:1] == ["--lint"]:
425	        return lint(argv[1:])
426	    dry = "--dry-run" in argv
427	    icons_only = "--icons" in argv
428	    targets = [a for a in argv if not a.startswith("--")]
429	    if not targets:
430	        print(__doc__)
431	        return 2
432	    total = 0
433	    for target in targets:
434	        path = pathlib.Path(target)
435	        files = sorted(path.rglob("*.swift")) if path.is_dir() else [path]
436	        for file in files:
437	            if any(part in file.as_posix() for part in SKIPPED):
438	                continue
439	            text = file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
440	            new, changed = rewrite(text, icons_only=icons_only)
441	            if not changed:
442	                continue
443	            total += changed
444	            print(f"{file}: {changed} line{'s' if changed != 1 else ''}")
445	            if dry:
446	                for old_line, new_line in zip(text.split("\n"), new.split("\n")):
447	                    if old_line != new_line:
448	                        print(f"  - {old_line.strip()}\n  + {new_line.strip()}")
449	            else:
450	                file.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
451	    print(f"rewrite_theme_tokens: {total} lines {'would change' if dry else 'changed'}")
452	    return 0
453	
454	
455	if __name__ == "__main__":
456	    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Rewrite the mechanical font and text-colour call sites to theme tokens.

Syntax only: every rewrite produces the accessor whose default is the very
value it replaces, so nothing changes on screen (the equalities are tested in
ripul-ios-sdk/Tests/RipulAgentTests/RipulThemeCoreTests.swift, and the pixel
identity of the hierarchy styles and of `.monospaced()` was measured; see
ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md). Anything that needs a decision is left alone
and still shows in `check_theme_tokens.py --list`.

  rewrite_theme_tokens.py <file or directory>...        rewrite in place
  rewrite_theme_tokens.py --dry-run <file or directory>...   show what would change
  rewrite_theme_tokens.py --icons <file or directory>...     only move role fonts on an Image to ripulIcon
  rewrite_theme_tokens.py --lint [<git range>] [-- <path>...]
        the mapping lint: read a migration diff (default: the working tree against
        HEAD) and accept a replacement only if the token's default is the very
        value it replaced, by the closed table in theming.md. Exit 1 otherwise.
        A deliberate exception takes `// theme-mapping: <reason>` on the new line.

What it rewrites:
  .font(.body)                                -> .font(.ripul(.body))
  .font(.caption.weight(.semibold))           -> .font(.ripul(.caption, weight: .semibold))
  .font(.caption) on an Image                 -> .font(.ripulIcon(.caption))           (an icon size, never themed)
  .font(.title.bold())                        -> .font(.ripul(.title).bold())        (kept as a call: bold() is not weight(.bold))
  .font(.caption.monospacedDigit())           -> .font(.ripul(.caption).monospacedDigit())
  .font(.caption.monospaced())                -> .font(.ripul(.caption, family: .code))
  .font(.system(.caption, design: .monospaced)) -> .font(.ripul(.caption, family: .code))
  .font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))   -> .font(.ripul(size: 14, weight: .medium))      on text
                                              -> .font(.ripulIcon(size: 14, weight: .medium))  on an Image
  .font(.system(size: 12, design: .monospaced)) -> .font(.ripul(size: 12, family: .code))
  .foregroundStyle(.secondary)                -> .foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))
      (also foregroundColor, fill, stroke, strokeBorder, background, tint; .primary/.tertiary/.quaternary;
       and a ternary whose two sides are both of these)
  Color.primary / Color.secondary             -> Color.ripul(.text) / Color.ripul(.textSecondary)

A fixed-size font is "on an Image" when the view its modifier chain hangs
from starts with `Image(`, and "on text" when it starts with `Text(`. Where
the script cannot tell, it leaves the line for you. Either way the pixels are
the same today; the choice only decides whether a theme's family will apply.

Never touched: a line marked `theme-exempt:`, a branch that compiles only for
macOS, CmsRender/, ThemeCore/, and
named colours (`Color.red`, `.foregroundStyle(.orange)`), which need a
decision each.
"""
import pathlib
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

STYLES = r"largeTitle|title[23]?|headline|subheadline|body|callout|footnote|caption2?"
HIERARCHY = {"primary": "text", "secondary": "textSecondary", "tertiary": "textTertiary", "quaternary": "textQuaternary"}
SKIPPED = ("/CmsRender/", "/ThemeCore/")

# A chain of simple calls after the style: .weight(.semibold).monospacedDigit()
CHAIN = r"(?:\.[A-Za-z]+\((?:[^()]|\([^()]*\))*\))*"
STYLE_FONT = re.compile(r"\.font\(\s*\.(" + STYLES + r")(" + CHAIN + r")\s*\)")
SYSTEM_STYLE_FONT = re.compile(r"\.font\(\s*\.system\(\s*\.(" + STYLES + r")\s*,\s*design:\s*\.monospaced\s*\)(" + CHAIN + r")\s*\)")
ARG = r"((?:[^,()]|\([^()]*\))+?)"
FIXED_FONT = re.compile(r"\.font\(\s*\.system\(\s*size:\s*" + ARG + r"(?:\s*,\s*weight:\s*" + ARG + r")?(?:\s*,\s*design:\s*\.(monospaced|default))?\s*\)(" + CHAIN + r")\s*\)")
STYLE_CALLS = r"foregroundStyle|foregroundColor|fill|stroke|strokeBorder|background|tint"
HIERARCHY_ARG = re.compile(r"\.(" + STYLE_CALLS + r")\(\s*\.(primary|secondary|tertiary|quaternary)\s*(?=[,)])")
HIERARCHY_TERNARY = re.compile(r"\.(" + STYLE_CALLS + r")\(\s*((?:[^()?:]|\([^()]*\))+?)\?\s*\.(primary|secondary|tertiary|quaternary)\s*:\s*\.(primary|secondary|tertiary|quaternary)\s*(?=[,)])")
COLOR_HIERARCHY = re.compile(r"\bColor\.(primary|secondary)\b")
WEIGHT_CALL = re.compile(r"^\.weight\(\s*(\.[A-Za-z]+)\s*\)")
MONO_CALL = re.compile(r"\.monospaced\(\)")


def style_font(match):
    style, chain = match.group(1), match.group(2)
    arguments = [f".{style}"]
    weight = WEIGHT_CALL.match(chain)
    if weight:
        arguments.append(f"weight: {weight.group(1)}")
        chain = chain[weight.end():]
    if MONO_CALL.search(chain):
        chain = MONO_CALL.sub("", chain, count=1)
        arguments.append("family: .code")
    return f".font(.ripul({', '.join(arguments)}){chain})"


def system_style_font(match):
    return f".font(.ripul(.{match.group(1)}, family: .code){match.group(2)})"


def base_of_chain(lines, index, column):
    """The start of the view expression a modifier at lines[index][column] hangs from."""
    before = lines[index][:column].strip()
    if before and not before.startswith("."):
        return before
    for back in range(index - 1, max(index - 40, -1), -1):
        text = lines[back].split("//", 1)[0].strip()
        if not text:
            continue
        if text.startswith(".") or text in ("}", ")", "})"):
            # Still in the chain, or a closing line of a multi-line base: give up on the
            # second, a builder closure could hold anything.
            if not text.startswith("."):
                return ""
            continue
        return text
    return ""


# A text-style font already written as a role, with at most a weight: `.font(.ripul(.caption))`.
ROLE_FONT = re.compile(r"\.font\(\s*\.ripul\(\s*(\.(?:" + STYLES + r")(?:\s*,\s*weight:\s*(?:[^,()]|\([^()]*\))+)?)\s*\)")
VIEW_NAMED = re.compile(r"\b(Image|Text|Label|TextField|TextEditor|SecureField)\(")


def on_an_image(lines, index, column):
    """True when the modifier at lines[index][column] hangs from an `Image(...)`."""
    views = VIEW_NAMED.findall(base_of_chain(lines, index, column))
    # Only an Image, and nothing that draws text beside it: a font on `Label` or on a
    # stack holding a `Text` too is type.
    return bool(views) and all(view == "Image" for view in views)


def icon_fonts(lines, index, code):
    """A font on a symbol is an icon size, never type: `.ripul(.caption)` there is `.ripulIcon(.caption)`."""
    return ROLE_FONT.sub(lambda m: f".font(.ripulIcon({m.group(1)})" if on_an_image(lines, index, m.start()) else m.group(0), code)


def rewrite(text, icons_only=False):
    lines = text.split("\n")
    changed = 0
    # A branch that compiles only for the Mac host is left exactly as it is.
    from check_theme_tokens import mac_only_lines
    mac_only = mac_only_lines(lines)
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if index in mac_only:
            continue
        if "theme-exempt:" in line or (index and "theme-exempt:" in lines[index - 1]):
            continue
        code, slashes, comment = line.partition("//")
        original = code
        if icons_only:
            code = icon_fonts(lines, index, code)
            if code != original:
                lines[index] = code + slashes + comment
                changed += 1
            continue
        code = SYSTEM_STYLE_FONT.sub(system_style_font, code)
        code = STYLE_FONT.sub(style_font, code)
        code = icon_fonts(lines, index, code)

        def fixed_font(match, index=index):
            size, weight, design, chain = match.group(1).strip(), match.group(2), match.group(3), match.group(4)
            base = base_of_chain(lines, index, match.start())
            # The last view named before the modifier decides: `Image(...)` or `Text(...)`.
            views = re.findall(r"\b(Image|Text|Label|TextField|TextEditor|SecureField)\(", base)
            kind = views[-1] if views else None
            if design == "monospaced":
                kind = "Text" if kind in (None, "Text", "TextField", "TextEditor", "SecureField") else kind
            if kind == "Image" and design != "monospaced":
                name, family = "ripulIcon", ""
            elif kind in ("Text", "TextField", "TextEditor", "SecureField"):
                name, family = "ripul", ", family: .code" if design == "monospaced" else ""
            else:
                return match.group(0)
            weight_part = f", weight: {weight.strip()}" if weight else ""
            return f".font(.{name}(size: {size}{weight_part}{family}){chain})"

        code = FIXED_FONT.sub(fixed_font, code)
        code = HIERARCHY_TERNARY.sub(
            lambda m: f".{m.group(1)}({m.group(2)}? .ripul(.{HIERARCHY[m.group(3)]}) : .ripul(.{HIERARCHY[m.group(4)]})", code)
        code = HIERARCHY_ARG.sub(lambda m: f".{m.group(1)}(.ripul(.{HIERARCHY[m.group(2)]})", code)
        code = COLOR_HIERARCHY.sub(lambda m: f"Color.ripul(.{HIERARCHY[m.group(1)]})", code)
        if code != original:
            lines[index] = code + slashes + comment
            changed += 1
    return "\n".join(lines), changed


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the mapping lint
#
# Both sides of a changed line are reduced to a skeleton in which every literal and
# every accessor is replaced by a name for the VALUE IT DRAWS BY DEFAULT. If the two
# skeletons are equal, each replacement kept its value, so nothing changed on screen.

NAMED_ROLE = {"red": "danger", "orange": "warning", "green": "success", "blue": "info", "gray": "neutral", "white": "onAccent"}
HUES = "red|orange|yellow|green|mint|teal|cyan|blue|indigo|purple|pink|brown|gray|white|black"
# A system colour that is also a role's default, in both toolkits.
SYSTEM_ROLE = {"systemBackground": "canvas", "secondarySystemGroupedBackground": "surface",
               "systemGroupedBackground": "surfaceSunken", "separator": "separator", "systemGreen": "success",
               "systemOrange": "warning", "systemRed": "danger", "systemBlue": "info", "systemGray": "neutral",
               "white": "onAccent"}
# UIKit's label colours are the text roles' defaults there. In SwiftUI they are NOT:
# `Color(.secondaryLabel)` is a fixed colour, `.secondary` is the hierarchical style.
UIKIT_TEXT = {"label": "text", "secondaryLabel": "textSecondary", "tertiaryLabel": "textTertiary",
              "quaternaryLabel": "textQuaternary", "tintColor": "accent"}
SYSTEM_NAMES = (r"system[A-Z]\w*|label|secondaryLabel|tertiaryLabel|quaternaryLabel|separator|opaqueSeparator|"
                r"placeholderText|link|(?:secondary|tertiary)System\w+|quaternarySystemFill|tintColor|white|black")
UIFONT_STYLE = {"largeTitle": "largeTitle", "title1": "title", "title2": "title2", "title3": "title3", "headline": "headline",
                "body": "body", "callout": "callout", "subheadline": "subheadline", "footnote": "footnote",
                "caption1": "caption", "caption2": "caption2"}


def role(name):
    return f"\u00a7{name}\u00a7"


def system(name):
    return role(SYSTEM_ROLE[name]) if name in SYSTEM_ROLE else f"\u00a7sys:{name}\u00a7"


def hue(name):
    return role(NAMED_ROLE[name]) if name in NAMED_ROLE else system("black" if name == "black" else "system" + name.capitalize())


BARE_HIERARCHY = re.compile(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.(primary|secondary|tertiary|quaternary)\b(?!\s*\(|:)")
# Evidence of a Color beside a bare name: the word, or a colour's symbol. Not the accent's
# (`.tint` is a style) and not another hierarchy name.
# `tint ?? .primary` counts too: `??` makes both sides one type, and the optional beside a
# colour name in a style call is in practice a `Color?`.
COLOUR_BESIDE = re.compile(r"\?\?|\bColor\b|\u00a7(?!accent\u00a7|\??text)|(?<![\w)\]])\.(?:" + HUES + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)")
STYLE_OPEN = re.compile(r"\.(?:" + STYLE_CALLS + r"|border|listRowBackground)\(")
TYPED_COLOR = re.compile(r":\s*\[?Color\b|->\s*Color\b")


def bare_hierarchy(code):
    if TYPED_COLOR.search(code):
        return BARE_HIERARCHY.sub(lambda m: role("C:" + HIERARCHY[m.group(1)]), code)
    spans = []
    for match in STYLE_OPEN.finditer(code):
        depth, start, end = 1, match.end(), len(code)
        for index in range(start, len(code)):
            depth += {"(": 1, ")": -1}.get(code[index], 0)
            if depth == 0:
                end = index
                break
        spans.append((start, end))
    out, last = [], 0
    for match in BARE_HIERARCHY.finditer(code):
        name = HIERARCHY[match.group(1)]
        inside = next(((a, b) for a, b in spans if a <= match.start() < b), None)
        if inside is None:
            symbol = role("?" + name)
        else:
            rest = code[inside[0]:match.start()] + code[match.end():inside[1]]
            rest = BARE_HIERARCHY.sub("", rest)
            is_color = COLOUR_BESIDE.search(rest) and "AnyShapeStyle(" not in rest
            # The other branch of a ternary is a name (`selected ? color : .secondary`): only the
            # compiler knows whether `color` is a Color, so either form is taken.
            beside_a_name = re.search(r"\?\s*[A-Za-z_]|\s:\s*[A-Za-z_]", rest) and "AnyShapeStyle(" not in rest
            symbol = role(("C:" if is_color else "?" if beside_a_name else "") + name)
        out.append(code[last:match.start()] + symbol)
        last = match.end()
    return "".join(out) + code[last:]


def same_value(before, after):
    """Equal skeletons, where an open `?name` on the old side takes either form on the new."""
    if before == after:
        return True
    pattern = re.escape(before)
    pattern = re.sub("\u00a7\\\\\\?(\\w+)\u00a7", lambda m: "\u00a7(?:C:|\\?)?" + m.group(1) + "\u00a7", pattern)
    return re.fullmatch(pattern, after) is not None


# The control modifiers of "Controls that style their own text" (docs/theming.md). With no
# theme each is the system's own style, or nothing at all, so the lint reads them that way.
CONTROL_IDENTITIES = [
    (re.compile(r"\.ripulProminentButtonStyle\(\)"), ".buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)"),
    (re.compile(r"\.ripulGlassProminentButtonStyle\(\)"), ".buttonStyle(.glassProminent)"),
    (re.compile(r"\.ripul(?:EmptyStateTitle|EmptyStateDescription|SectionHeader|SectionFooter)\(\)"), ""),
    # The accent once a theme names one; with no theme, the role it replaced.
    (re.compile(r"\.ripul\(\s*accentOr:\s*\.(\w+)\s*\)"), r".ripul(.\1)"),
    # Not a token: the notification's name.
    (re.compile(r"\.ripulThemeDidChange\b"), ".themeDidChange"),
]


def control_identities(code):
    for pattern, replacement in CONTROL_IDENTITIES:
        code = pattern.sub(replacement, code)
    return code


def skeleton(code):
    code = control_identities(code)
    if TYPED_COLOR.search(code):
        # On a line whose type is Color, a bare `.ripul(.textSecondary)` is the Color form.
        code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.ripul\(\s*\.(text\w*)\s*\)", lambda m: role("C:" + m.group(1)), code)
    # A monospaced font whose style is chosen at run time: `.system(flag ? .caption : .callout, design: .monospaced)`.
    code = re.sub(r"\.system\(\s*([^,()]*\?\s*\.(?:" + STYLES + r")\s*:\s*\.(?:" + STYLES + r"))\s*,\s*design:\s*\.monospaced\s*\)",
                  lambda m: f".ripul({m.group(1).strip()}, family: .code)", code)
    # A design chosen at run time: `.system(.caption, design: flag ? .monospaced : .default)`.
    # Both spellings of its replacement are read as the first one.
    code = re.sub(r"\.system\(\s*\.(" + STYLES + r")\s*,\s*design:\s*([^?]+?)\s*\?\s*\.monospaced\s*:\s*\.default\s*\)",
                  lambda m: f".ripul(.{m.group(1)}, family: {m.group(2).strip()} ? .code : nil)", code)
    # Fonts first, by the same rules the rewrite applies, with every fixed size read as text.
    code = SYSTEM_STYLE_FONT.sub(system_style_font, code)
    code = STYLE_FONT.sub(style_font, code)
    code = FIXED_FONT.sub(lambda m: ".font(.ripul(size: %s%s%s)%s)" % (
        m.group(1).strip(), f", weight: {m.group(2).strip()}" if m.group(2) else "",
        ", family: .code" if m.group(3) == "monospaced" else "", m.group(4)), code)
    # The same forms with no type written before them (`v.font = .preferredFont(...)`, a
    # property typed Font, a branch of a ternary inside `.font(`).
    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.system\(\s*\.(" + STYLES + r")\s*,\s*design:\s*\.monospaced\s*\)", r".ripul(.\1, family: .code)", code)
    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.system\(\s*size:", ".ripul(size:", code)
    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.preferredFont\(\s*forTextStyle:\s*\.(\w+)\s*\)",
                  lambda m: f".ripul(.{UIFONT_STYLE.get(m.group(1), m.group(1))})", code)
    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.monospacedSystemFont\(\s*ofSize:\s*([^,()]+)(,\s*weight:\s*[^,()]+)?\)",
                  lambda m: f".ripul(size: {m.group(1).strip()}{m.group(2) or ''}, family: .code)", code)
    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.systemFont\(\s*ofSize:", ".ripul(size:", code)
    code = re.sub(r"\bFont\.(" + STYLES + r")\b", r"Font.ripul(.\1)", code)
    # A bare text style wherever it stands (`return .headline`, `flag ? .caption2 : .caption`,
    # a property typed Font) is the same replacement as inside `.font(`. A name that is not a
    # font (an enum's `.body`) is changed on both sides alike, so it still compares equal.
    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w.)\]])(?<!ripul\()(?<!Icon\()(?<!To: )(?<!Style: )\.(" + STYLES + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)", r".ripul(.\1)", code)
    # `.ripul(.body).weight(w)` and `.ripul(.body, weight: w)` are one value, whatever `w` is.
    code = re.sub(r"\.ripul\(\s*\.(" + STYLES + r")\s*\)\.weight\(((?:[^()]|\([^()]*\))*)\)",
                  lambda m: f".ripul(.{m.group(1)}, weight: {m.group(2).strip()})", code)
    code = re.sub(r"\bFont\.system\(\s*size:", "Font.ripul(size:", code)
    code = re.sub(r"\bUIFont\.preferredFont\(\s*forTextStyle:\s*\.(\w+)\s*\)",
                  lambda m: f"UIFont.ripul(.{UIFONT_STYLE.get(m.group(1), m.group(1))})", code)
    code = re.sub(r"\bUIFont\.monospacedSystemFont\(\s*ofSize:\s*([^,()]+)(,\s*weight:\s*[^,()]+)?\)",
                  lambda m: f"UIFont.ripul(size: {m.group(1).strip()}{m.group(2) or ''}, family: .code)", code)
    code = re.sub(r"\bUIFont\.systemFont\(\s*ofSize:", "UIFont.ripul(size:", code)
    code = code.replace(".ripulIcon(", ".ripul(")
    # `UIFont.ripul(.body)` and a bare `.ripul(.body)` assigned to a UIFont are one thing.
    code = re.sub(r"\b(?:UIFont|Font)\.ripul\(", ".ripul(", code)
    # The ternary written outside is the same font as the ternary in the family.
    code = re.sub(r"\.font\(\s*([^?]+?)\s*\?\s*\.ripul\(\s*\.(" + STYLES + r")\s*,\s*family:\s*\.code\s*\)\s*:\s*\.ripul\(\s*\.\2\s*\)\s*\)",
                  lambda m: f".font(.ripul(.{m.group(2)}, family: {m.group(1).strip()} ? .code : nil))", code)
    # Colours. Wrapped UIKit colours in SwiftUI are fixed system colours.
    code = re.sub(r"\bColor\(\s*(?:uiColor:\s*)?(?:UIColor)?\.(" + SYSTEM_NAMES + r")\s*\)", lambda m: system(m.group(1)), code)
    code = re.sub(r"(?:\b(?:Color|UIColor))?\.ripul\(\s*system:\s*\.(\w+)\s*\)", lambda m: system(m.group(1)), code)
    code = re.sub(r"\bUIColor\.ripul\(\s*\.(\w+)\s*\)", lambda m: role(m.group(1)), code)
    code = re.sub(r"\bUIColor\.(" + SYSTEM_NAMES + r")\b",
                  lambda m: role(UIKIT_TEXT[m.group(1)]) if m.group(1) in UIKIT_TEXT else system(m.group(1)), code)
    # A Color is not the hierarchical style of the same name: `Color.secondary` and
    # `.secondary` draw differently in a list row, a button and a section header
    # (measured). `foregroundColor` takes a Color, so its argument is the Color form.
    code = re.sub(r"\.foregroundColor\(\s*\.(primary|secondary)\b", lambda m: ".foregroundColor(" + role("C:" + HIERARCHY[m.group(1)]), code)
    code = re.sub(r"\.foregroundColor\(\s*\.ripul\(\s*\.(text\w*)\s*\)", lambda m: ".foregroundColor(" + role("C:" + m.group(1)), code)
    code = re.sub(r"\bColor\.ripul\(\s*\.(text\w*)\s*\)", lambda m: role("C:" + m.group(1)), code)
    code = re.sub(r"\bColor\.ripul\(\s*\.(\w+)\s*\)", lambda m: role(m.group(1)), code)
    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.ripul\(\s*\.(text\w*|accent|onAccent|canvas|surface\w*|separator|success|warning|danger|info|neutral)\s*\)",
                  lambda m: role(m.group(1)), code)
    code = re.sub(r"\bColor\.(primary|secondary)\b", lambda m: role("C:" + HIERARCHY[m.group(1)]), code)
    code = re.sub(r"\bColor\.accentColor\b|(?<![\w)\]])\.(?:tint|accentColor)\b(?!\s*\()", role("accent"), code)
    code = re.sub(r"\bColor\.(" + HUES + r")\b", lambda m: hue(m.group(1)), code)
    # A bare `.secondary` is the style or the Color depending on its type, which only the
    # compiler knows. Three cases can be told from the text:
    #  - the whole argument of a style call, with no colour beside it: the style;
    #  - in a style call beside a colour (`flag ? .white : .primary`): a Color, because the
    #    two branches must share one type and `.white` is only a Color;
    #  - on a line that says its type is Color: a Color.
    # Anywhere else (`tint: .secondary`, `return .secondary`) it is left open, and either
    # form is accepted in its place.
    code = bare_hierarchy(code)
    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.(primary|secondary|tertiary|quaternary)\b(?!\s*\(|:)", lambda m: role(HIERARCHY[m.group(1)]), code)
    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.(" + HUES + r")\b(?!\s*\(|:)", lambda m: hue(m.group(1)), code)
    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.(label|secondaryLabel|tertiaryLabel|quaternaryLabel|tintColor)\b", lambda m: role(UIKIT_TEXT[m.group(1)]), code)
    code = re.sub(r"(?<![\w)\]])\.(system[A-Z]\w*|(?:secondary|tertiary)System\w+|quaternarySystemFill|separator|opaqueSeparator|placeholderText|link)\b(?!\s*\(|:)", lambda m: system(m.group(1)), code)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", "", code)


def lint(arguments):
    paths = []
    if "--" in arguments:
        cut = arguments.index("--")
        arguments, paths = arguments[:cut], arguments[cut + 1:]
    revision = arguments[0] if arguments else "HEAD"
    import subprocess
    diff = subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "-U0", "--no-color", revision, "--", *(paths or ["*.swift"])],
                          capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    problems, checked, file, removed, added, line = [], 0, "", [], [], 0

    def flush():
        nonlocal checked
        # The accessors' own implementation is not a call site (the check does not count it either).
        if "/ThemeCore/" in file:
            return
        # A line whose only `.ripul` is a control modifier holds no token: nothing to pair.
        touched = [a for a in added if ".ripul" in control_identities(a[1])]
        if not touched:
            return
        if len(removed) != len(added):
            for number, text in touched:
                if "theme-mapping:" not in text:
                    problems.append((file, number, text, "the hunk adds and removes different numbers of lines; pair it by hand, "
                                                          "or mark the line `// theme-mapping: <reason>`"))
            return
        for (_, old), (number, new) in zip(removed, added):
            if ".ripul" not in new:
                continue
            if ".ripul" not in control_identities(new) and skeleton(old.split("//", 1)[0]) == skeleton(new.split("//", 1)[0]):
                checked += 1
                continue
            checked += 1
            if "theme-mapping:" in new or "theme-exempt:" in new:
                continue
            before, after = skeleton(old.split("//", 1)[0]), skeleton(new.split("//", 1)[0])
            if not same_value(before, after):
                problems.append((file, number, new, f"was: {old.strip()}"))

    for raw in diff.splitlines():
        if raw.startswith("+++ "):
            flush(); removed, added = [], []
            file = raw[6:] if raw.startswith("+++ b/") else raw[4:]
        elif raw.startswith("@@"):
            flush(); removed, added = [], []
            line = int(re.search(r"\+(\d+)", raw).group(1))
        elif raw.startswith("-") and not raw.startswith("---"):
            removed.append((0, raw[1:]))
        elif raw.startswith("+") and not raw.startswith("+++"):
            added.append((line, raw[1:])); line += 1
    flush()
    for file, number, text, why in problems:
        print(f"{file}:{number}: {text.strip()}\n    {why}")
    if problems:
        print(f"\nrewrite_theme_tokens --lint: {len(problems)} of {checked + len(problems)} replacements do not keep the value they replaced.\n"
              "The closed table in ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md gives the one token for each literal. Where the\n"
              "change is meant, put `// theme-mapping: <reason>` on the new line.")
        return 1
    print(f"rewrite_theme_tokens --lint: {checked} replacements, each keeps the value it replaced")
    return 0


def main(argv) -> int:
    if argv[:1] == ["--lint"]:
        return lint(argv[1:])
    dry = "--dry-run" in argv
    icons_only = "--icons" in argv
    targets = [a for a in argv if not a.startswith("--")]
    if not targets:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    total = 0
    for target in targets:
        path = pathlib.Path(target)
        files = sorted(path.rglob("*.swift")) if path.is_dir() else [path]
        for file in files:
            if any(part in file.as_posix() for part in SKIPPED):
                continue
            text = file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            new, changed = rewrite(text, icons_only=icons_only)
            if not changed:
                continue
            total += changed
            print(f"{file}: {changed} line{'s' if changed != 1 else ''}")
            if dry:
                for old_line, new_line in zip(text.split("\n"), new.split("\n")):
                    if old_line != new_line:
                        print(f"  - {old_line.strip()}\n  + {new_line.strip()}")
            else:
                file.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"rewrite_theme_tokens: {total} lines {'would change' if dry else 'changed'}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Write the map from an element's identifier to the theme tokens it is drawn with.
3	
4	The View Explorer inspects UIKit views, and SwiftUI draws into layers: the view a person
5	taps holds no colour and no font to read back. The source does. Every identified element
6	is a view expression that ends in `.uiKitIdentifier("…")` (or `.accessibilityIdentifier`),
7	and the theme accessors written in that expression are what it is drawn with. This script
8	reads them and writes one JSON file, which the app bundles and the SDK's
9	`RipulBaseTokenProvider` looks up (ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md, "The View Explorer").
10	
11	  theme_usage_map.py --out <file>     write the map (this is what the app build runs)
12	  theme_usage_map.py --stats          how many identifiers it could name tokens for
13	  theme_usage_map.py --explain <id>   the entry for one identifier, as JSON
14	  theme_usage_map.py --roots A B ...  read these directories instead of Ripul's own
15	
16	For each identifier it records the accessors
17	
18	  own        in the element's own expression, and not inside a part with its own identifier
19	  inherited  on a `.font(…)`, `.foregroundStyle(…)`, `.foregroundColor(…)` or `.tint(…)`
20	             applied to a view that encloses the element in the same function
21	  via        in a view type, a view-returning member or a View-extension modifier the
22	             expression names, two steps deep and sixteen tokens at most
23	
24	An accessor inside a `Button`, `Menu` or `Link` is marked with the control and any
25	`.buttonStyle` chained to it: there the system's hierarchical styles follow the control's
26	tint, so a default text role is drawn in the accent whatever the source names. A control
27	with no foreground written at all is recorded too, since its label is the tint.
28	
29	It is a reader of text, not a compiler. What it cannot see, it leaves out: an identifier
30	held in a variable, a font set by a caller in another type, a colour passed in as a
31	parameter. An identifier with an interpolation (`"row.\\(id)"`) is kept as a pattern
32	(`row.*`). It never fails a build: any error is a warning and an empty map.
33	"""
34	import json
35	import pathlib
36	import re
37	import sys
38	
39	REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
40	ROOTS = ["ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent", "ripul-native-app/iOS", "ripul-native-app/Shared",
41	         "ripul-native-app/Browser"]
42	SKIP_DIRS = {"ThemeCore"}
43	
44	COLOUR_ROLES = {"accent", "onAccent", "canvas", "surface", "surfaceSunken", "text", "textSecondary",
45	                "textTertiary", "textQuaternary", "separator", "success", "warning", "danger", "info", "neutral"}
46	TEXT_ROLES = {"largeTitle", "title", "title2", "title3", "headline", "body", "callout", "subheadline",
47	              "footnote", "caption", "caption2", "display", "eyebrow", "code"}
48	KEYWORDS = {"return", "in", "else", "if", "let", "var", "case", "default", "guard", "while", "for", "do",
49	            "try", "await", "throw", "where", "switch", "some", "any", "is", "as", "func", "static"}
50	PROPERTY = {"foregroundStyle": "Foreground", "foregroundColor": "Foreground", "fill": "Fill",
51	            "background": "Background", "tint": "Tint", "stroke": "Stroke", "strokeBorder": "Stroke",
52	            "border": "Border", "shadow": "Shadow", "font": "Font", "listRowBackground": "Row background",
53	            "overlay": "Overlay", "toolbarBackground": "Bar background", "scrollContentBackground": "Background",
54	            "presentationBackground": "Sheet background", "symbolRenderingMode": "Symbol"}
55	INHERITING = ("font", "foregroundStyle", "foregroundColor", "tint", "ripulTextStyle")
56	MAX_TOKENS = 40
57	MAX_DEPTH = 2
58	MAX_VIA = 16
59	IDENT = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_]")

61	
62	def mask(src: str) -> str:
63	    """The source with comments blanked and string contents replaced, same length.
64	
65	    Code inside a string's `\\( )` is kept, so brackets still pair up across it.
66	    """
67	    out = list(src)
68	    n = len(src)
69	    i = 0
70	
71	    def blank(a, b):
72	        for k in range(a, b):
73	            if out[k] != "\n":
74	                out[k] = " "
75	
76	    def string(start):
77	        triple = src.startswith('"""', start)
78	        q = 3 if triple else 1
79	        k = start + q
80	        while k < n:
81	            if src[k] == "\\" and k + 1 < n:
82	                if src[k + 1] == "(":
83	                    out[k] = "\x01"
84	                    k = code(k + 2, close=")")
85	                    continue
86	                out[k] = out[k + 1] = "\x01"
87	                k += 2
88	                continue
89	            if src.startswith('"' * q, k):
90	                return k + q
91	            if not triple and src[k] == "\n":
92	                return k
93	            if src[k] != "\n":
94	                out[k] = "\x01"
95	            k += 1
96	        return n
97	
98	    def code(start, close=None):
99	        k = start
100	        depth = 0
101	        while k < n:
102	            c = src[k]
103	            if c == "/" and src.startswith("//", k):
104	                e = src.find("\n", k)
105	                e = n if e < 0 else e
106	                blank(k, e)
107	                k = e
108	            elif c == "/" and src.startswith("/*", k):
109	                e = src.find("*/", k + 2)

131	    return re.sub(r"(?m)^[ \t]*#(?:if|elseif|else|endif)\b[^\n]*", lambda m: " " * len(m.group(0)), masked)

133	
134	def pair(code: str):
135	    match = {}
136	    stack = []
137	    opens = {"(": ")", "[": "]", "{": "}"}
138	    for i, c in enumerate(code):
139	        if c in opens:
140	            stack.append(i)
141	        elif c in ")]}":
142	            while stack and opens[code[stack[-1]]] != c:
143	                stack.pop()
144	            if stack:
145	                o = stack.pop()
146	                match[o] = i
147	                match[i] = o
148	    return match

151	class File:
152	    def __init__(self, rel: str, src: str):
153	        self.rel = rel
154	        self.src = src
155	        self.code = mask(src)
156	        self.match = pair(self.code)
157	        self.starts = [0]
158	        for m in re.finditer("\n", src):

161	        self.members = []    # (type name, member, open, close, header)
162	        self.stamps = []     # dicts

165	        self.locals = []     # (name, let position, initialiser start, initialiser end)
166	        self.controls = []   # dicts: a Button, Menu or Link call, label closures included
167	        self.toolbars = []   # (start, end) of `.toolbar { }` and `ToolbarItem( ) { }`
168	        self.menus = []      # (start, end) where the system draws items its own way: a menu's
169	                             # content, a context menu, swipe actions, an alert, a dialog

171	    def line(self, pos: int) -> int:
172	        lo, hi = 0, len(self.starts) - 1
173	        while lo < hi:
174	            mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
175	            if self.starts[mid] <= pos:
176	                lo = mid
177	            else:
178	                hi = mid - 1

181	    def back(self, i: int) -> int:
182	        """The last character at or before i that is not white space; -1 if none."""
183	        code = self.code
184	        while i >= 0 and code[i] in " \t\n\r":
185	            i -= 1

188	    def ident_start(self, k: int) -> int:
189	        code = self.code
190	        while k > 0 and IDENT.match(code[k - 1]):
191	            k -= 1
192	        return k

194	    def chain_start(self, dot: int) -> int:
195	        """Where the expression that `.modifier` at `dot` is applied to begins."""
196	        code, match = self.code, self.match
197	        j = dot
198	        while True:
199	            k = self.back(j - 1)
200	            if k < 0:
201	                return j
202	            c = code[k]
203	            if c in ")]}":
204	                o = match.get(k)
205	                if o is None:

207	                if c == "}":
208	                    p = self.back(o - 1)
209	                    if p >= 0 and code[p] == ":":

268	        """(callee name, argument label, open, close) of the nearest call around `pos`."""
269	        code, match = self.code, self.match

273	            c = code[i]

275	                i = match.get(i, i) - 1
276	                continue
277	            if c in "([{":
278	                close = match.get(i, len(code) - 1)
279	                if c == "(":
280	                    k = i - 1
281	                    s = self.ident_start(k + 1)

284	                        label = None

299	def call_end(f: File, i: int) -> int:
300	    """Where a call that starts its arguments or closures at `i` ends: `( ) { } label: { }`."""
301	    code, match = f.code, f.match
302	    n = len(code)
303	
304	    def ws(k):

318	        if m and (k + m.end() - 1) in match:

323	
324	def chained_style(f: File, i: int):
325	    """The argument of a `.buttonStyle( )` among the modifiers after `i`."""
326	    code, match = f.code, f.match
327	    for _ in range(30):

329	        if not m:

332	        if o not in match:

341	    close = f.match.get(open_paren)

346	    code, match = f.code, f.match
347	
348	    for m in re.finditer(r"\b(struct|class|enum|extension|actor)\s+([A-Za-z_][\w.]*)([^{};]*)\{", code):
349	        o = m.end() - 1
350	        if o in match:
351	            f.types.append((m.group(2).split(".")[-1], o, match[o], m.group(3)))
352	
353	    def type_at(pos):
354	        best = None
355	        for t in f.types:
356	            if t[1] < pos < t[2] and (best is None or t[1] > best[1]):
357	                best = t
358	        return best

361	        i = m.end()

363	        depth = 0
364	        body = None
365	        while i < len(code):
366	            c = code[i]
367	            if c in "(<[":
368	                depth += 1

371	                    pass

373	                    depth -= 1

378	                break
379	            i += 1
380	        if body is None or body not in match:
381	            continue
382	        t = type_at(m.start())
383	        f.members.append((t[0] if t else None, m.group(2), body, match[body], code[header_start:body],
384	                          t[3] if t else ""))

388	    for m in re.finditer(r"(?<![\w.])(Button|Menu|Link|ShareLink)\s*(?=[({])", code):
389	        end = call_end(f, m.end())

395	        f.menus.append((m.start(), call_end(f, m.end())))
396	    for control in f.controls:
397	        if control["name"] != "Menu":
398	            continue
399	        # Everything in a Menu but its `label:` closure is the menu's content.
400	        span = code[control["start"]:control["end"]]
401	        label = [x for x in re.finditer(r"\blabel\s*:\s*\{", span)]
402	        if label and (control["start"] + label[-1].end() - 1) in match:
403	            lo = control["start"] + label[-1].start()
404	            f.menus.append((control["start"] + 4, lo))
405	            f.menus.append((match[control["start"] + label[-1].end() - 1], control["end"]))
406	        else:
