# Sandsend Retreats

An iPhone app for guests of Sandsend Retreats: three holiday cottages (East Hampton, Montauk, Sag Harbor) in the Saltmoore grounds at Sandsend, owned by the Maude family. It onboards a guest (welcome, which cottage, arriving) and then is their guide to the stay. Native SwiftUI, iOS 26, iPhone only, portrait.

Remote: `github.com/ripulio/sandsend-retreats` (private). The business's website is `www.sandsendretreats.com`.

## What is in the app

- **Onboarding** (`Onboarding/`): welcome, choose your cottage, what you need to arrive. Shown until a cottage is chosen.
- **Stay** tab (`Stay/`): check-in and check-out, the keypad, getting here, parking, your cottage with its photos, dogs, no smoking, contact, the owners' story.
- **Explore** tab (`Explore/`): the neighbourhood's places, twelve activities, the spa, private chefs, the village's history.
- **What's On** tab (`WhatsOn/`): the site's calendar of local events, those still to come first.

**Not in the app, because the website does not have it:** door codes, Wi-Fi details, how the heating and appliances work, bins, emergency numbers, anything about one booking. A guide that onboards a guest properly needs these from Peter. Do not invent them.

## The words and photos come from the website

Every sentence a guest reads, apart from headings and button labels, is the website's own, in `SandsendRetreats/Content/guide.json`. Every photo is from the website, in `SandsendRetreats/Photos`.

- **Do not edit `guide.json` by hand.** Change the wording on the website, then run `python3 scripts/import_site.py` and read the diff. The script cuts each page by the headings it has today and stops with an error when one has moved.
- **Photos are chosen in `scripts/photos.json`**: an asset name, the photo's address on the site, and a caption (the app's accessibility label and gallery caption). Add a line and run the script; it downloads, shrinks to 1320 points and converts to HEIC. It skips photos it already has, so delete a file to fetch it again.
- **Photos are plain files, not an asset catalogue**, shown with `PhotoView` or `Image(photo:)`. In an archive build Xcode re-encodes catalogue photos losslessly: 12 MB of photos became 87 MB of assets, whatever the image set's compression setting, and the 111 MB IPA was too big for build hosting (100 MB). Do not move them back.
- `Content/Guide.swift` is the Swift shape of `guide.json`. A field added to one must be added to the other, or the app stops at launch saying which.
- **Whose photos they are.** The cottages, the beach and the family are the owners' own. The activity and chef photos are stock (Pexels, Unsplash, Pixabay, by their filenames). The twelve neighbourhood photos include some taken from those businesses. Nobody has checked the rights for use in an app; the site's event photos were left out for that reason.
- The site spells one cottage both "Sag Harbor" and "Sag Harbour" (the slate sign says Harbour). The app follows the cottage's own page: Harbor.

## Layout

```
project.yml                    XcodeGen spec. The source of truth for the project.
scripts/import_site.py         Website -> guide.json and the photo sets.
scripts/photos.json            Which photos, from where, with what caption.
scripts/ship_ota.py            Publishes a build to the install page.
SandsendRetreats/Content/      guide.json and its Swift model.
SandsendRetreats/Shared/       Theme, shared views (GuidePage, GuideCard, GuideRow), routes and levers.
SandsendRetreats/Theme/        The two theme documents.
SandsendRetreats/Fonts/        The brand theme's fonts, their licences and where they came from.
scripts/theme_usage_map.py     Which theme tokens each named control uses, for the View Explorer.
SandsendRetreats/Developer/    The Ripul developer console and the identifier helper.
```

## Rules

- **The `.xcodeproj` is generated and gitignored.** Run `xcodegen generate` after cloning, after changing `project.yml`, and after adding or removing a source file. Never edit the `.xcodeproj`.
- **One DerivedData path: `build`.** Always pass `-derivedDataPath build`. Do not invent another.
- **The bundle id is `io.ripul.sandsendretreats`** (`SANDSEND_BUNDLE_ID` in `project.yml`), chosen by Peter on 10 October 2026. Do not change it. The first device build (10 October 2026) was signed with the team's wildcard profile, so the id has no App ID of its own at Apple yet; it will need one for push notifications, TestFlight or any other entitlement.
- Use the platform's own controls and the iOS 26 Liquid Glass material; do not re-skin a web look in SwiftUI.
- **Name every control with `.identified("screen.element")`**, not a bare `.accessibilityIdentifier`. Give each control its own name; a name on a container is inherited by what is inside it.
- **Navy buttons say `.tint(Brand.navy)`.** The accent colour turns pale blue in dark mode, and white text on it cannot be read.
- The app icon is a placeholder ("SR" in the signs' navy and cream).

## The theme (branch `theme-trial`, a trial of the Ripul SDK's theme system)

Every font and colour is a theme token of the Ripul SDK: `.font(.ripul(.headline))`, `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))`, `.background(.ripul(.surface))`. The SDK's `docs/theming.md` (in the package checkout, `build/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/docs`) is the contract: read it before writing a view. This puts the SDK in Release builds' code for the first time; before it, every use was inside `#if DEBUG`.

- **Two looks, each a document in `SandsendRetreats/Theme`.** `sandsend-default.json` is the app as it was (it names one thing: the display family is the system serif). `sandsend-brand.json` is the website's and install page's look: paper and navy, Playfair Display for names and headings, Source Sans 3 for text. `Shared/AppTheme.swift` loads one at launch; Stay, More, Look changes it while the app runs.
- **The fonts are stand-ins.** The website uses IvyPresto Display and Freight Sans Pro, which are Adobe Fonts and may not be put in an app. `SandsendRetreats/Fonts/SOURCES.md` says where the bundled ones came from; their licences are beside them.
- **A new `Text` needs `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))`** or it stays black on the brand's paper. Do not set it on a container: it recolours the buttons, links and list headers inside.
- **Headings say `family: .display`**; a symbol's size is `.ripulIcon(...)`; white on a photo is `.ripul(system: .white)`.
- **`Brand.navy` and `Brand.cream`** are the theme's accent and what reads on it once a theme names them. Read them where they are used.
- **A list** takes `.themedList()` and each of its sections `.themedRows()`.
- **`scripts/theme_usage_map.py`** runs in a Debug build and writes `ripul-theme-usage.json` into the app, from which the View Explorer names the tokens of a selected element. The SDK documents such a script and does not ship one; this was written from the SDK's source.
- **Checking the default look has not moved:** screenshots of sixteen screens, light and dark, before and after, compared pixel for pixel (11 October 2026: all the same).
- **Known faults, all the SDK's (0.7.170):** after changing back to Standard while running, the selected tab is system blue until the next launch; tab labels take the brand's font only after a change while running, not at launch; a list's section headers and large navigation titles keep the system's colours.

## Looking at a screen without tapping

A Debug build takes launch arguments that open a given screen (`Shared/Routes.swift`, `Levers`). An agent cannot tap until a person has signed in to the developer console, so this is how to check a change:

```bash
xcrun simctl launch --terminate-running-process <simulator> io.ripul.sandsendretreats \
  -onboarded YES -cottage montauk -tab explore -route activity:surfing
```

| Argument | Values |
|---|---|
| `-onboarded` | `YES` the guide, `NO` onboarding |
| `-cottage` | `east-hampton`, `montauk`, `sag-harbor` |
| `-onboardingStep` | `picker`, `arrival` |
| `-tab` | `stay`, `explore`, `whatsOn` |
| `-route` | `cottage:<id>`, `activity:<id>`, `dogs`, `story`, `wellness`, `chefs`, `history` (opens on the tab `-tab` names) |
| `-scrollToEnd YES`, `-scrollY <points>` | where the page is scrolled to |
| `-gallery YES` | with `-route cottage:<id>`, the photos full screen |
| `-theme` | `standard`, `brand`: the look, kept for later launches (this one works in Release too) |
| `-themeThen` | `standard`, `brand`: changes the look a moment after launch, as the More menu does |
| `-themeReadout YES` | prints what the View Explorer's Appearance section says of each named control on screen (read it with `simctl launch --console-pty`) |

Then `xcrun simctl io <simulator> screenshot <file>`. Add a lever when a new screen cannot be reached by these. A Release build ignores them all.

## Shipping a build: the install page

**https://demo.ripul.io/sandsend** is where a build is installed from, and the app's list of updates: the newest build with what changed in it, and the five before it with theirs. It is hosted by Ripul's build hosting, as app `sandsend`, the way Ripul's own page (`/ios`) is.

```bash
nohup python3 scripts/ship_ota.py "What changed in this build" > /tmp/sandsend-ota.log 2>&1 & disown
tail -n 5 /tmp/sandsend-ota.log
```

- It archives the app, exports a development-signed IPA, publishes it, and then checks the page: that its manifest names this build and that the IPA it serves is the one exported. It ends with "Published and verified" or with the reason it stopped.
- **It ships committed, pushed work only**, and refuses otherwise. Commit and push first.
- **The notes are what a person reads on the page.** Say what changed for a guest, in a sentence or two; they are cut at 400 characters. With none given, the newest commit's subject is used.
- **The page is public.** Anyone with the address can download a build, though only iPhones registered with the team can install one. Peter asked for it to work like Ripul's and WAC's, which are public in the same way.
- Builds are Debug, like a direct install: the developer console and the launch levers are in them.
- A build number is the minute it was made. Publishing twice in one minute is refused with HTTP 409; run it again.
- **A phone registered after the signing profile was made cannot install a build**: iOS says "Unable to Install". The app signs with the team's wildcard profile ("iOS Team Provisioning Profile: *"), and Xcode keeps using its cached copy however old. On 10 October 2026 the copy was from 4 October with 42 phones, and Oxana's iPhone, registered that day, was the 43rd. The cure, once the phone is registered with the team: move the wildcard profile out of `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/UserData/Provisioning Profiles` (to `~/.ripul/appstoreconnect/moved-aside-<date>/`), then ship; the archive fetches a fresh one, using the App Store Connect key in `~/.ripul/appstoreconnect` when the Mac has it. The script prints which profile a build was signed with and for how many iPhones, and `SANDSEND_REQUIRE_DEVICES="<udid> <udid>"` makes it refuse to publish a build those phones could not install. Each Mac has its own cache.
- **The publish token is per Mac**, in `~/.ripul/sandsend-build-token` (the Mac Studio has one). A new Mac gets its own: `openssl rand -hex 32`, then a row in `build_publish_tokens (token_hash, app_id, label)` for app `sandsend`, holding the token's SHA-256, in Ripul's database (`wrangler d1 execute llm-proxy-db --remote --env production`, from `chrome-extension/packages/api` in the ripul repo). Never copy another Mac's token.
- The page's wording and look are in the ripul repo, `chrome-extension/functions/sandsend.ts`: its text, and `LOOK`, the styles (the serif, paper and navy, the card for a build's notes). Its photo is `chrome-extension/public/install/sandsend-hero.jpg`, the beach the app opens on. A change there goes out with Ripul's web deploy, and Ripul's own `/ios` page shares the code underneath, so run that repo's `tests/installPage.test.ts`.

## The Ripul developer console

The app carries the RipulAgent SDK so that coding agents on Peter's Mac can see and tap through it (`device_inspect_screen`, `device_tap_element` and the other `device_…` tools). Read the `sdk` guide from the `ripul_guide` tool before changing any of it.

- **The console exists in Debug builds only.** Every use of the SDK in the app's code is inside `#if DEBUG`: `DeveloperConsole.swift`, the menu item on the Stay tab, and the Debug branch of `.identified`. Keep it that way, and build Release after touching it.
- **The SDK itself is still linked into a Release build.** Xcode links a package into every configuration, so the Release app carries the SDK's code and resource bundles though nothing calls them (57 MB against 93 MB for Debug, simulator builds of the bare app, measured 10 October 2026). Nothing has been done about this. Decide with Peter before the first TestFlight or App Store build: take the package out of Release, or ship it as WAC does.
- **Opening it.** Stay tab, the More menu (top right), Developer Console. After that a bubble floats over the app and comes back on each launch.
- **Opening it without a tap.** Launch with `-openDeveloperConsole YES`. This is how an agent brings the sign-in screen up for a person.
- **Agents get nothing until a person has signed in** to their Ripul account in the console, and only while the app is open in the foreground.
- **The pin is `exactVersion` in `project.yml`.** The project's `Package.resolved` is not in git. To take an SDK release, change that line and rebuild.
- The microphone and speech-recognition descriptions in `project.yml` are for dictation in the console, and are set for Debug only.

name: SandsendRetreats
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: io.ripul
  deploymentTarget:
    iOS: "26.0"
  generateEmptyDirectories: true

settings:
  base:
    # Chosen by Peter, 10 October 2026. Automatic signing registers it with the
    # team at the first device build.
    SANDSEND_BUNDLE_ID: io.ripul.sandsendretreats
    DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: C7AA358R56
    CODE_SIGN_STYLE: Automatic
    SWIFT_VERSION: "5.9"
    MARKETING_VERSION: "0.1.0"
    CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION: "1"

# The .xcodeproj is not in git, so neither is its Package.resolved. The exact
# version here is the pin: move it by hand to take an SDK release.
packages:
  RipulAgent:
    url: https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk
    exactVersion: 0.7.170

targets:
  SandsendRetreats:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    sources:
      - SandsendRetreats
    dependencies:
      - package: RipulAgent
    # The Ripul View Explorer names the theme tokens of a selected element from
    # this file. Debug only, like the explorer.
    postCompileScripts:
      - name: Theme usage map
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: |
          if [ "$CONFIGURATION" = "Debug" ]; then
            python3 "$SRCROOT/scripts/theme_usage_map.py" --roots "$SRCROOT/SandsendRetreats" \
              --out "$TARGET_BUILD_DIR/$UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH/ripul-theme-usage.json"
          fi
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: $(SANDSEND_BUNDLE_ID)
        ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING: NO
        TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY: "1"
        GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES
        INFOPLIST_KEY_CFBundleDisplayName: Sandsend Retreats
        INFOPLIST_KEY_UILaunchScreen_Generation: YES
        INFOPLIST_KEY_UIApplicationSceneManifest_Generation: YES
        INFOPLIST_KEY_UISupportedInterfaceOrientations_iPhone: UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait
        ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME: AppIcon
        ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GLOBAL_ACCENT_COLOR_NAME: AccentColor
      configs:
        # Voice input in the developer console. Debug only, like the console.
        Debug:
          INFOPLIST_KEY_NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: Lets you dictate messages in the Ripul developer console.
          INFOPLIST_KEY_NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription: Turns what you dictate in the Ripul developer console into text.
.gitignore

Every font and colour is a theme token of the Ripul SDK: `.font(.ripul(.headline))`, `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))`, `.background(.ripul(.surface))`. The SDK's `docs/theming.md` (in the package checkout, `build/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/docs`) is the contract: read it before writing a view. This puts the SDK in Release builds' code for the first time; before it, every use was inside `#if DEBUG`.

- **Two looks, each a document in `SandsendRetreats/Theme`.** `sandsend-default.json` is the app as it was (it names one thing: the display family is the system serif). `sandsend-brand.json` is the website's and install page's look: paper and navy, Playfair Display for names and headings, Source Sans 3 for text. `Shared/AppTheme.swift` loads one at launch; Stay, More, Look changes it while the app runs.
- **The fonts are stand-ins.** The website uses IvyPresto Display and Freight Sans Pro, which are Adobe Fonts and may not be put in an app. `SandsendRetreats/Fonts/SOURCES.md` says where the bundled ones came from; their licences are beside them.
- **A new `Text` needs `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))`** or it stays black on the brand's paper. Do not set it on a container: it recolours the buttons, links and list headers inside.
- **Headings say `family: .display`**; a symbol's size is `.ripulIcon(...)`; white on a photo is `.ripul(system: .white)`.
- **`Brand.navy` and `Brand.cream`** are the theme's accent and what reads on it once a theme names them. Read them where they are used.
- **A list** takes `.themedList()` and each of its sections `.themedRows()`.
- **`scripts/theme_usage_map.py`** runs in a Debug build and writes `ripul-theme-usage.json` into the app, from which the View Explorer names the tokens of a selected element. The SDK documents such a script and does not ship one; this was written from the SDK's source.
- **Checking the default look has not moved:** screenshots of sixteen screens, light and dark, before and after, compared pixel for pixel (11 October 2026: all the same).
- **Known faults, all the SDK's (0.7.170):** after changing back to Standard while running, the selected tab is system blue until the next launch; tab labels take the brand's font only after a change while running, not at launch; a list's section headers and large navigation titles keep the system's colours.

## Looking at a screen without tapping

A Debug build takes launch arguments that open a given screen (`Shared/Routes.swift`, `Levers`). An agent cannot tap until a person has signed in to the developer console, so this is how to check a change:

```bash
xcrun simctl launch --terminate-running-process <simulator> io.ripul.sandsendretreats \
  -onboarded YES -cottage montauk -tab explore -route activity:surfing
```

| Argument | Values |
|---|---|
| `-onboarded` | `YES` the guide, `NO` onboarding |
| `-cottage` | `east-hampton`, `montauk`, `sag-harbor` |
| `-onboardingStep` | `picker`, `arrival` |
| `-tab` | `stay`, `explore`, `whatsOn` |
| `-route` | `cottage:<id>`, `activity:<id>`, `dogs`, `story`, `wellness`, `chefs`, `history` (opens on the tab `-tab` names) |
| `-scrollToEnd YES`, `-scrollY <points>` | where the page is scrolled to |
| `-gallery YES` | with `-route cottage:<id>`, the photos full screen |
| `-theme` | `standard`, `brand`: the look, kept for later launches (this one works in Release too) |
| `-themeThen` | `standard`, `brand`: changes the look a moment after launch, as the More menu does |
| `-themeReadout YES` | prints what the View Explorer's Appearance section says of each named control on screen (read it with `simctl launch --console-pty`) |

Then `xcrun simctl io <simulator> screenshot <file>`. Add a lever when a new screen cannot be reached by these. A Release build ignores them all.

## Shipping a build: the install page

**https://demo.ripul.io/sandsend** is where a build is installed from, and the app's list of updates: the newest build with what changed in it, and the five before it with theirs. It is hosted by Ripul's build hosting, as app `sandsend`, the way Ripul's own page (`/ios`) is.

```bash
nohup python3 scripts/ship_ota.py "What changed in this build" > /tmp/sandsend-ota.log 2>&1 & disown
tail -n 5 /tmp/sandsend-ota.log
```

- It archives the app, exports a development-signed IPA, publishes it, and then checks the page: that its manifest names this build and that the IPA it serves is the one exported. It ends with "Published and verified" or with the reason it stopped.
- **It ships committed, pushed work only**, and refuses otherwise. Commit and push first.
- **The notes are what a person reads on the page.** Say what changed for a guest, in a sentence or two; they are cut at 400 characters. With none given, the newest commit's subject is used.
- **The page is public.** Anyone with the address can download a build, though only iPhones registered with the team can install one. Peter asked for it to work like Ripul's and WAC's, which are public in the same way.
- Builds are Debug, like a direct install: the developer console and the launch levers are in them.
- A build number is the minute it was made. Publishing twice in one minute is refused with HTTP 409; run it again.
- **A phone registered after the signing profile was made cannot install a build**: iOS says "Unable to Install". The app signs with the team's wildcard profile ("iOS Team Provisioning Profile: *"), and Xcode keeps using its cached copy however old. On 10 October 2026 the copy was from 4 October with 42 phones, and Oxana's iPhone, registered that day, was the 43rd. The cure, once the phone is registered with the team: move the wildcard profile out of `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/UserData/Provisioning Profiles` (to `~/.ripul/appstoreconnect/moved-aside-<date>/`), then ship; the archive fetches a fresh one, using the App Store Connect key in `~/.ripul/appstoreconnect` when the Mac has it. The script prints which profile a build was signed with and for how many iPhones, and `SANDSEND_REQUIRE_DEVICES="<udid> <udid>"` makes it refuse to publish a build those phones could not install. Each Mac has its own cache.
- **The publish token is per Mac**, in `~/.ripul/sandsend-build-token` (the Mac Studio has one). A new Mac gets its own: `openssl rand -hex 32`, then a row in `build_publish_tokens (token_hash, app_id, label)` for app `sandsend`, holding the token's SHA-256, in Ripul's database (`wrangler d1 execute llm-proxy-db --remote --env production`, from `chrome-extension/packages/api` in the ripul repo). Never copy another Mac's token.
- The page's wording and look are in the ripul repo, `chrome-extension/functions/sandsend.ts`: its text, and `LOOK`, the styles (the serif, paper and navy, the card for a build's notes). Its photo is `chrome-extension/public/install/sandsend-hero.jpg`, the beach the app opens on. A change there goes out with Ripul's web deploy, and Ripul's own `/ios` page shares the code underneath, so run that repo's `tests/installPage.test.ts`.

## The Ripul developer console

The app carries the RipulAgent SDK so that coding agents on Peter's Mac can see and tap through it (`device_inspect_screen`, `device_tap_element` and the other `device_…` tools). Read the `sdk` guide from the `ripul_guide` tool before changing any of it.

- **The console exists in Debug builds only.** Every use of the SDK in the app's code is inside `#if DEBUG`: `DeveloperConsole.swift`, the menu item on the Stay tab, and the Debug branch of `.identified`. Keep it that way, and build Release after touching it.
- **The SDK itself is still linked into a Release build.** Xcode links a package into every configuration, so the Release app carries the SDK's code and resource bundles though nothing calls them (57 MB against 93 MB for Debug, simulator builds of the bare app, measured 10 October 2026). Nothing has been done about this. Decide with Peter before the first TestFlight or App Store build: take the package out of Release, or ship it as WAC does.
- **Opening it.** Stay tab, the More menu (top right), Developer Console. After that a bubble floats over the app and comes back on each launch.
- **Opening it without a tap.** Launch with `-openDeveloperConsole YES`. This is how an agent brings the sign-in screen up for a person.
- **Agents get nothing until a person has signed in** to their Ripul account in the console, and only while the app is open in the foreground.
- **The pin is `exactVersion` in `project.yml`.** The project's `Package.resolved` is not in git. To take an SDK release, change that line and rebuild.
- The microphone and speech-recognition descriptions in `project.yml` are for dictation in the console, and are set for Debug only.

each counted line is in docs/theming-for-hosts.md and docs/theming.md.

  ripul-theme check <file or dir>...     those files

app can run it in its build. With a baseline it exits 1 only when a count has risen: an app
part way through a migration runs that, and its count only falls.

Counted, per line, comments stripped:
  font       .font(.body), Font.system(...), UIFont.systemFont(...) and the like
  colour     Color.red, .foregroundStyle(.orange), UIColor.systemBackground, Color(red:...), .cgColor of those
  hierarchy  .primary/.secondary/.tertiary/.quaternary as a style, Color.primary, Color.secondary
  stored     an accessor's result kept in a `static let`: it would never follow a theme change

`fill`, `tint` and the rest), in an argument whose label names a colour (`tint: .blue`,
`colors: [.blue, .purple]`), on a line that says its type is `Color`, and after `return`.
A bare text style (`.caption`) is counted anywhere inside a `.font(...)` argument, on a
line that says its type is `Font`, and after `return`.

it, so a count of zero is not proof that a file is clean. Read the diff too.

reaches those through the window's tint with no edit), view-level `.fontWeight()`,
`.bold()` and `.italic()`, and anything in a branch that compiles only for macOS
(`#if os(macOS)`, `#elseif os(macOS)`, the `#else` of `#if os(iOS)`).

Exempt: a line marked `// theme-exempt: <reason>` (on the line or the line
above), and a file with `// theme-exempt-file: <reason>` in its first 30 lines.

The SDK's own repository runs the same counting over its own layout, by stream
(ripul-native-app/scripts/check_theme_tokens.py imports this file).
"""

    """One file's counts per category, "system", "exempt", and "lines": [(number, text, categories)]."""

        if whole_file or "theme-exempt:" in line or (index and "theme-exempt:" in lines[index - 1]):

            continue
        for category in CATEGORIES:
            entry[category] += counts[category]
        entry["lines"].append((index + 1, line.strip(), [c for c in CATEGORIES if counts[c]]))
    return entry

    """Every Swift file in the given files and directories, build folders left out."""
    for target in targets:
        path = pathlib.Path(target)
        if path.is_file():
            yield path
            continue
        for file in sorted(path.rglob("*.swift")):

            if not any(part in SKIPPED_DIRS or part.startswith("build-") or part.startswith(".") for part in parts):

          "  .font(.caption)                  ->  .font(.ripul(.caption))\\n"
          "  .foregroundStyle(.secondary)     ->  .foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))\\n"
          "  Color.red for an error           ->  Color.ripul(.danger)\\n"
          "`ripul-theme migrate <file or directory>` rewrites the mechanical ones. The full list is in the\\n"
          "SDK's docs/theming-for-hosts.md. A colour that is data, not theme, takes\\n"
          "`// theme-exempt: <reason>` on its line.")


def main(argv) -> int:
    baseline = None
    if "--baseline" in argv:
        i = argv.index("--baseline")
        if i + 1 >= len(argv):
            print("--baseline needs a file")
            return 2
        baseline = pathlib.Path(argv[i + 1])
        argv = argv[:i] + argv[i + 2:]
    update = "--update" in argv
    quiet = "--quiet" in argv
    targets = [a for a in argv if not a.startswith("--")] or ["."]
    now = {c: 0 for c in CATEGORIES + ("system", "exempt")}
    count = 0
    for file in swift_files(targets):
        entry = scan_file(file)
        count += 1
        for category in now:
            now[category] += entry[category]
        if not quiet and not (baseline and not update and baseline.exists()):
            for number, text, categories in entry["lines"]:
                print(f"{file}:{number}: [{','.join(categories)}] {text}")
    total = sum(now[c] for c in CATEGORIES)
    summary = (f"ripul-theme check: {total} direct fonts and colours in {count} files "
               f"({now['font']} font, {now['colour']} colour, {now['hierarchy']} hierarchy, {now['stored']} stored); "
               f"{now['system']} in the system form, {now['exempt']} exempt")
    if baseline is None:
        print(summary)
        if total:
            print(ADVICE)
        return 1 if total else 0
    kept = json.loads(baseline.read_text()) if baseline.exists() else None
    if update or kept is None:
        new = {c: min(now[c], int(kept.get(c, now[c]))) if kept else now[c] for c in CATEGORIES}
        new["stored"] = 0
        baseline.write_text(json.dumps(new, indent=2) + "\\n")
        print(summary)
        print(f"ripul-theme check: baseline {'lowered' if kept else 'written'}: {baseline}")
        return 0
    risen = [(c, int(kept.get(c, 0)), now[c]) for c in CATEGORIES if now[c] > int(kept.get(c, 0))]
    print(summary)
    for category, was, is_now in risen:
        # Xcode shows a line that starts "error:" in the build log.
        print(f"error: ripul-theme check: {is_now} direct {category} uses, above the baseline of {was}.")
    if risen:
        print(ADVICE)
        print("To see the lines, run it with no --baseline.")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tests of the theme tools on a small app that is not Ripul's: python3 tools/test_theme_tools.py"""
import json
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
TOOLS = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(TOOLS))
import theme_rewrite  # noqa: E402
import theme_usage_map  # noqa: E402

APP = '''import SwiftUI

extension View {
    func identified(_ name: String) -> some View {
        #if DEBUG
        return uiKitIdentifier(name)
        #else
        return accessibilityIdentifier(name)
        #endif
    }
    func named(as label: String) -> some View { self.identified(label) }
}

struct Stay: View {
    var body: some View {
        VStack {
            Text("Montauk")
                .font(.ripul(.title, family: .display))
                .foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))
                .identified("stay.cottage")
            Text("Dogs welcome")
                .font(.ripul(.footnote))
                .named(as: "stay.dogs")
            Image(systemName: "house").font(.title2)
            Text("Old").font(.headline).foregroundStyle(.secondary).background(Color(.systemBackground))
            Button("Book") {}.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
            Text("Late").foregroundStyle(.red)
        }
    }
}
'''


class Tools(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.folder = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ripul-theme-tools-"))
        (self.folder / "App").mkdir()
        (self.folder / "App" / "Stay.swift").write_text(APP)
        # A build folder holds copies of other people's source: never read.
        (self.folder / "build" / "SourcePackages").mkdir(parents=True)
        (self.folder / "build" / "SourcePackages" / "Other.swift").write_text('Text("x").font(.body).uiKitIdentifier("other")\n')

    def run_tool(self, *arguments):
        return subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(TOOLS / "ripul-theme"), *arguments], cwd=self.folder,
                              capture_output=True, text=True)

    def test_the_map_follows_a_hosts_own_identifier_modifier(self):
        result, stats = theme_usage_map.build(["."], self.folder)
        self.assertEqual(stats["wrappers"], ["identified", "named"])
        self.assertEqual(sorted(result["elements"]), ["stay.cottage", "stay.dogs"])
        roles = {t.get("role") for t in result["elements"]["stay.cottage"][0]["tokens"]}
        self.assertEqual(roles, {"title", "text"})
        self.assertEqual(result["elements"]["stay.cottage"][0]["file"], "App/Stay.swift")
        self.assertEqual([t["role"] for t in result["elements"]["stay.dogs"][0]["tokens"]], ["footnote"])

    def test_migrate_rewrites_what_keeps_its_value(self):
        new, changed = theme_rewrite.rewrite(APP)
        self.assertIn('Image(systemName: "house").font(.ripulIcon(.title2))', new)
        self.assertIn('.font(.ripul(.headline)).foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary)).background(Color.ripul(.canvas))', new)
        self.assertIn('Button("Book") {}.ripulProminentButtonStyle()', new)
        self.assertIn('.foregroundStyle(.red)', new, "a named colour is left without --named")
        self.assertEqual(changed, 3)
        named, _ = theme_rewrite.rewrite(APP, named=True)
        self.assertIn('.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.danger))', named)
        # Every replacement is one the lint reads as keeping its value.
        for old, replaced in zip(APP.split("\\n"), named.split("\\n")):
            if old != replaced:
                self.assertTrue(theme_rewrite.same_value(theme_rewrite.skeleton(old), theme_rewrite.skeleton(replaced)), replaced)

    def test_check_counts_then_reads_zero_and_a_baseline_only_falls(self):
        first = self.run_tool("check")
        self.assertEqual(first.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn("5 direct fonts and colours in 1 files", first.stdout)
        self.assertNotIn("Other.swift", first.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_tool("check", "--baseline", "theme-baseline.json").returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_tool("check", "--baseline", "theme-baseline.json").returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_tool("migrate", "--named", ".").returncode, 0)
        after = self.run_tool("check")
        self.assertEqual(after.returncode, 0, after.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_tool("check", "--baseline", "theme-baseline.json", "--update").returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads((self.folder / "theme-baseline.json").read_text())["font"], 0)
        (self.folder / "App" / "New.swift").write_text('import SwiftUI\\nlet t = Text("x").font(.body)\\n')
        risen = self.run_tool("check", "--baseline", "theme-baseline.json")
        self.assertEqual(risen.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn("above the baseline of 0", risen.stdout)

    def test_the_build_phase_writes_only_in_debug(self):
        import os
        out = self.folder / "Products" / "App.app"
        env = dict(os.environ, SRCROOT=str(self.folder), TARGET_BUILD_DIR=str(self.folder / "Products"),
                   UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH="App.app", CONFIGURATION="Release")
        command = [sys.executable, str(TOOLS / "ripul-theme"), "usage-map", "--no-sdk"]
        subprocess.run(command, env=env, check=True, capture_output=True)
        self.assertFalse((out / "ripul-theme-usage.json").exists())
        subprocess.run(command, env=dict(env, CONFIGURATION="Debug"), check=True, capture_output=True)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(json.loads((out / "ripul-theme-usage.json").read_text())["elements"]), ["stay.cottage", "stay.dogs"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
E

# A theme for your app

This page is for an app that links the RipulAgent package and wants its own
fonts and colours to come from a theme: one JSON document, light and dark,
switchable while the app runs. It starts from "add the package" and is in the
order to do the work. The full contract, with every measurement behind a rule
here, is [theming.md](theming.md); you should not need it to get through this
page.

What you write, in total: one line at the root, a theme document, your font
files, one line of build setup for the View Explorer, and whatever the
migration command leaves for a person to decide. Everything else is the SDK's.

Where a thing is not built, this page says so. The list is at the end.

## The idea

Every token has a default that is the system value you write today.
`Font.ripul(.body)` is `Font.body`. `.ripul(.textSecondary)` is the system's
`.secondary` style. So moving a call site to a token changes no pixel, and an
app with no theme document looks exactly as it did. A document changes a token
only by naming it.

## 1. Add the package and name your theme

Pin the package (`https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk`), then put one
modifier on the root view of each window group:

```swift
import RipulAgent

WindowGroup {
    ContentView()
        .ripulThemeRoot(theme: "brand")     // brand.json in the app's bundle
}
```

That line is the whole setup. From it the SDK:

- finds `brand.json` in the bundle (at its top level, or in a folder named
  `Themes` or `Theme`), reads it and puts it in use before the first view is
  drawn;
- registers the font files the document names (step 3);
- keeps a choice made with `RipulTheme.select` between launches (step 6);
- falls back to `brand`, and then to the system look, when a document is
  missing, is not a theme document, or was written for a newer SDK. It logs
  which, with the prefix `[RipulTheme]`.

Two other ways to say the same thing, for an app that cannot put it on a root:

- the Info.plist key `RipulTheme` with the document's name, and a plain
  `.ripulThemeRoot()`;
- `RipulTheme.install(theme: "brand")` in the `App`'s `init` or the app
  delegate, for a UIKit app.

With no name at all, `.ripulThemeRoot()` leaves the app on the system look.

The root carries the accent (as the window's tint, so `.tint`,
`Color.accentColor` and control tints follow with no edit) and the theme's
body font for text with no font of its own. A sheet presented with
`.ripulSheet` has a root already. A presented `UIHostingController` of your
own needs `.ripulThemeRoot()` on its root view.

## 2. Write the document

Every key is optional, and an absent key is today's look. Start with
`{ "schema": 1, "name": "Brand" }`, which changes nothing, and add to it.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "name": "Brand",
  "palette": {
    "navy":  { "light": "#24386b", "dark": "#a9bdeb" },
    "paper": { "light": "#f7f3ec", "dark": "#0d1428" },
    "ink":   "#1c2540"
  },
  "roles": {
    "ripul.accent": "navy",
    "ripul.canvas": "paper",
    "ripul.text": "ink"
  },
  "typography": {
    "families": { "text": "Source Sans 3", "display": "Playfair Display", "code": "system-monospaced" },
    "roles": {
      "display": { "size": 34, "weight": "bold" },
      "eyebrow": { "tracking": 1.8, "uppercase": true }
    }
  }
}
```

- **`palette`** names your colours. A value is `#RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBBAA`,
  `system:<name>` (a live system colour such as `system:label`), or a light
  and dark pair of those. Light and dark are written here and nowhere else.
- **`roles`** gives each colour role a palette name, another role, or a colour
  string. The fifteen roles, each with the system colour it is by default:

  | Role | Default | For |
  |---|---|---|
  | `accent` | the app's tint | selection, links, primary buttons |
  | `onAccent` | white | text and icons on an accent fill |
  | `canvas` | `systemBackground` | the app's background |
  | `surface` | `secondarySystemGroupedBackground` | cards and grouped rows |
  | `surfaceSunken` | `systemGroupedBackground` | the ground behind cards |
  | `text`, `textSecondary`, `textTertiary`, `textQuaternary` | `.primary` to `.quaternary` | text |
  | `separator` | `separator` | hairlines |
  | `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `neutral` | green, orange, red, blue, grey | state |

  The set is closed: a document cannot add a role (see the end).
- **`typography.families`** names the three families, `text`, `display` and
  `code`. Each is a font family you bundle, or one of `system`,
  `system-serif`, `system-rounded`, `system-monospaced`.
- **`typography.roles`** changes a type role: `size`, `weight`, `family`,
  `relativeTo`, `tracking`, `uppercase`, `catalystSize`. The roles are the
  eleven system text styles by their own names, plus `display` (a title in
  the display family), `eyebrow` and `code`.

**A serif that is yours already.** `"display": "system-serif"` draws what
`.font(.system(.title, design: .serif))` draws (compared pixel for pixel in a
host's trial on iOS 27, at the default text size). There is no accessor for
`design: .serif` itself. So an app whose headings are serif today keeps them
by naming `system-serif` as its display family and writing
`.font(.ripul(.title, family: .display))` at those headings. Its document is
then not empty, and the plain system look (`RipulTheme.systemThemeName`) is
not the look it had.

Check a dark value against its background yourself: nothing checks contrast.

## 3. Fonts

Put the font files in the app's bundle, at its top level or in a folder named
`Fonts`. Do nothing else. When a document names a family that is not the
system's, the SDK reads the bundled `.ttf`, `.otf` and `.ttc` files and
registers those that hold a face of that family. No `UIAppFonts` entry and no
registration call.

- The name in the document is the font's family name ("Source Sans 3"), not
  its file name.
- A variable font takes weights; a family with one weight draws that weight
  whatever is asked, and the system does not fake a bold.

## 4. Move the call sites: one command

The package brings its tools. In an Xcode project they are in the package
checkout, under the build's DerivedData:

```bash
# with -derivedDataPath build
RIPUL_THEME=build/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme
# with Xcode's default DerivedData
RIPUL_THEME=$(ls -d ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/<Project>-*/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme | head -1)
# in a Swift package
RIPUL_THEME=.build/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme
```

They need `python3` and nothing else.

```bash
$RIPUL_THEME migrate --dry-run --named <your source folder>   # what would change
$RIPUL_THEME migrate --named <your source folder>             # change it
```

Every rewrite is to the token whose default is the value it replaces, so
nothing moves on screen. It rewrites:

| You wrote | It writes |
|---|---|
| `.font(.body)`, `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold))` | `.font(.ripul(.body))`, `.font(.ripul(.caption, weight: .semibold))` |
| `.font(.title2)` or `.font(.system(size: 18))` on an `Image` | `.font(.ripulIcon(.title2))`, `.font(.ripulIcon(size: 18))`: a symbol's size, never themed |
| `.font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))` on a `Text` | `.font(.ripul(size: 14, weight: .medium))` |
| `.caption.monospaced()`, `design: .monospaced` | `family: .code` |
| `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` and the other hierarchy styles | `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))` |
| `Color.primary`, `Color.secondary` | `Color.ripul(.text)`, `Color.ripul(.textSecondary)` |
| `Color(.systemBackground)`, `UIColor.systemBackground`, `UIColor.label` | `Color.ripul(.canvas)`, `UIColor.ripul(.canvas)`, `UIColor.ripul(.text)` |
| any other system colour, `Color(.systemGray5)` | the system form, `Color.ripul(system: .systemGray5)`: drawn as before, never themed |
| `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)` | `.ripulProminentButtonStyle()`: its label is drawn in `onAccent` under a theme |
| with `--named`: `Color.red`, `.foregroundStyle(.orange)` | `Color.ripul(.danger)`, `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.warning))` |
| with `--named`: `.white`, `.black`, `.yellow` and the other hues | the system form, `.ripul(system: .white)` |

Then see what is left, and check the change:

```bash
$RIPUL_THEME check <your source folder>     # every font and colour still written directly; exit 1 while any is left
$RIPUL_THEME lint                           # the working tree's diff: did each replacement keep its value?
```

These need a person, because each is a decision or something the SDK does not
yet do for you.

1. **Text with no colour of its own.** A `Text` that never had a colour is
   drawn in the system's label colour, not the theme's `text`. Give it
   `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))`. It must go on the text itself. On the
   root, or on a container, it changes what `.secondary` draws and recolours
   the labels of bordered and prominent buttons, links in a list and section
   headers, even under the default document (measured). Until the SDK finds
   a way, this is one line a text, and a new `Text` without it stays the
   system's colour silently.
2. **Lists.** A grouped list's ground, rows and separators stay the system's
   under a theme. Set them where you want them themed:
   `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` and `.background(.ripul(.surfaceSunken))`
   on the list, `.listRowBackground(Color.ripul(.surface))` on a section or a
   row (on the list itself it does nothing), `.listRowSeparatorTint(Color.ripul(.separator))`.

   been measured as identical by the SDK.

   `Section(themed: "Title")`, a custom header `RipulSectionHeader { … }`, and
   `ContentUnavailableView("T", systemImage: "i")` becomes
   `ContentUnavailableView(themed: "T", systemImage: "i")`. Without these a
   header loses its weight under a themed family. Not inside a menu, a picker
   or a toolbar. A header takes the family and keeps the system's colour.

   form for white. Where the white sits on an accent fill, write
   `.ripul(.onAccent)`. Where a blue was the app's own colour and not a
   notice, write `.ripul(accentOr: .info)`: the accent once a theme names one.

   place for it in the document yet. Keep it in your code, and if it should
   give way to the theme, read `RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent)` where it is
   used: `RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent) ? myNavy : Color.ripul(.accent)`.
6. **Fonts the command could not place:** a fixed size on a view that is
   neither a `Text` nor an `Image`, a font held in a property
   (`var titleFont: Font { .caption }` becomes `.ripul(.caption)`), `.rounded`
   and `.serif` designs. `check` lists them.
7. **Colours that are data** (a category's colour, a chart's, a brand mark):
   mark the line `// theme-exempt: <reason>` and leave it.

a change. Read the accessor where the value is used.

Script phase:

```bash
"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" check "$SRCROOT/<your source folder>"
```

An app part way through adds `--baseline "$SRCROOT/theme-baseline.json"`: the
first run writes today's counts there, later runs fail only when a count
rises, and `--baseline <file> --update` lowers it. A zero from `check` is not
proof: it reads lines, not types, and cannot see a bare `.orange` passed to an
unlabelled parameter.

Both come from the document: every palette entry that should differ is a
pair. A role left at its default follows the system in both. Look at every
screen in both; the pair for `onAccent` is the one most often wrong (white on
a pale dark-mode accent cannot be read).

## 6. Switching while the app runs

```swift
RipulTheme.select("brand-large")              // another document in the bundle; kept for later launches
RipulTheme.select(RipulTheme.systemThemeName) // the system look, kept as a choice
RipulTheme.select(nil)                        // forget the choice: back to the theme the root names
RipulTheme.selectedTheme                      // what is in use; read in a body, it follows a change
RipulTheme.bundledThemes                      // every theme document in the bundle, with its own name

RipulThemePicker("Look")                      // a picker over all of the above, in one line
```

Everything on screen repaints, with nothing written in your views.
`select` returns false and changes nothing when the document is missing or
refused.

- **A launch argument:** `-ripul.theme.document <name>` (the choice is a
  `UserDefaults` key of that name).
- **A link, in a Debug build only:** `<your app's scheme>://theme?name=<name>`,
  with `name=system` for the system look. The root handles it. A store build
  ignores it; pass a URL to `RipulTheme.handleThemeLink(_:)` yourself if you
  want it there.

A build that must show one theme whatever was chosen before installs with
`RipulTheme.install(theme: "brand", keepsChoice: false)`.

What does not repaint by itself: UIKit code that read a colour or a font once
(read it again on `Notification.Name.ripulThemeDidChange`), and anything
computed outside a view's body and kept.

## 7. The View Explorer names your tokens

In a Debug build, selecting an element in the Ripul View Explorer lists the
theme tokens that style it, each with its value and whether it comes from the
document. The explorer reads that from a map written at build time. Add one
Run Script build phase holding one line:

```bash
"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" usage-map
```

In an XcodeGen `project.yml`:

```yaml
    postCompileScripts:
      - name: Theme usage map
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: '"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" usage-map'
```

It reads Xcode's own settings. It does nothing outside a Debug build, reads
the Swift files under the project's folder and the SDK's own screens, and
writes `ripul-theme-usage.json` into the app. It never fails a build. The
target needs `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = NO`, as any script that reads
the source does.

An element is known by its identifier: `.uiKitIdentifier("screen.element")` or
`.accessibilityIdentifier(…)`. **Your own identifier modifier is followed.** If
the app names controls through a wrapper,

```swift
func identified(_ name: String) -> some View { uiKitIdentifier(name) }
```

then `.identified("stay.cottage")` is read like the two it wraps. Nothing
declares it; the build log says which wrappers it followed.

To ask it directly: `$RIPUL_THEME usage-map --roots <folder> --no-sdk --stats`,
and `--explain <identifier>` for one element.

## 8. Check that nothing moved

Before the first edit, take screenshots of your screens in light and dark.
After the migration, with no document or an empty one, take them again and
compare them pixel for pixel. They should be the same. Where they are not, a
replacement was a judgement and not an identity: `lint` names most of those,
and the lists and text colours of step 4 are the usual rest.

## What the system draws that a theme does not reach

- **Reached, with no edit:** the accent on toolbar buttons, toggles, buttons,
  menus, progress bars, sliders, the selected tab and alert buttons; the text
  family on form rows, buttons, navigation titles (large and inline),
  segmented controls and tab bar labels.
- **Not reached:** the colour of a large navigation title and of a section
  header (the family is); alerts' text, menus, swipe action labels, a menu
  picker's value; a navigation title on Mac Catalyst.
- **Under a themed accent, things that had no colour take it:** toolbar
  buttons, a swipe action with no tint, a toggle's on colour.
- A document cannot ask for a font feature (lining figures, for one).

  needs a root inside it. See "Measured again, with Mac Catalyst" in

## Not built

Each of these is a decision the SDK has not taken yet. Until it is, the cost
is yours, as described above.

- **A theme layer on its own.** The theme is part of `RipulAgent`: an app that
  wants only the theme links the whole package, in Release too.
- **Your own roles in the document.** The fifteen are all there are.
- **Text colour without a line a text.**
- **Lists themed from the root.**
- **Editing a theme in the app.** A look is tried by loading a document.

  the package and install the theme themselves.

## The API in one place

```swift

RipulTheme.install(theme:bundle:keepsChoice:)
RipulTheme.select(_:)   RipulTheme.selectedTheme   RipulTheme.bundledThemes
RipulTheme.handleThemeLink(_:)           RipulThemePicker(_:systemTitle:)
RipulTheme.adopt(documentData:)          // a document from anywhere else, such as your server
RipulTheme.resetToDefaults()
RipulTheme.color(.accent)   RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent)

Font.ripul(.body)   Font.ripul(.title, weight: .bold, family: .display)   Font.ripul(size: 14)
Font.ripulIcon(.title2)   Font.ripulIcon(size: 18)
.ripul(.textSecondary)            // as a style: foregroundStyle, fill, background, tint
Color.ripul(.danger)              // where a Color is required
.ripul(system: .systemGray5)      // a system colour, never themed
.ripul(accentOr: .info)
UIColor.ripul(.canvas)   UIFont.ripul(.caption)
.ripulTextStyle(.eyebrow)   .ripulProminentButtonStyle()   Section(themed:)   ContentUnavailableView(themed:)
```

This page is for an app that links the RipulAgent package and wants its own
fonts and colours to come from a theme: one JSON document, light and dark,
switchable while the app runs. It starts from "add the package" and is in the
order to do the work. The full contract, with every measurement behind a rule
here, is [theming.md](theming.md); you should not need it to get through this
page.

What you write, in total: one line at the root, a theme document, your font
files, one line of build setup for the View Explorer, and whatever the
migration command leaves for a person to decide. Everything else is the SDK's.

Where a thing is not built, this page says so. The list is at the end.

## The idea

Every token has a default that is the system value you write today.
`Font.ripul(.body)` is `Font.body`. `.ripul(.textSecondary)` is the system's
`.secondary` style. So moving a call site to a token changes no pixel, and an
app with no theme document looks exactly as it did. A document changes a token
only by naming it.

## 1. Add the package and name your theme

Pin the package (`https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk`), then put one
modifier on the root view of each window group:

```swift
import RipulAgent

WindowGroup {
    ContentView()
        .ripulThemeRoot(theme: "brand")     // brand.json in the app's bundle
}
```

That line is the whole setup. From it the SDK:

- finds `brand.json` in the bundle (at its top level, or in a folder named
  `Themes` or `Theme`), reads it and puts it in use before the first view is
  drawn;
- registers the font files the document names (step 3);
- keeps a choice made with `RipulTheme.select` between launches (step 6);
- falls back to `brand`, and then to the system look, when a document is
  missing, is not a theme document, or was written for a newer SDK. It logs
  which, with the prefix `[RipulTheme]`.

Two other ways to say the same thing, for an app that cannot put it on a root:

- the Info.plist key `RipulTheme` with the document's name, and a plain
  `.ripulThemeRoot()`;
- `RipulTheme.install(theme: "brand")` in the `App`'s `init` or the app
  delegate, for a UIKit app.

With no name at all, `.ripulThemeRoot()` leaves the app on the system look.

The root carries the accent (as the window's tint, so `.tint`,
`Color.accentColor` and control tints follow with no edit) and the theme's
body font for text with no font of its own. A sheet presented with
`.ripulSheet` has a root already. A presented `UIHostingController` of your
own needs `.ripulThemeRoot()` on its root view.

## 2. Write the document

Every key is optional, and an absent key is today's look. Start with
`{ "schema": 1, "name": "Brand" }`, which changes nothing, and add to it.

```json

  "name": "Brand",
  "palette": {
    "navy":  { "light": "#24386b", "dark": "#a9bdeb" },
    "paper": { "light": "#f7f3ec", "dark": "#0d1428" },
    "ink":   "#1c2540"
  },
  "roles": {
    "ripul.accent": "navy",
    "ripul.canvas": "paper",
    "ripul.text": "ink"
  },
  "typography": {
    "families": { "text": "Source Sans 3", "display": "Playfair Display", "code": "system-monospaced" },
    "roles": {
      "display": { "size": 34, "weight": "bold" },
      "eyebrow": { "tracking": 1.8, "uppercase": true }
    }
  }
}
```

  `system:<name>` (a live system colour such as `system:label`), or a light
  and dark pair of those. Light and dark are written here and nowhere else.
- **`roles`** gives each colour role a palette name, another role, or a colour
  string. The fifteen roles, each with the system colour it is by default:

  | Role | Default | For |
  |---|---|---|
  | `accent` | the app's tint | selection, links, primary buttons |
  | `onAccent` | white | text and icons on an accent fill |
  | `canvas` | `systemBackground` | the app's background |
  | `surface` | `secondarySystemGroupedBackground` | cards and grouped rows |
  | `surfaceSunken` | `systemGroupedBackground` | the ground behind cards |
  | `text`, `textSecondary`, `textTertiary`, `textQuaternary` | `.primary` to `.quaternary` | text |
  | `separator` | `separator` | hairlines |
  | `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `neutral` | green, orange, red, blue, grey | state |

  `code`. Each is a font family you bundle, or one of `system`,
  `system-serif`, `system-rounded`, `system-monospaced`.

  `relativeTo`, `tracking`, `uppercase`, `catalystSize`. The roles are the
  eleven system text styles by their own names, plus `display` (a title in
  the display family), `eyebrow` and `code`.

`.font(.system(.title, design: .serif))` draws (compared pixel for pixel in a
host's trial on iOS 27, at the default text size). There is no accessor for
`design: .serif` itself. So an app whose headings are serif today keeps them
by naming `system-serif` as its display family and writing
`.font(.ripul(.title, family: .display))` at those headings. Its document is

# A theme for your app

This page is for an app that links the RipulAgent package and wants its own
fonts and colours to come from a theme: one JSON document, light and dark,
switchable while the app runs. It starts from "add the package" and is in the
order to do the work. The full contract, with every measurement behind a rule
here, is [theming.md](theming.md); you should not need it to get through this
page.

What you write, in total: one line at the root, a theme document, your font
files, one line of build setup for the View Explorer, and whatever the
migration command leaves for a person to decide. Everything else is the SDK's.

Where a thing is not built, this page says so. The list is at the end.

## The idea

Every token has a default that is the system value you write today.
`Font.ripul(.body)` is `Font.body`. `.ripul(.textSecondary)` is the system's
`.secondary` style. So moving a call site to a token changes no pixel, and an
app with no theme document looks exactly as it did. A document changes a token
only by naming it.

## 1. Add the package and name your theme

Pin the package (`https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk`), then put one
modifier on the root view of each window group:

```swift
import RipulAgent

WindowGroup {
    ContentView()
        .ripulThemeRoot(theme: "brand")     // brand.json in the app's bundle
}
```

That line is the whole setup. From it the SDK:

- finds `brand.json` in the bundle (at its top level, or in a folder named
  `Themes` or `Theme`), reads it and puts it in use before the first view is
  drawn;
- registers the font files the document names (step 3);
- keeps a choice made with `RipulTheme.select` between launches (step 6);
- falls back to `brand`, and then to the system look, when a document is
  missing, is not a theme document, or was written for a newer SDK. It logs
  which, with the prefix `[RipulTheme]`.

Two other ways to say the same thing, for an app that cannot put it on a root:

- the Info.plist key `RipulTheme` with the document's name, and a plain
  `.ripulThemeRoot()`;
- `RipulTheme.install(theme: "brand")` in the `App`'s `init` or the app
  delegate, for a UIKit app.

With no name at all, `.ripulThemeRoot()` leaves the app on the system look.

The root carries the accent (as the window's tint, so `.tint`,
`Color.accentColor` and control tints follow with no edit) and the theme's
body font for text with no font of its own. A sheet presented with
`.ripulSheet` has a root already. A presented `UIHostingController` of your
own needs `.ripulThemeRoot()` on its root view.

## 2. Write the document

Every key is optional, and an absent key is today's look. Start with
`{ "schema": 1, "name": "Brand" }`, which changes nothing, and add to it.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "name": "Brand",
  "palette": {
    "navy":  { "light": "#24386b", "dark": "#a9bdeb" },
    "paper": { "light": "#f7f3ec", "dark": "#0d1428" },
    "ink":   "#1c2540"
  },
  "roles": {
    "ripul.accent": "navy",
    "ripul.canvas": "paper",
    "ripul.text": "ink"
  },
  "typography": {
    "families": { "text": "Source Sans 3", "display": "Playfair Display", "code": "system-monospaced" },
    "roles": {
      "display": { "size": 34, "weight": "bold" },
      "eyebrow": { "tracking": 1.8, "uppercase": true }
    }
  }
}
```

- **`palette`** names your colours. A value is `#RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBBAA`,
  `system:<name>` (a live system colour such as `system:label`), or a light
  and dark pair of those. Light and dark are written here and nowhere else.
- **`roles`** gives each colour role a palette name, another role, or a colour
  string. The fifteen roles, each with the system colour it is by default:

  | Role | Default | For |
  |---|---|---|
  | `accent` | the app's tint | selection, links, primary buttons |
  | `onAccent` | white | text and icons on an accent fill |
  | `canvas` | `systemBackground` | the app's background |
  | `surface` | `secondarySystemGroupedBackground` | cards and grouped rows |
  | `surfaceSunken` | `systemGroupedBackground` | the ground behind cards |
  | `text`, `textSecondary`, `textTertiary`, `textQuaternary` | `.primary` to `.quaternary` | text |
  | `separator` | `separator` | hairlines |
  | `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `neutral` | green, orange, red, blue, grey | state |

  The set is closed: a document cannot add a role (see the end).
- **`typography.families`** names the three families, `text`, `display` and
  `code`. Each is a font family you bundle, or one of `system`,
  `system-serif`, `system-rounded`, `system-monospaced`.
- **`typography.roles`** changes a type role: `size`, `weight`, `family`,
  `relativeTo`, `tracking`, `uppercase`, `catalystSize`. The roles are the
  eleven system text styles by their own names, plus `display` (a title in
  the display family), `eyebrow` and `code`.

**A serif that is yours already.** `"display": "system-serif"` draws what
`.font(.system(.title, design: .serif))` draws (compared pixel for pixel in a
host's trial on iOS 27, at the default text size). There is no accessor for
`design: .serif` itself. So an app whose headings are serif today keeps them
by naming `system-serif` as its display family and writing
`.font(.ripul(.title, family: .display))` at those headings. Its document is
then not empty, and the plain system look (`RipulTheme.systemThemeName`) is
not the look it had.

Check a dark value against its background yourself: nothing checks contrast.

## 3. Fonts

Put the font files in the app's bundle, at its top level or in a folder named
`Fonts`. Do nothing else. When a document names a family that is not the
system's, the SDK reads the bundled `.ttf`, `.otf` and `.ttc` files and
registers those that hold a face of that family. No `UIAppFonts` entry and no
registration call.

- The name in the document is the font's family name ("Source Sans 3"), not
  its file name.
- A variable font takes weights; a family with one weight draws that weight
  whatever is asked, and the system does not fake a bold.
- Ship each font's licence beside it. That is yours to get right.

## 4. Move the call sites: one command

The package brings its tools. In an Xcode project they are in the package
checkout, under the build's DerivedData:

```bash
# with -derivedDataPath build
RIPUL_THEME=build/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme
# with Xcode's default DerivedData
RIPUL_THEME=$(ls -d ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/<Project>-*/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme | head -1)
# in a Swift package
RIPUL_THEME=.build/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme
```

They need `python3` and nothing else.

```bash
$RIPUL_THEME migrate --dry-run --named <your source folder>   # what would change
$RIPUL_THEME migrate --named <your source folder>             # change it
```

Every rewrite is to the token whose default is the value it replaces, so
nothing moves on screen. It rewrites:

| You wrote | It writes |
|---|---|
| `.font(.body)`, `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold))` | `.font(.ripul(.body))`, `.font(.ripul(.caption, weight: .semibold))` |
| `.font(.title2)` or `.font(.system(size: 18))` on an `Image` | `.font(.ripulIcon(.title2))`, `.font(.ripulIcon(size: 18))`: a symbol's size, never themed |
| `.font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))` on a `Text` | `.font(.ripul(size: 14, weight: .medium))` |
| `.caption.monospaced()`, `design: .monospaced` | `family: .code` |
| `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` and the other hierarchy styles | `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))` |
| `Color.primary`, `Color.secondary` | `Color.ripul(.text)`, `Color.ripul(.textSecondary)` |
| `Color(.systemBackground)`, `UIColor.systemBackground`, `UIColor.label` | `Color.ripul(.canvas)`, `UIColor.ripul(.canvas)`, `UIColor.ripul(.text)` |
| any other system colour, `Color(.systemGray5)` | the system form, `Color.ripul(system: .systemGray5)`: drawn as before, never themed |

| with `--named`: `Color.red`, `.foregroundStyle(.orange)` | `Color.ripul(.danger)`, `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.warning))` |
| with `--named`: `.white`, `.black`, `.yellow` and the other hues | the system form, `.ripul(system: .white)` |

Then see what is left, and check the change:

```bash
$RIPUL_THEME check <your source folder>     # every font and colour still written directly; exit 1 while any is left
$RIPUL_THEME lint                           # the working tree's diff: did each replacement keep its value?
```

### What it leaves for you

These need a person, because each is a decision or something the SDK does not
yet do for you.

1. **Text with no colour of its own.** A `Text` that never had a colour is
   drawn in the system's label colour, not the theme's `text`. Give it

   root, or on a container, it changes what `.secondary` draws and recolours
   the labels of bordered and prominent buttons, links in a list and section
   headers, even under the default document (measured). Until the SDK finds
   a way, this is one line a text, and a new `Text` without it stays the
   system's colour silently.
2. **Lists.** A grouped list's ground, rows and separators stay the system's
   under a theme. Set them where you want them themed:
   `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` and `.background(.ripul(.surfaceSunken))`
   on the list, `.listRowBackground(Color.ripul(.surface))` on a section or a
   row (on the list itself it does nothing), `.listRowSeparatorTint(Color.ripul(.separator))`.
   Compare a screenshot under the default document afterwards: these have not
   been measured as identical by the SDK.

Pass the same registry instance to `AgentView` and to the console's `RipulSessionsConfiguration`. Keep the console behind the app's own developer-only switch.

## Making screens identifiable

Agents address elements by accessibility identifier, visible text, role and class. Identifiers are the only stable one.

- UIKit: set `accessibilityIdentifier` on each control.
- SwiftUI: use `.uiKitIdentifier("screen.element")`, which sets the accessibility identifier and also marks the element's exact frame.
- Give each control its own identifier. An identifier on a container is inherited by what is inside it, and a tap by that identifier becomes ambiguous.
- To say what a component means, add `.ripulAIContext(.init(id:label:value:role:))`, or set `view.ripulAIContext` in UIKit and update it when the value changes.

## What is kept private

When a person attaches Current screen or Selected element to a message, nothing is captured until they choose it and review a preview. To leave a region out, use `.ripulAIContextExcluded()` in SwiftUI, `view.ripulAIContext = .excluded` in UIKit, or the attribute `data-ripul-context-excluded` on a web element. Excluded regions are removed from the description and painted out of the screenshot.

Fields are not excluded automatically, secure fields included: mark every field that holds something private.

'''

## The SDK's response

Written by the agent that changed the SDK, 11 October 2026, after the first trial and before the second. Released as SDK 0.7.171 (commits `a3df64632` and `62420e493`). Everything marked measured was run; everything else is said to be reasoned.

### What this tranche took off the host

Each line is what the host does now, against what Sandsend did in the morning. The morning's figures are the ledger's above. "Now" was measured by taking the morning's branch in a throwaway copy under `/tmp`, pointing it at the changed SDK and deleting what the SDK now does: **8 lines added, 283 removed** (`git diff --shortstat`), and it built and ran in the simulator in all four states (each theme at launch, and each switch while running).

| | The morning, on 0.7.170 | Now, on 0.7.171 |
|---|---|---|
| **A theme by name** (items 2 and 4) | 76 lines: a 64-line loader, 2 in the app, 10 for a picker | 1 line, `.ripulThemeRoot(theme: "<name>")` (or the Info.plist key `RipulTheme`), and 1 line for a picker, `RipulThemePicker("Look")`. The SDK finds the document, adopts it, keeps the choice, falls back, and switches with `RipulTheme.select`. The launch argument `-ripul.theme.document` and the link `<scheme>://theme?name=` work in any host; the link in Debug builds only. |
| **Fonts** (item 3) | registration code, about 5 of the 64 lines | 0 lines. Files in the bundle; the SDK registers those whose family a document names. The files and their licences are still the host's. |
| **The tools** (items 5 and 6) | a 30-line rewrite written and thrown away, a 202-line map generator written from the SDK's source, 11 lines of build setup, no check and no lint | 0 lines of script. `tools/ripul-theme` in the package: `migrate`, `check`, `lint`, `usage-map`. The map is one Run Script line and follows a host's own identifier modifier, found and not declared (measured: `.identified(` in Sandsend, and `.cmsInspectorID(` in Ripul's own source, which the old script had missed: 23 more identifiers). `migrate` now also does wrapped system colours and prominent buttons, and with `--named` the named colours. |
| **The two tab bar faults** (8 and 9 under "What did not work") | no cure in the host | Fixed in the SDK and measured by screenshot on iOS 27.0. The first was wider than reported: after a themed accent the whole window went system blue, not only the tab. The root now puts back the colour the app's asset catalogue names. Tab labels take the family at launch. Under the default document the screen is the same pixel for pixel as before the fix, the clock apart. |
| **A page for hosts** (item 11) | 985 lines of `theming.md` written for this repository, and 1,776 lines of source | `docs/theming-for-hosts.md`, 385 lines, from "add the package", with none of this repository's paths. It says that `system-serif` draws what `design: .serif` draws, what the migration leaves for a person, and what is not built. The `sdk` guide of `ripul_guide` points to it. |

Ripul's own app is the proof for the first two: `ripul-native-app/iOS/RipulAppTheme.swift` (64 lines) is deleted, and the app names its document in one call. Its build step for the usage map went from five lines to the one line any host writes.

### What was checked

- SDK builds for the iOS simulator (the `--triple` form) and for macOS. 51 theme tests pass, 12 of them new (the loader, the kept choice, the fallbacks, the link, font registration). 4 tests of the tools on a small app that is not Ripul's.
- `check_theme_tokens.py` reads zero, the lint passes on the diff, the private-function check is clean, Ripul's app compiles.
- Ripul's usage map: the same as the old script's but for the 23 identifiers the wrapper search added (compared as JSON).
- Reference screens under the default document, 56 captures against `~/.ripul/theme-reference/baseline`: none differs in a way this change could cause. Twelve differ: a spinner, a busy row and the start chooser (animated, and marked so by the tool); the session list's right-hand column and the lozenge list, which differ in the same places between yesterday's own captures; and one explorer screen whose inspector panel sat in a different place on a fresh install. I looked at each.
- WAC compiles against the local SDK (a throwaway worktree under `/tmp`, removed).

Not checked: Mac Catalyst, iOS 17, a store build, and the font registration on a phone before the second trial runs it.

### What a host still pays, and four proposals

These were left out because each is a design decision. For each: the proposal I would make, its cost in my own working time (an agent's, reasoned from the size of the code, not measured), and its risk.

**1. A theme layer a host can link without the rest (item 10).**
Proposal: a `RipulTheme` library product in `Package.swift`, with no dependencies, holding `ThemeCore/`; `RipulAgent` re-exports it, so nothing a host or WAC writes today changes.
Cost: about half a day. Eight files move; the usage-map reader and the root have a few reaches into the rest of the SDK to cut (the legacy refresh environment key, the token provider stays behind).
Risk: Xcode links a package product into every configuration, so Sandsend gets the saving only if nothing in its Release build imports `RipulAgent`; today its console is already Debug-only, so it would. The Release app would lose about 60 MB (reasoned from the first trial's measurement, not built). A module rename can break a host that spells a type `RipulAgent.RipulTheme`; none of ours does.

**2. A host's own colours in the document (item 9).**
Proposal: a host declares its roles once in code, each with the colour it is today (`static let navy = RipulHostRole("navy", default: …)`), reads them with the same accessors (`.ripul(.navy)`), and names them in the same document under `roles`. The default is today's value, so the rule that nothing changes holds. The check, the lint and the usage map learn the declared names.
Cost: about a day, most of it the three tools and the tests.
Risk: two role types behind one accessor name can make `.ripul(.x)` ambiguous to the compiler where a host picks a name the SDK also uses; the alternative, turning the fixed enum into an open type, is cleaner to read and touches every `switch` over roles in the SDK. This is also the first step of moving WAC off the legacy engine, so its shape should be chosen with that in mind.

**3. Text that has no colour of its own (item 7).**
Proposal: do not look for a root-level cure; it was measured not to exist. Make it mechanical instead: `migrate` adds `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))` to every `Text` with no foreground in its chain, and `check` counts a bare `Text` so a new one fails the build.
Cost: about half a day, plus a measurement pass in each container (a button, a link, a list row, a toolbar) to prove the added line is an identity there.
Risk: the tool reads text, not types, so a `Text` built in a helper is missed, and inside a control an explicit text role is drawn as the control's tint, which is right today and may surprise under a theme. It is still a line a text; it stops being a line a person writes.

**4. Lists (item 8).**
Proposal: first spend two hours measuring whether a root can do it at all: `scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` set at the root reaches the lists below it, but a row's background set from outside a list does not (the first trial found that). If the root can carry the ground and UIKit's appearance can carry the rows, lists are themed with no edit. If not, one modifier, `.ripulThemedList()`, that `migrate` adds to each `List` and `Form`, with the rows' background applied by the SDK's `Section(themed:)`.
Cost: two hours to know, then half a day either way.
Risk: the system's grouped look has parts no public setting reaches on iOS 26 and later (the inset card's shape and its selected state); a themed row background may lose the system's highlight. Under the default document it must stay the system's own, which a modifier that does nothing until a theme names `surface` guarantees.

Also still the host's, with no proposal here: a font feature in the document (lining figures), the colour of a large navigation title and of a section header, and a way to keep a serif without a second document.
E
